title: Retention and disk safety: the janitor, the disk budget, store caps, blob GC, quotas and the fill-past-cap test
description:
## Goal
Make "every growing store is capped" and "safe defaults" enforceable: one janitor for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint; a disk budget (amber at 80 %, `storage_full` at 95 %, reads and deletes always work); quotas that stop a looping agent; and a test that fills each store past its cap and shows it back under. This chain sets Slice 1's date (decision 41), so it starts as soon as data snapshots land (§6a) and runs beside the Health/export bead rather than after it.

## Scope
- [ ] Janitor framework (`pf-janitor`): `JanitorJob` trait + registry, scheduler (hourly/daily jittered/weekly/monthly, one job at a time, ≤ 1,000 rows per transaction), reference-safety guard run inside the writer (never deletes anything a live or binned part references), `janitor_runs` rows in `/data/insights.db` (created on first start with its own writer), metrics, admin "run now".
- [ ] Main-DB jobs: events 30 d, build logs (last 20 builds per part, 30 d; clears `log_hash`), runtime errors 30 d (the 1,000-per-part trigger exists), audit yearly segments (1 year), idempotency 24 h, scratch expiry → bin (+ part epoch bump), bin purge at 30 d keeping the name as a tombstone.
- [ ] Data-snapshot retention (daily keep 7, hourly keep 48, on-demand not counted, keep the last one after 90 idle days until the part leaves the bin), WAL checkpoint on both DBs + monthly `VACUUM` when free pages > 20 %. Scheduled-export rotation is registered by the Health/export bead when exports exist.
- [ ] Blob GC: one mark function from every reference (version files and manifests, build files + br, build output and log, `build_deps.blob_hash`, `part_previews` poster and video hashes, drafts, data snapshots, assets, `shared_blobs`, `mirror_cache`, and later sources as they land: kept image tarballs, unexpired screenshots); sweep sets `unref_since`, deletes after a **7-day grace**; blobs written after the mark began are never swept. Export reuses the same mark function, so the two can't disagree.
- [ ] Disk budget: `[disk] budget_percent` (default 80 % of the volume, bounded); used = `/data` + runner images + BuildKit cache (0 until the runner exists); measured every 30 s plus counters on blob put/delete, never `du` on the hot path. States ok / warn ≥ 80 % / full ≥ 95 % of the budget. In `full` the writer refuses versions, assets, builds, deploys and `/_rt` writes with `storage_full` (507, exit 7); reads, deletes, grants and revocations continue. Replaces the blob store's own volume check so there is one rule.
- [ ] Store-cap registry `{name, size_fn, cap_bytes, retention}` with metrics (`pf_store_bytes{store}`, `pf_store_cap_bytes{store}`) and a `HealthCheck` row per store (amber ≥ 80 %, red ≥ 100 %) plus the budget row, in the observability bead's check registry so the Health page renders them; safe-defaults registry `{name, config keys, unsafe_key}` for what exists (secure headers, rate limits, quotas, ingress TLS, log redaction, retention caps; the nightly export and the container template register when they land): turning one off without `[unsafe] <name> = "off"` fails `config check` (exit 2, naming the key); with it, a Health warning row. Caps only within declared bounds.
- [ ] Quotas enforced in the writer, below the registry, on every surface: per space (default 2,000 parts, 20 GiB, 1,000 versions a day) and per agent connection (500 versions a day, 2 GiB introduced), NULL = default, unlimited only with `[unsafe] quotas = "off"`. `quota_exceeded {kind, limit, retry_after?}` (429, exit 6); one deduplicated quota-hit entry per principal/kind/day (a Health row); `pf_quota_hits_total`.
- [ ] Retention test: one fill-past-cap case per existing §5h store (pruned stores come back under after a janitor cycle; a store whose §5h policy is "stop at the cap", such as Previews, refuses the next write instead), plus a completeness check against the registry so a new growing store without a cap and a case fails. Later beads (exports, Insights, logs, backend rings, images, BuildKit cache) add their cases when they land.

## Plan refs
§5h Disk safety (table, janitor, safe defaults); §5d Maintenance and Abuse prevention (quotas, blob GC, disk pressure); §5c data snapshots; §3e the bin; §5e (`janitor_runs`, GC sources, `quota_*`); §4b errors; §6a ("start the janitor as soon as snapshots land"); §7 Operations; definition of done item 6; decisions 33, 41, 48.

## Considerations
- Quotas key on the connection, not the token (tokens rotate hourly), and are checked inside the single writer (race-free). A rejection stores no idempotency row; `retry_after` only for the daily window. Until the token service lands, tests use fixture `agent_connections` rows; per-connection quotas against a real agent token are proven again by the security suite in the Shipping bead.
- Binned parts count toward quotas until purged. Bin purge never touches blobs; GC does, after its grace (which covers have/need uploads, long builds and a running export).
- Under `storage_full`, data roll back and reset are refused too (they snapshot first); the hint says to delete something.
- Later stores (exports, Insights, traces, logs, backend rings, images, BuildKit cache) register their own jobs, store-cap rows and retention cases when they land.
- `build_deps` rows (round 3) cascade with their build, and their `blob_hash` is a GC reference.
- The Health page itself is the Health/export bead's (it runs after this one and renders these rows); this bead's gate reads the same rows from `/metrics` and the check registry, so it doesn't wait on the page.

## Tests and logging
- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/{janitor_e2e.rs::full_cycle_on_fixture, jobs_main_db.rs, jobs_snapshots.rs, blob_gc.rs, retention_table.rs::fill_past_cap::<store>, retention_table.rs::registry_complete}`; `crates/partifactory/tests/{storage_full.rs, quotas.rs, safe_defaults.rs}`; `tests/e2e/disk_full.spec.ts` on a small loopback volume; the 10k-create quota loop.
- Logs asserted: `event="janitor.job" store=<s> action=<a> items=<n> freed_bytes=<b> outcome="ok|error"`, `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"`, `event="op" op="part_create" outcome="storage_full"`, `event="op" op="part_create" outcome="quota_exceeded"`. Metrics `pf_disk_budget_bytes`, `pf_disk_used_bytes`, `pf_disk_budget_state`, `pf_store_bytes`, `pf_store_cap_bytes`, `pf_quota_hits_total`.

## Verification gate
1. Binary from `main` in the e2e harness: each existing store filled past its cap comes back under after a janitor cycle (`janitor_runs` rows, `pf_store_bytes` ≤ `pf_store_cap_bytes`); at 95 % of a loopback volume's budget `part_create` gets 507 while a delete and a read (`part_get` and a `/c/` fetch) succeed and `pf_disk_budget_state` reports full; a 10k-create loop stops at `quota_exceeded` with one quota-hit entry.
2. CI green on `main` with the tests above (nextest job) and `disk_full.spec.ts` (e2e job).
3. Logs checked: `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"` and `event="janitor.job"` lines asserted.
4. The full e2e suite, every earlier gate included, still passes.
5. Close with SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts and the `/metrics` excerpt; `ci_green` and `verified` recorded via `br gate report`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A test job registered through the trait runs on schedule and writes a `janitor_runs` row and metrics; a panicking or failing job records `error` and the scheduler continues.
- [ ] `/data/insights.db` is created on first start with the schema; `janitor_runs` rows land there; `partifactory.db` has no `janitor_runs` table (schema test).
- [ ] On a fixture each job frees exactly the expected rows and writes its `janitor_runs` row with the bytes freed (also on `/metrics`); a 31-day-old event is pruned, a 29-day one kept; only the newest 20 builds' logs per part remain referenced.
- [ ] The reference guard keeps a candidate referenced only by a binned part.
- [ ] Purged part names stay reserved (tombstone); undelete at 29 d ok, 31 d fails.
- [ ] A scratch part past `expires_in` moves to the bin and its caps die (part epoch bumped).
- [ ] A daily part keeps exactly 7 scheduled snapshots; hourly keeps 48; on-demand ones aren't counted; after 90 days idle exactly one snapshot remains until the part leaves the bin.
- [ ] Checkpoint and VACUUM run on both DBs, VACUUM only above 20 % free pages; `janitor_runs` rows with `checkpoint`/`vacuum`.
- [ ] An unreferenced blob is deleted after the 7-day grace; a blob referenced by any version, build, draft, snapshot, asset or `build_deps.blob_hash` is never collected; a blob written after the mark phase began is never swept in that run; a re-referenced `unref_since` blob is cleared.
- [ ] `build_deps` rows are deleted with their build (cascade).
- [ ] At 95 % of the budget every listed write class (versions, assets, builds, `/_rt` writes; deploys once they exist) is refused with `storage_full` (507, exit 7), while reads, deletes, grants and revocations succeed; at 80 % the budget state is warn.
- [ ] A store at 80 % of its cap reports amber and at 100 % red in its check-registry row and on `/metrics`.
- [ ] Switching rate limits (or any registered safe default) off without its `[unsafe]` key fails `config check` (exit 2, naming the key); with it, a warning row appears; caps outside their bounds are rejected by `config check`; no `[unsafe]` key is set in the default config.
- [ ] Every §5h row whose store exists has a passing fill-past-cap case; adding a growing store without a cap and a case fails the completeness test.
- [ ] A loop of 10k creates stops at the quota with `quota_exceeded {kind, limit}` and exactly one quota-hit entry for that principal/kind/day.
- [ ] Quotas apply identically on MCP, HTTP and the CLI (enforced below the registry), keyed on the agent connection, not the token; NULL means the default and unlimited needs `[unsafe] quotas = "off"`; a quota rejection stores no idempotency row.
- [ ] The "Previews" store (`part_previews` blobs; in Slice 1 only latest-render screenshots, seeded as fixture rows because the part_check bead may land later) is in the store-cap registry at 2 GiB; its case follows §5h ("new previews stop at the cap"): past the cap a new poster is refused and the old one stays; a replaced poster is collected by GC after its grace.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness, the fill-past-cap run fills each existing store past its cap on the running server and shows it back under after a janitor cycle (`janitor_runs` rows and `pf_store_bytes` ≤ `pf_store_cap_bytes` on `/metrics`).
- [ ] GATE: On a loopback volume at 95 % of the budget, `part_create` gets 507 `storage_full`, a delete and a read (`part_get` and a `/c/` fetch) succeed and `pf_disk_budget_state` reports full; a 10k-create loop stops at `quota_exceeded` with one quota-hit entry.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with `crates/pf-janitor/tests/*`, `crates/partifactory/tests/{storage_full,quotas,safe_defaults}.rs` (nextest job) and `tests/e2e/disk_full.spec.ts` (e2e job).
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"` and `event="janitor.job"` lines.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command excerpts and the `/metrics` excerpt; `ci_green` and `verified` recorded with `br gate report`.

title: P2b Invites: native invites and local passkey accounts, then the Authentik provisioner
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Let the admin invite people who aren't users yet. First the vendor-free default: partifactory's own invite links that create local passkey accounts, so a deployment with plain OIDC (or no IdP) can invite anyone. Then the Authentik provisioner for the example deployment, starting with a permission gate against the real IdP that decides how much of it ships.

## Scope
- [ ] Invite tokens at `parts.<domain>/i/<id>`: kinds `single`, `multi` ("up to N people"), `email`, `recovery`; counted uses, status `sent -> opened -> enrolled | expired | revoked`, 7-day default expiry, one-click revoke, a cap on outstanding invites, enrolment rate-limited per invite and per IP.
- [ ] Local passkey accounts (`webauthn-rs`, discoverable credentials, conditional UI): "What should we call you?" -> Create passkey -> land on the part with the invite's grants applied. Passkey-only; no password path exists.
- [ ] Recovery: "Send a new passkey link" on an existing person (single-use, bound to the account, revokes the old passkeys). Linking a local account to an IdP identity (sign in with OIDC once while signed in locally).
- [ ] Local `pf-*` groups ("Make a group for this"), the invite UI in the share sheet and Admin -> Invites, `part_link_for {action: "invite"}` returning `#share=invite`.
- [ ] Cleanup lists: invitees who never enrolled, people inactive for 180 days, one-click remove with a 10 s undo.
- [ ] The device approval page offers to register a passkey for next time once local accounts exist.
- [ ] The portability lane's IdP-less pass (§5f): no `[idp]`, the admin via `partifactory admin bootstrap` (Slice 1), everyone else a local account through native invites; it joins the lane the rest of P1 built and gates releases from then on.
- [ ] Authentik provisioner gate (`partifactory provision --gate`): try each forbidden operation and expect 403, record `[idp.provisioner] tier = A | B | C` in site config.
- [ ] Authentik invites: `/i/<id>` -> the `partifactory-invite` flow (invitation -> one field -> passkey enrolment -> user write into a holding group -> login); grants and `pf-*` memberships applied by API after enrolment; the IdP invitation deleted at the Nth enrolment.
- [ ] Authentik extras per tier: add by email (the IdP sends the mail), IdP recovery links, IdP-side `pf-*` groups; tier B/C paths hand the change to `provision`.

## Plan refs
§3a Invitations, the admin section (provisioner least privilege), UX click budgets; §4a.6 Invites; §5c provisioner gate; §5e `invites`, `invite_enrolments`, `passkeys`, `users`; §5f Invites + accounts row and the portability lane; §6 P2b; §6a P2b; §7 Identity and admin; decisions 23, 34.

## Considerations
- Inviting and creating groups are outward, admin-only actions with step-up; agents only hand over the `#share=invite` deep link (decision 34). No agent op creates an invite or group.
- Use counts live in partifactory for every kind (native invites have no IdP; Authentik invitations have no use count). Increment inside the single writer so concurrent enrolments on a multi-use link can't overshoot `max_uses`; the CHECK is a backstop.
- Multi-use links exist because single-use links pasted into family chats lose a race. Used or expired links show one plain page that doesn't reveal the part.
- `rp.id` is the apex, as for step-up. Local accounts count in `everyone-signed-in` and are what the IdP-less portability pass runs on.
- Recovery binds to the existing account and revokes the old passkeys in the same transaction, so no zombie account appears and a stolen device stops at once. IdP recovery keeps the same `sub`, so grants keyed on it survive.
- Removal is a revoke, not a delete (`users.status = 'removed'`, epoch bumps, agent connections revoked by the same cascade); undo re-grants from the audit rows.
- Authentik facts (checked 2026-10-23): invitations can't set groups, and have no use count. Unverified items (object-level permission names, `is_superuser` protection, blueprint-over-API, recovery-link permission) are gate items, not assumptions. Every runtime IdP write respects the recorded tier; the UI hides what the tier excludes. The `state` parameter binds the login to the invite; a mismatch or replay grants nothing.
- partifactory never sends email; "By email" shows only with a provisioner. Site config (the gate report, flow names) is private; the public repo ships the gate code and a report template.

## Order inside the phase
Native invites and local accounts -> cleanup lists; then the Authentik provisioner gate -> Authentik invites -> Authentik extras. Needs the Authentik adapter and `provision` from the rest of P1.

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build in the e2e harness with no provisioner: the admin mints an invite from the share sheet (Chromium, virtual authenticator), a new person on webkit-mobile creates a passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out on the next request. With the Authentik provisioner on staging: an invited email enrols the same way and an IdP removal locks them out within a minute.
- CI green on `main` with the invite e2e specs in the harness job and the portability lane (IdP-less pass).
- Logs checked: `event="invite.enrolled"` and `event="epoch.bump"` lines asserted by the e2e run; the gate report lists each forbidden operation and its status.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run id, the gate commands and output excerpts, engine and simulator runtime versions for the invite pass on `webkit-mobile` and in the iOS Simulator (the real-phone acceptance is the non-blocking human-checks bead's); `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Authentik provisioner gate: the report in site config lists each forbidden operation and its observed HTTP status, and records `[idp.provisioner] tier`; the UI hides what the tier excludes
- [ ] Status transitions sent→opened→enrolled; N+1th use refused; expired and revoked links refused.
- [ ] Invitee creates a passkey with the virtual authenticator and lands on the part already granted; can sign in again later with the passkey alone.
- [ ] Recovery keeps the same user id and grants and revokes the old passkey (old passkey assertion fails).
- [ ] Linked account signs in via OIDC and keeps its parts and grants.
- [ ] Click budget: Share → "Invite someone" → Copy link (+ step-up).
- [ ] `part_link_for {action: "invite"}` returns the deep link; the link grants nothing (non-admin sees the sheet without the option).
- [ ] No agent op can create an invite or group on any surface.
- [ ] With the Authentik provisioner on, an invitee enrols with a virtual authenticator through the IdP and lands on the part already granted; the Authentik invitation is deleted at the Nth enrolment
- [ ] A recovery link keeps the same `sub` and grants; tier-B/C paths hand the change to `provision`, run by the admin, instead of calling the IdP
- [ ] Cleanup lists: fixture users (never-enrolled invitees, people inactive 180 days) appear in the right list; one-click remove revokes their grants and connections with audit rows and a 10 s undo re-grants them
- [ ] Local accounts are passkey-only (no password path exists anywhere).
- [ ] The portability lane gains its IdP-less pass (§5f): no `[idp]`, the admin bootstrapped with `partifactory admin bootstrap`, every person a local account, the full suite (including a native invite and enrolment) green; the release tag gate requires it.
- [ ] Concurrent enrolments on a multi-use link never overshoot `max_uses` (increment inside the single writer; the CHECK is a backstop); a used or expired link shows one plain page that doesn't reveal the part.
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `invite` in `part_link_for` in the same change that ships it, and the /skill.md regeneration test passes.
- [ ] The invitee flow (name, Create passkey, land on the part) also runs in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator where WebKit allows a software authenticator, recorded as `verified` evidence; the real-phone invite acceptance is the human-checks bead's and never blocks.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build in the e2e harness with no provisioner: the admin mints an invite from the share sheet, a new person on webkit-mobile creates a passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out on the next request; with the Authentik provisioner on staging, an invited email address enrols the same way and removing them in the IdP locks them out within a minute.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the invite e2e specs in the harness job and the IdP-less portability lane pass.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="invite.enrolled"` and `event="epoch.bump"` lines; the provisioner gate report is recorded.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command output, engine and simulator runtime versions) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.

title: Builds: the build child, Slice 1 kinds, mirror-on-build and build_deps
description: ## Goal Turn a committed source version into a build record and servable output, safely, for the four Slice 1 kinds (`html`, `markdown`, `text`, prebuilt `files`). Every kind is built, so `live` only ever moves through an `ok` build and a broken save never replaces a working page. Mirror-on-build makes Claude-written CDN `
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A build that panics, hangs or exceeds memory marks the build failed/timeout, the server keeps serving, and `live` is unchanged: the panic, infinite-loop and 2 GiB-allocation fixtures yield `failed/builder_crashed`, `timeout` and `failed` respectively, within deadline + 100 ms.
- [ ] A killed worker is replaced and subsequent builds succeed; the pool size formula is verified for 1, 2, 4 and 16 cores.
- [ ] Commit v1, v2, v3 quickly with one worker busy: v2 ends `superseded`, v1 and v3 build; a running build is never cancelled.
- [ ] The same source rebuilt (a restore of v1 as v4 with an identical manifest) reuses the output with no child spawn (`event="build.cache_hit"`); a change to `toolchain_version`, `library_set_version` or the mirror resolution misses the cache.
- [ ] Boot recovery re-queues stale `running` rows.
- [ ] A failed build of v3 leaves live at v2; an `ok` build of v2 arriving after v3 is live does not move live back; `part.live_changed` is appended exactly once per switch, inside the switch's transaction, and reaches a broadcast subscriber only after commit.
- [ ] An `after_check` version whose injected check fails stays off live; with no renderer configured it goes live with the `check_skipped` warning.
- [ ] `wait_for_build` returns within the 2 s and 15 s bounds (test clock), with `status: running` when the build is still going.
- [ ] Brotli: quality 11 for text ≤ 1 MiB, 5 above it, none for already-compressed types, and never for the entry.
- [ ] Each `mirror_failed` reason (`not_allowlisted`, `private_address`, `too_large`, `timeout`, `integrity_mismatch`, `http_<status>`) is produced by a dedicated fixture, leaves the source version committed and `live` unchanged; an off-allowlist redirect fails; a DNS-rebinding fixture (first lookup public, second private) is still refused because the connection uses the vetted IP.
- [ ] jsDelivr `/gh/...` is refused and `/npm/...` allowed; the per-build budgets (200 assets, 50 MiB, depth 8, 30 s) each fail cleanly at budget + 1.
- [ ] A floating version resolves to the pinned URL, is recorded `requested → pinned → hash` in `mirror_cache` with a `cdn_unpinned` warning, and re-uses the cache within 24 h (test clock); an exact version is never re-fetched.
- [ ] Golden mirror fixtures: the contract's React UMD `<script>` pair from cdnjs, Google Fonts CSS with woff2 (fetched with the fixed UA, fonts one level deep), a jsDelivr `+esm` module importing further modules, a CSS `@import` chain, `srcset`, and a `sourceMappingURL` comment; the output references only `blobs-part` URLs, every mirrored file has a `shared_blobs` row, and the source manifest is unchanged byte for byte.
- [ ] An SRI mismatch fixture fails with `integrity_mismatch`; without `integrity=` the fetched hash is recorded in the build record.
- [ ] Kind detection: `index.html` → html, `*.md` → markdown, `*.txt` → text; `files` is never detected; an `.svg` entry in Slice 1 is `invalid_input` naming the kinds that exist; a `.txt` part's raw output equals its input bytes exactly, with stable 1-based `L1..Ln` anchors; the golden render corpus is byte-stable across runs and machines.
- [ ] The entry HTML is stored with only the sandbox rewrites applied (no prelude tag, import map, `pf-boot` or `pf-shell.css` hash at build time); a root-relative string literal none of the rewrites can reach yields `root_relative_url`.
- [ ] Each build with mirrored libraries writes `build_deps` rows: cdnjs, jsDelivr `/npm/`, unpkg and esm.sh URLs map to npm `name@version`; an unparseable URL is stored with ecosystem `unknown` and the URL as written; deleting a build deletes its rows (decision 48, provisional).
- [ ] The `[mirror] test_resolve` override pins only the named hosts, every other private resolution is still refused, and `config check` rejects the key in a release build.
- [ ] No build log line contains a fixture's canary content string or a URL query string.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` (dev feature) running in the e2e harness with the fake CDN, `partifactory dev put` builds an html, a markdown, a text and a `files` part to `ok`; their output references only `blobs-part` URLs; `mirror_cache` and `build_deps` rows are present (npm `name@version`, and `unknown` for an unparseable URL); private-address and off-allowlist fixtures end `mirror_failed` with `live` unchanged; a fault-injection panic ends `builder_crashed` while `/healthz` keeps answering.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the `pf-build` unit, golden and integration tests in the nextest job (`ci/test.sh`).
- [ ] GATE: The run's server JSONL shows `event="build.finished"` for each build and `event="egress.refused" reason="private_address"`, with no file content or query strings logged.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite and every earlier bead's gate tests still pass.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, the dev commands and a `builds`/`build_deps` excerpt) and `br gate report` passes for `ci_green` and `verified`.

comments.author: admin
comments.text:
From spike pf-twz8 (docs/spikes/compiler.md, spikes/spike-compiler): the build-child protocol is a GO, observed in tests. Start from spikes/spike-compiler/src/lib.rs:
(1) Re-exec current_exe() as build-worker, with piped stdin/stdout. Frames are a u32 big-endian length + CBOR (ciborium =0.2.2) with a 64 MiB cap. One worker serves many requests until EOF.
(2) Parent: a reader thread per worker feeding a channel, recv_timeout(deadline). On timeout, child.kill() (SIGKILL) + reap -> timeout. EOF or a bad frame -> reap and record the signal -> builder_crashed. The server is never affected.
(3) Pool of max(1, min(2, cores/2)) pre-forked workers that respawns any worker that dies. Measured: spawn + ping costs ~3 ms p50 against 0.02 ms warm, so the pool is for isolation and steadiness more than speed.
(4) Memory: in the worker, setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS, 1 GiB) plus a counting #[global_allocator] armed only in worker mode. macOS doesn't enforce RLIMIT_AS; on Linux both apply. A breach aborts with SIGABRT -> builder_crashed. For tools the worker runs (esbuild), use env_clear(), a private tempdir, and rlimits via pre_exec or a cgroup.
(5) Outcomes ok|failed|timeout|builder_crashed, logged as event="build.child" outcome=... Port the 5 tests in spikes/spike-compiler/tests/child.rs (panic, hang at the deadline, memory breach, virtual React resolved once via the import map, compile_error is failed, not a crash).
The Slice 1 kinds can use the same child unchanged.

comments.author: GrayLark
comments.text: Preparatory implementation recovered from the prior worker draft: CBOR child protocol, deny-network sandbox, worker memory/deadline faults, queue recovery/supersession, monotonic live switch, CheckGate, restore cache reuse, CDN TLS mirroring and exact source preservation. Workspace child tests pass on the actual partifactory binary. Gate runs in progress; bead remains blocked by prerequisite gate closures, with no policy bypass.

title: Updates and advisories: OSV matching, the advisory surfaces, part_edit update, auto-update
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Parts are built once and left alone, so partifactory must notice when a library a part carries gets a known vulnerability, say so where people and agents already look, and make the fix one call or one tap, without ever changing a live part by itself. Slice 1 already records each build's library list (`build_deps`, decision 48); this epic adds the advisory data, matching, the surfaces and the update paths for frontends. Backend image SBOMs and base-image digest checks belong to P2a.

## Scope
- [ ] Advisories spike first: measure the OSV bulk dump sizes for the ecosystems in use, matching speed against 10k `build_deps` rows, and pick Syft or Trivy as the runner's pinned scanner image (for P2a); sets the advisory-DB cap. Go/no-go note in `docs/spikes/advisories.md`.
- [ ] `AdvisorySource` adapter, chosen by `[advisories] source`: `osv-bulk` (default: daily download of `https://storage.googleapis.com/osv-vulnerabilities/<ECOSYSTEM>/all.zip`, incremental from `modified_id.csv`, stored under `/data/advisories/`, matched locally), `osv-api` (`POST /v1/querybatch`, sends only package names and versions; the config comment says so), `none` (a warning on Health and in `doctor`). Attribution stored and shown per record (CC-BY 4.0, CC0, MIT, Apache, CC-BY-SA for Ubuntu).
- [ ] Nightly matching against `build_deps` (and, once P2a lands, stored SBOMs) writing `advisories` rows (`part_id, build_id, ecosystem, package, version, osv_id, severity, fixed_in, first_seen, state open|fixed|ignored, ignored_by, reason`); `unknown` deps listed as such; inline code reported as "inline code isn't checked".
- [ ] Severity in context: OSV severity plus context; frontend advisories shown, not alarmed, raised one level when the part has a Can-contribute link or a backend; never a bare CVSS number.
- [ ] Surfaces: chrome badge for owner and editors (with Update libraries and Ignore…), counts on Health and in Insights (Parts page, by layer and severity, time open), `advisories` in `part_get`, `dep_advisory` warning in `part_check` and `build.warnings`, a `part.advisory` event, the ops webhook only for a critical advisory on a backend or a contribute-link part.
- [ ] Fix paths: `part_edit {rebuild: true, update: "patch" | "minor" | "latest"}` re-resolves recorded libraries within the range and builds a new version under the part's `live` setting; the Update libraries button (2 interactions, undo is the normal restore); ignore with a reason by a person or an agent with `parts:write`, audited.
- [ ] Auto-update (decision 49, provisional): `[advisories] auto_update = "never" | "patch"`, per part override; frontends default `never`; a part on `patch` updates only with `fixed_in`, through `after_check`, rolled back automatically on a failed check, recorded as `system`. The backend default (`patch`) and its rollback, which is a backend rollback and so code only and best effort (decision 51), land with P2a when backends join matching.
- [ ] Storage and retention rows (§5h): advisory DB latest sync only under a cap; SBOMs kept with their build under a per-build cap; `advisories` rows deleted with their build; the janitor covers all three and the retention test gains the rows. `/data/advisories/` is never exported.
- [ ] Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `update` on `part_edit` and `advisories` on `part_get` (item shape `{ecosystem, package, version, osv_id, severity, context, fixed_in, state, attribution}`) in the same change that ships them.

## Plan refs
§3h Updates and advisories; §4 op table (`part_edit`, `part_get`), Events; §4a.6 Part view (Advisories), Admin Health; §4a.7 budgets; §4b warnings; §5e `build_deps`, `advisories`; §5f Advisory data row; §5g Parts page; §5h rows; §7 Updates and advisories; decisions 44-49.

## Considerations
- Immutability stays the rule: old builds keep their frozen import maps and image digests, so rollback stays exact. An update is always a new version.
- `osv-bulk` is the default because only public data comes in and nothing goes out about what the household runs. With `osv-api`, nothing but ecosystem, package and version may leave (canary test).
- It fails open: a DB more than 7 days stale turns Health amber; builds never block on it.
- No approval queues and no notifications for people: a finding is a record, not a queue.
- **What plugs in later, without an edge** (§6a puts this epic right after Slice 1, beside the rest of P1): the `doctor` warning for `source = none` and the stale-DB check (`doctor` is the rest of P1's), the Insights Parts-page counts (the Insights pages are the rest of P2's) and the ops webhook (the rest of P1's). Whichever lands second wires the connection, and its bead says so. Everything backend (SBOM matching, base-image `update`, the backend severity bump and webhook case, the backend auto-update default and rollback) is P2a's, which depends on this epic.
- Dump sizes and matching speed are unmeasured; the spike sets the cap and decides whether matching needs an index beyond `build_deps_pkg`.

## Order inside the phase
The spike → OSV sync and matching with its surfaces → `update` and the Update libraries button → auto-update. Backend SBOMs and base-image checks join from P2a.

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build in the e2e harness: a part built against a library with a seeded OSV fixture advisory shows the badge, the Health count, `advisories` in `part_get` and `dep_advisory` in `part_check`; Update libraries makes a new version that goes live under `after_check`, and restore undoes it.
- Each child bead's own gate observed; CI green on `main` with the advisories suites; logs checked: `event="advisory.sync"`, `event="advisory.match"` and the `part.advisory` event.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, `communal_pixel_editor` included, passes.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run ids, the spike note, a screenshot of the badge; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The advisories spike note records the OSV dump sizes for the ecosystems in use, matching time against 10k `build_deps` rows, the advisory-DB cap, and the Syft-or-Trivy choice for the runner, with the versions it ran on.
- [ ] With the default `osv-bulk` source the advisory DB syncs daily into `/data/advisories/`, incrementally after the first download, and nothing about parts leaves the box.
- [ ] With `source = "osv-api"`, the outbound requests carry only ecosystem, package name and version, never part content, names, titles or URLs (canary test).
- [ ] With `source = "none"`, Health shows a warning, and so does `doctor` (its advisory slot is filled by whichever of this epic and `doctor` lands second).
- [ ] An advisory DB more than 7 days stale turns Health amber, and a build with the DB stale or missing still succeeds (fail open).
- [ ] Matching a seeded OSV fixture against `build_deps` writes an `advisories` row per affected build; an `unknown` dependency is listed as unknown, and the part's list says inline code isn't checked.
- [ ] Severity is shown as OSV severity plus context; a frontend advisory is raised one level when the part has a Can-contribute link (the backend case is tested with P2a), and is never shown as a bare CVSS number.
- [ ] An open advisory appears as a chrome badge for the owner and editors, a count on Health and in Insights (the Insights Parts-page count is wired by whichever of this epic and the Insights pages lands second), `advisories` in `part_get`, a `dep_advisory` warning in `part_check` and `build.warnings`, and a `part.advisory` event; each record shows its attribution.
- [ ] The ops webhook fires only for a critical advisory on a part with a contribute link (the backend case is P2a's) and for nothing below critical.
- [ ] `part_edit {rebuild: true, update: "patch"}` re-resolves the recorded libraries within the range and builds a new version that goes live under the part's `live` setting; restore undoes it.
- [ ] Update libraries in the chrome takes 2 interactions; Ignore asks for a reason, works for a person or an agent with `parts:write`, and is audited.
- [ ] An advisory sync or match never changes a live part's import map or image digest; only `part_edit {update}`, Update libraries or opt-in auto-update makes a new version, and auto-update is recorded as `system`.
- [ ] `[advisories] auto_update` is read from site config with a per-part override; frontends default to `never`; a part set to `patch` updates only on an advisory with `fixed_in`, through the `after_check` gate, is recorded as `system`, and rolls back automatically when the check fails. (The backend default `patch` and its code-only rollback are P2a's.)
- [ ] `advisories` rows are deleted with their build; the advisory DB keeps only the latest sync under its cap; the retention test covers both, and `/data/advisories/` is never in an export.
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `update` on `part_edit` and `advisories` on `part_get` in the same change that ships them, and the `/skill.md` regeneration test passes.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build in the e2e harness: a part with a seeded fixture advisory shows the badge, the Health count, `part_get` advisories and the `dep_advisory` warning; Update libraries makes a new version live under `after_check`; restore undoes it.
- [ ] GATE: Every bead this epic is broken into is closed with its own observed gate.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the advisory sync, matching, surfaces and canary suites.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the runs assert `event="advisory.sync"`, `event="advisory.match"` and the `part.advisory` event.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, `communal_pixel_editor` included, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run ids, the spike note and a badge screenshot in `br close --reason`, with `ci_green` and `verified` reported.

title: The op registry and core ops: part_create, part_edit, part_get, the HTTPS API and the part CLI
description:
## Goal
Define every agent-facing op once, in Rust, and render it as the HTTPS JSON API (with a truthful OpenAPI 3.1 document) and the `part` CLI, with one error catalogue written so an LLM can self-correct. Deliver the core ops behind them: `part_create` over the store's part service, the `part_edit` engine (ordered anchor edits, per-file compare-and-set, auto-rebase, idempotent replay, mode fields) and the `part_get` read path. MCP and discovery are later generated from the same registry, so nothing exists on one surface only.

## Scope
- [ ] Registry crate: `trait Op` (`NAME`, `SCOPE`, `HINTS`, `Output`, executable `examples()`, `run`), a registry macro, `Ctx` with the one `(person, connection, scopes, spaces)` principal, the Slice 1 op types exactly as in docs/agent-contract.md (`part_check`, `part_data`, `part_link_for` typed here, filled by their beads); `deny_unknown_fields` with "did you mean"; `request_id` format (1–128 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, required on every mutating op); `SCOPE` enforced by the registry for every op, with `parts:delete` for `delete`/`undelete`.
- [ ] One `OpError` catalogue with the §4b HTTP and CLI-exit maps; an op or error without description, hint and example fails the build; `insta` schema snapshots; non-object outputs wrapped for rmcp. Every API error body and CLI `--json` error carries the request id from the observability bead, so a report can be matched to its log lines.
- [ ] HTTPS API on `:8080`: `POST /api/v1/{op}` (200 on success), GET aliases (`GET /api/v1/parts/{name}`, `…/files/{path}`) and `PUT …/files/{path}` with `If-Match` over the same handlers; pluggable bearer authenticator (dev token under the `dev` feature until agent connections land); 401 + `WWW-Authenticate`, 429 + `Retry-After`; JSON-RPC body gets the "MCP lives at /mcp" hint; bodies capped before auth (8 MiB request, 2 MiB source file, 25 MiB blob).
- [ ] Blob have/need (`POST /api/v1/blobs`, `POST /api/v1/blobs/missing`, `{path: {blob: sha256}}` in writes); `/openapi.json` via `aide` (ETag = build hash) with a generated `Error.code` enum, an additive-only snapshot test and the GPT Actions lint.
- [ ] `part` CLI from the registry: `part <op> --json @file|-`, scalar flags, aliases `put` (file or dir, `--name`, `--kind`), `get`, `edit --replace`, `check`, `help <op>`; one `request_id` per invocation reused on retry; token from `PARTIFACTORY_TOKEN`, keychain, then a mode-600 config file, server from `PARTIFACTORY_URL`; §4b exit codes. (`part login` is added by the agent connections bead, `part skill install` by the MCP and discovery bead.)
- [ ] `part_create` op over the store's part service: every Slice 1 field in the contract (`title`, `name`, `kind`, `content`/`files`, `space`, `from`, `expires_in`, `tags`, `description`, `snapshots`, `shared_data_writers`, `live`, `check_only`, `request_id`), name reserved in the same transaction, `< 10 ms` before any build, `check_only` → `{available, name, suggestions}`, `name_taken` with suggestions, `kind` required with `content`, `upload` rejected as `unknown_field` until after Slice 1.
- [ ] `part_edit` engine: `replace`/`write`/`delete`/`rename` in order, all or none, byte-exact anchors occurring exactly once; §3d limits (≤ 64 edits, `old_str` ≤ 64 KiB, file ≤ 2 MiB, request ≤ 8 MiB); anchor errors with `edit_index`, best-match context (Levenshtein ≥ 0.6, else the file's first 600 chars, ±3 lines, ≤ 2 KiB), `lines`, `similarity`.
- [ ] Rebase inside the single writer (`base_unknown`, `invalid_against_base`, `if_match` against head, `rebased_from`), wrapped in the part service's idempotency layer: replay checked before anchors, a rejected write stores nothing, different arguments under a committed id → `request_id_reused`.
- [ ] Mode fields, exactly one per call: `restore`, `delete` (`parts:delete`, epoch bump), `undelete`, `rebuild`, `meta` (no version; `shared_data_writers` audited, freeze hook); `wait` 2 s, or 15 s with `check`/`after_check`; `live` stored on the version; `check_skipped` while no renderer exists.
- [ ] `part_get`: version selection (`head`, `live`, n), `files`, `content` for parts ≤ 32 KiB, `file`/`range` (`range` needs `file`), `history`, `diff_from`/`diff_to`, `build: <id>` with its log, the latest 20 `runtime_errors`, `not_found` outside the connection's spaces.

## Plan refs
§3c; §3d Creation contract, Idempotent, Concurrency contract, Big files, `wait`; §3e Versions and the bin; §4 op table, Slice 1 op fields, Names, `part` CLI; §4b registry, Adapters, Errors; §5d body caps; docs/agent-contract.md "Calling ops", "The ops", "Kinds", "Errors", Rules 1-2; decision 11.

## Considerations
- `schemars` + `aide` (and rmcp's `schemars`) give one schema generator. `v1` is additive only: a breaking change is a new op name.
- An invisible part is `not_found`, never `forbidden`. A failed build is not an error (200, `build.status: "failed"`).
- One writer serialises commits, so versions are gap-free and rebase runs in the same critical section.
- The store bead owns the part service (create, fork, scratch, names, idempotency, get, history, diff, bin, restore); this bead owns the op layer over it: typed inputs, scope and space checks, error mapping and the surfaces. Don't reimplement service logic here.
- CLI aliases are sugar and add no behaviour; the dev token works only on a `dev`-feature server.
- Round 3: `part_edit {update}` and `part_get` `advisories` come with the advisories work; the contract gains both then.
- MCP, `/skill.md` and four-driver conformance are the MCP, discovery and conformance bead.
- Blocked by the identity bead (the policy engine decides `not_found` and roles) and by the builds bead (`part put`, `wait` and `rebuild` need real builds). It does not wait for the part host: `delete` bumps epochs through the store bead's `EpochStore`, and `part_get`'s `runtime_errors` reads rows the tests seed directly (the prelude's real `errors.report` path is the part host bead's `runtime_errors.spec.ts`). So the registry runs beside the part host, as §6a's third chain. The wrapper bead runs in parallel; its chrome `summary` becomes a view over `part_get` once both have landed. The agent connections bead builds on this one (`/api`, the CLI).
- `/api` registers its rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead); 429 + `Retry-After` come from it.
- The Slice 1 `OpError` catalogue holds only codes reachable in Slice 1 (the table test requires each one to be reachable). Codes PLAN §4b lists for later features (`claimed`, `block_*`, `cursor_expired`, `image_not_allowed`, `backends_unavailable`, `version_conflict`) join the catalogue, the OpenAPI `Error.code` enum and the contract with the feature that raises them; the enum is additive, so that isn't a breaking change.

## Tests and logging
- Registry: `pf_ops::snapshots::schemas_match`, `catalogue::*` (+ a `trybuild` negative), `validate::unknown_field_suggests`, `validate::request_id_format`, `scope::every_op_enforces_scope`, `examples::examples_roundtrip`.
- Engine: `pf_model::edit::tests` table, `prop::all_or_none`, golden best-match fixtures, `pf_model::rebase::tests`, `concurrent_editors.rs`, `part_edit_end_to_end.rs`, `part_edit_modes.rs`.
- API/CLI: `openapi.rs`, `blobs.rs`, `errors.rs`, `gpt_actions_lint.rs`, `timeout_retry.rs`, `part_create_op.rs`, `part_get_op.rs`, `part_edit_wait.rs`, `runtime_errors_roundtrip.rs`; CLI `roundtrip.rs`, `exit_codes.rs`, `put_dir.rs`, `credentials.rs`, `request_id.rs`.
- Logs asserted: `event="http.request" route_class="api" op outcome` with `request_id`; `event="op" op="part_create" surface="cli"`; `event="part.edit" rebased_from`; no `event="blob.put"` on a second `put ./dist`; no content (canary).

## Verification gate
- On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness (dev token): `part put x.html --name packing` then `part get packing` returns the same bytes; a second `part put ./dist` uploads nothing; two disjoint edits from one base both commit; a retried timed-out edit returns `replayed: true`; `/openapi.json` validates as OAS 3.1.
- CI green on `main`: the tests above in the nextest job, the OpenAPI snapshot and the GPT Actions lint.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="http.request" route_class="api"` lines and zero `blob.put` on the second put.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts; `ci_green` and `verified` reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Snapshot test of generated JSON Schemas (including `part_edit`'s schema and examples); adding an op or error without a description, hint and example fails the build.
- [ ] Slice 1 op types match docs/agent-contract.md field-for-field; unknown fields are rejected as `unknown_field` with a suggestion; each op example parses against its schemas.
- [ ] OpenAPI validates as OAS 3.1; every route is in the document and vice versa; the snapshot test fails on a non-additive diff.
- [ ] Table-driven test of every error code: each variant is reachable with the catalogue shape, the right `details`, HTTP status and CLI exit code.
- [ ] Error responses: 401 carries `WWW-Authenticate`, 429 carries `Retry-After`; bodies over 8 MiB get 413 `too_large` before auth; a JSON-RPC body on `/api` gets the "MCP lives at /mcp" hint.
- [ ] Every op enforces its `SCOPE`: a token without it gets `forbidden {scope_needed}`; `part_edit {delete}` and `{undelete}` need `parts:delete`; a `request_id` outside 1–128 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` is `invalid_input`.
- [ ] `part put x.html --name packing` then `part get packing` returns the same bytes; `part put ./dist --kind files` twice uploads nothing the second time; exit codes follow the §4b map.
- [ ] `part_create` with no files returns `head: 0, live: null, build: null`, with `content` `head: 1, build.status: "queued"`; `check_only` returns `{available, name, suggestions}` and creates nothing; a taken name is `name_taken` with free suggestions; `content` without `kind` is `invalid_input`; `upload` is `unknown_field`.
- [ ] Edits apply in order (edit 2 can target text introduced by edit 1); any failure leaves inputs untouched and saves nothing (all or none).
- [ ] Two agents editing disjoint anchors from one base both commit (`rebased_from` on the second); an overlapping anchor change → `anchor_not_found` with context, `lines` and `similarity`.
- [ ] A retried timed-out edit returns the original result with `replayed: true`, never `anchor_not_found`; a rejected write leaves no idempotency row, so the fixed call may reuse the id; different arguments under a committed id → `request_id_reused`.
- [ ] Each mode works and is exclusive; restore of v3 creates v(n+1) equal to v3; `meta` creates no version and audits a `shared_data_writers` change.
- [ ] `wait` timings respected (2 s / 15 s); with no renderer, `live: "after_check"` behaves as `always` with `check_skipped`.
- [ ] `part_get` on a 20 KiB single-file part returns the file; on a 100 KiB part it returns the file list, and a `range` returns exactly those lines; `history` and `diff_from`/`diff_to` return the contract's shapes; a seeded `runtime_errors` row appears in `part_get`'s `runtime_errors` (latest 20).
- [ ] `part_get` with a part outside the connection's spaces → `not_found`; `build: <id>` returns the build record with its log.
- [ ] A small `part_edit` with no compile has p99 < 10 ms on the bench fixture (tracked, not gated).
- [ ] `part_edit {update}` and `part_get` `advisories` are absent in Slice 1 (`unknown_field`); they arrive with the advisories work, and docs/agent-contract.md gains both sections in the same change.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness with a dev token, `part put`/`part get` round-trips bytes, a second `part put ./dist` uploads nothing, two disjoint edits from one base both commit (`rebased_from` on the second), a retried timed-out edit returns `replayed: true`, and `/openapi.json` validates as OAS 3.1.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the registry, edit-engine, API and CLI tests (nextest job), the OpenAPI snapshot test and the GPT Actions lint.
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="http.request" route_class="api" op=… outcome=…` lines with request ids, and zero `event="blob.put"` lines on the second put.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run id, gate command excerpts) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.

title: The rest of P1: edge, identity extras, workspace extras, previews (posters and og:video), Insights store, doctor, portability lane, bench
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Finish P1 "Edge + identity" beyond what Slice 1 shipped: adapters for the example deployment, the everyday workspace UI, the admin area, the Insights store with traces and logs, `doctor`, the portability lane that proves no vendor is required, and the honest performance comparison. P1 is done when the admin opens a part on a phone via SSO, the portability lane is green, a public link unfurls as a titled card from mobile data, the §7 checklist passes from outside, and the drill restores everything on a second OCI host in under 15 minutes.

## Scope
- [ ] Titled public card: SVG template -> usvg/resvg -> 1200x630 PNG with bundled Plex fonts and rustybuzz wrapping, content-addressed `/og/<sha256>.png`; the root goes back to the content-free card when the last public link is revoked.
- [ ] Previews (§4c "Previews: posters always, `og:video` when the agent wants one", decision 53; pulled forward from P4), after the titled card:
  - **Automatic posters.** A low-priority `preview` render job on every new live version, coalesced, never on the save path. It screenshots the live version at 1200x630 as a JPEG part blob into `part_previews`. The agent's `preview.poster` wins; with the sidecar off, the titled card is the poster. The poster is also the gallery thumbnail, replacing Slice 1's latest-render screenshot.
  - **Optional `og:video`, the agent's choice** (default `"off"`):
    - The agent's own MP4 (H.264 `yuv420p`, no audio, ≤ 10 s, ≤ 1280x720, ≤ 8 MiB, `moov` first), probed in the build child, with `preview_invalid` naming the fault.
    - Or `preview.video: "record"`: the same job records 2–10 s of CDP screencast while running `preview.actions`, or a slow scroll without them, encoded by `ffmpeg` in the render image (pinned by digest).
    - The last good clip survives a failed recording.
  - **Public links:** `public_links.preview` is `video | image | card`, default `video`, falling back to the poster. The share sheet rung offers Preview: Video · Image · Card only, with the poster and the "apps keep their own copy" line. An agent can't change it.
  - **Serving:** `https://<name>-part.<domain>/og/<sha256>.{mp4,jpg}` on the part host only, cookie-free, `nosniff`, `Accept-Ranges`/206, `public, max-age=3600`. It answers only while an active public link allows it and is otherwise byte-identical to an unknown path. The tags are `og:image` = the poster plus `og:video`, `:secure_url`, `:type`, `:width` and `:height` with a clip; `twitter:card` stays `summary_large_image`.
  - **Gallery clips:** muted and looped while on screen, never under `prefers-reduced-motion`, from `/api/v1/thumbs/<part>?v=<n>&media=video` (session- and grant-checked, `private, immutable`).
  - **Agent surface, with its contract section in the same change:**
    - `preview` on `part_create` and in `part_edit {meta}`;
    - `part_check {record: true}`: the clip the server would make, stored nowhere; HTTP `video: {url, expires_at, width, height, seconds, bytes}`, MCP the poster block plus a link;
    - `part_get.preview`;
    - the `preview_invalid` error;
    - `/skill.md` guidance: a poster is automatic, and agents should consider a clip for animated or interactive parts.
  - **Disk:** the "Previews" store-cap row (2 GiB) with its fill-past-cap case; at the cap new previews stop and the last poster or the titled card is used.
- [ ] Search: FTS5 over title, description, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 x recency; policy-filtered results.
- [ ] Workspace extras: versions rail (restore, compare, preview old), Bin view, search sheet, agent activity, Details sheet, install part as app, ⋯ extras (zip, Pin with a `pins` table), inward share rungs, Move to Family, Ask for access.
- [ ] `partifactory provision`: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, `manual` providers, ownership rules, dry-run, run log, `family` + `system` spaces.
- [ ] Cloudflare adapter (tunnel ingress + `tunnel` compose profile, DNS plugin, cache rules, one rate rule, fallback Worker, health probe; sandbox spike item 11, the wildcard CNAME to the tunnel serving a new `*-part` name, is verified here) and the Authentik spike, then the Authentik adapter (60 s directory poll, cloned flows, invite flow, provisioner account).
- [ ] Optional ops-alert webhook, off by default, one signer shared with agent webhooks.
- [ ] Deliverable extras: nginx and Traefik configs (taking the proxy settings the sandbox spike recorded for them in item 12, `docs/spikes/sandbox.md`), arm64, SBOM, cosign, example CI workflows.
- [ ] `partifactory doctor` with an exit-code table and hook slots (provisioner, runner firewall, advisories).
- [ ] Insights store (`insights.db`, its own writer, typed content-free events, salted viewer keys, rollups), request-id propagation + tail-sampled traces, the log pipeline (zstd segments, export/tail, push adapters), and the no-content-in-logs fuzz test.
- [ ] Admin area shell: tabs, step-up chip, Audit ledger, People/Groups/Agents, the `unsandboxed` toggle and list, owner change.
- [ ] Workspace PWA + the cross-page error-page e2e; visual regression suite; thumbnails endpoint and `views?` in `part_get`; the one-screen regrant UI.
- [ ] Portability lane: Dex pass, adapter-excluded build, vendor egress blocked, release tag gate, `communal_pixel_editor` in the lane. The IdP-less pass (local passkey accounts, `admin bootstrap`) joins the lane in P2b, which ships local accounts.
- [ ] nginx + HAProxy comparison on the real content path (needs the regression bench, which the tsx and rest-of-P0 epic carries).

## Plan refs
§3 Topology and ingress; §3a identity, Ask for access, Admin; §3e Search; §4 ops alerts; §4a.6-§4a.7 screens and budgets; §4c Tier (a); §5a; §5b; §5c provision; §5d doctor; §5f portability lane; §5g Insights; §5h; §6 P1; §6a "The rest of P1"; §7; decisions 21-24, 32, 33, 40, 42.

## Considerations
- Adapters never land before their generic default, and nothing outside an adapter may depend on its results. Authentik facts (checked 2026-10-23): invitations can't set groups and have no use count; conditional-UI passkeys need a WebAuthn validation stage on the identification stage (2025.12+). Spike results live in the private site repo; the public repo keeps a generic `docs/spikes/authentik.md`.
- Cloudflare: Free allows one rate-limit rule (IP only, 10 s), and it caches by file extension, so `blobs-part/b/*` and `parts/og/*` need "eligible for cache" rules. Part blobs are `private` and must never be HIT. Edge caching is never needed for correctness.
- Directory fail open: an unreachable IdP keeps last-known membership, marks it stale (`kv` `directory.stale_since`), never bumps an epoch, and alerts after 10 minutes (`idp_unreachable_10m`); a definite removal fails closed.
- Previews follow the audience, not the card: a private part's unfurl never carries a poster or a clip, because the unfurler can't open it. Public links get them by default (the admin, 2026-10-23), and the gallery only for viewers who could open the part. Agents never have to make a clip; the poster always exists.
- Card inputs are fixed fields, never part content; separate private/public input types make the content-free guarantee a compile-time fact. The audience decides the card, never the User-Agent.
- Search indexes readable text, never code; notes and comments index through hooks the P2 work calls. No query text in logs.
- Insights never back-pressures serving: bounded channel, drop and count. No free-text fields, no raw IPs (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48, HMAC with a daily in-memory salt); `insights.db` already exists from Slice 1 (the janitor writes `janitor_runs` there), so adopt it, don't re-author the DDL. Request ids use one prefix, `r_`.
- Stdout always carries every log line; disk segments and push adapters can drop, stdout can't. OTLP logs use the `[otlp]` section (P4 adds traces and metrics to it).
- `/admin/*` answers non-admins with 403 (§7), never 404. The `/_pf/doctor` probe is byte-identical whether a part exists or not.
- The comparison runs off-hours on the deploy host; shared CI runners are too noisy to gate on. Results are tracked, not gated.
- §5f's lane has a second pass with no IdP at all. It needs local passkey accounts and `partifactory admin bootstrap`, which are P2b's (and P2b depends on this epic), so this epic's lane ships the Dex pass and P2b adds the IdP-less pass and gates on it.
- The Agents page's "Undo all" revokes the grants a connection made, and only agent sharing (`share:household`, the rest of P2) makes such grants; the page ships here and its Undo-all test lands with agent sharing.
- Work that plugs in later without an edge: doctor's provisioner probe (P2b gate), runner-firewall check (P2a), advisory checks (the advisories epic, which may land before or after `doctor`: whichever lands second fills the slot); the Insights store and log pipeline register janitor jobs and retention-test rows when they land.

## Order inside the phase
search -> the workspace extras; `provision` -> the Cloudflare and Authentik adapters (Authentik spike first); `doctor` after the disk budget; the Insights store -> traces and the log pipeline -> the no-content fuzz test; the ops-alert webhook after Health and the disk budget; the deliverable extras -> the portability lane; the bench -> the nginx/HAProxy comparison; the titled card after the wrapper.

## Verification gate
- Previews: on the compose deployment, the pixel board with `preview: {video: "record", actions: [taps that paint]}` and a public link unfurls (a Playwright-driven unfurl fetch) with the poster and a playable `og:video` (206 on a range request); switching the link to Card only removes both at once; the e2e JSONL shows `event="preview.done" kind="video"`.
- Observed on a real build: the P1 "Done when" on the compose deployment, with the phone steps on Playwright's mobile projects and in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (local lane, evidence attached to `verified`): SSO open at the part's own host, a signed-out public link unfurling as the titled card, §7 passing from outside against staging, the drill restoring everything on a second OCI host in < 15 min, `doctor` all-ok, the portability lane green from the published compose file. Real phones never block: the real-phone pass is the non-blocking human-checks bead's.
- Every bead this epic becomes closes with its own observed gate first.
- CI green on `main` with the lane, `no-content-in-logs`, visual regression and the new e2e specs required.
- Logs checked: `provision.step`, `doctor.check`, `directory.poll`, `search.query`, `alert.sent` asserted in the e2e runs.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, every Slice 1 gate test and `communal_pixel_editor` still pass.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI ids, lane summary JSON, the comparison table, engine and simulator runtime versions, `br gate report` for `ci_green` and `verified`.

title: Prelude pagehide storage flush is rejected by the runtime Fetch Metadata guard
description: Observed Chromium 1.64.1 on the Mac: an opaque sandbox sends navigator.sendBeacon with a text/plain Blob as Origin:null, Sec-Fetch-Mode:no-cors (target/beacon-mode.json). The runtime deliberately requires cors, so the inherited prelude loses dirty localStorage on pagehide. Use native fetch with credentials:omit, mode:cors and keepalive:true for pagehide writes; keep the simple text/plain payload and foreign-origin checks. Update the part-host scope to describe a pagehide keepalive flush and add a real browser close-within-100-ms persistence regression. Verification: actual served part across Chromium, WebKit and Firefox; no OPTIONS; persisted value after immediate page close/reopen; guard still rejects no-cors and foreign origins; CI green and full e2e.

title: Spike: opaque-origin sandbox and wrapper flow on every browser engine (emulated and simulated)
description:
## Goal
Verify, in the first week and before the content listener starts, every browser behaviour the serving model rests on: each part document served with CSP `sandbox` (no `allow-same-origin`) runs in an opaque origin with no cookies, on its own host `<name>-part.<domain>`, framed by a trusted wrapper at the part host's root that gets its cap from a `#pf=` fragment, with admin step-up by WebAuthn with `rp.id` = the apex. Every engine is covered by emulation or simulation, so nothing here waits on a person or a phone: Playwright Chromium (desktop, and mobile emulation with the virtual authenticator), Playwright WebKit (desktop and a mobile profile), Playwright Firefox, and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator on the Mac. If WebKit or the simulator behaves differently, the part host, prelude and wrapper change now rather than after they're built. Items 10, 12 and 13 decide the wrapper flow.

## Scope
- [ ] A throwaway rig in `tests/sandbox-spike/` on a TLS test domain with an internal-CA wildcard cert: workspace host `parts.` setting a `__Host-` `SameSite=Lax` test cookie, part hosts `a-part.` and `b-part.`, a sibling `canary.` service that echoes received cookies and headers, and `blobs-part.`. Part responses carry the canonical CSP verbatim from §2 and answer `Origin: null` with `ACAO: null` + `Vary: Origin`, never `Allow-Credentials` or `CORP`. Every item is a self-reporting page that posts `{item, browser, ua, result, detail}` to a collector, so the same page runs under Playwright and under `simctl openurl`.
- [ ] Lanes: `run.sh` drives Playwright Chromium (`chromium-desktop`, `chromium-mobile` with a phone viewport, touch and the CDP virtual authenticator), WebKit (`webkit-desktop`, `webkit-mobile`) and Firefox (`firefox-desktop`), all in CI. `ios-sim.sh` drives Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`xcrun simctl boot`, `simctl keychain add-root-cert` for the rig CA, `simctl openurl` per item page, `simctl io screenshot` after each) locally on the Mac, or on a macOS runner if one exists; its `results.jsonl` and screenshots are attached as evidence. The observability bead grows `tests/device/ios-sim.sh` from this script and collector.
- [ ] Items 1-9 (opaque-origin semantics, §5 Maturity check), one page each: `'self'` matching; `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site` values on a fetch to the part's own host, plus the `Sec-Fetch-Dest`/`Sec-Fetch-Mode` values for a framed navigation, a top-level navigation and a subresource (the part host's re-grant rule keys on them); fetch, module scripts and `import()` with `ACAO: null`; the `localStorage` redefinition visible to later scripts; blob workers and the relative-URL wrapper; popups escaping the sandbox, clipboard, `navigator.share`, fullscreen; `cookieStore.set` and `document.cookie` failing; no Lax cookies on fetch/POST to a sibling service or the workspace; `sandbox` honoured from the header but not from `Report-Only` or `<meta>`.
- [ ] Item 10, the wrapper flow (seven checks): no-cap `location.replace` to a stub `/grant`; the `#pf=` fragment surviving the 302; `history.replaceState` clearing it before any other script, never in `Referer` or logs; explicit part-host `frame-ancestors` admitting the same-host wrapper; a credentialed same-site `fetch` to the workspace carrying the Lax cookie, with WebKit's tracking prevention on (desktop WebKit, `webkit-mobile` and the iOS Simulator); the framed part failing to read `parent.document` and `parent.sessionStorage`; a `#share=public` fragment surviving the hop.
- [ ] Item 11 (Cloudflare adapter only): a wildcard CNAME to `<tunnel>.cfargotunnel.com` serves a new `*-part` name. Recorded as "not run: no test zone" and handed to the Cloudflare adapter work (the rest-of-P1 epic).
- [ ] Item 12: WebSocket (`Origin: null` handshake) and SSE under `/c/<cap>/api/` and `/_rt/events`, held 60 s with a 25 s heartbeat, through Caddy (the shipped proxy) and through draft nginx and Traefik configs kept in the rig only (those example configs ship after Slice 1); the proxy settings needed are recorded for each.
- [ ] Item 13: a passkey registered on `parts.` with `rp.id` = the apex, asserted from the wrapper origin: with the virtual authenticator on Chromium (desktop and mobile emulation), and in the iOS Simulator where WebKit allows a software authenticator (otherwise record what the simulator shows, and that the real-device confirmation sits in the human-checks bead). Playwright has no virtual authenticator for WebKit or Firefox, so those lanes record "not assertable in Playwright" rather than a pass. The Telegram in-app webview is approximated by the WebKit lanes and a WKWebView-shaped simulator page; the real Telegram result belongs to the human-checks bead and never blocks this one.
- [ ] The known losses (§2) confirmed per lane: no service workers, no remembered permissions, no persistent IndexedDB, own-host `<a download>` names lost (`?dl=1` instead).
- [ ] `docs/spikes/sandbox.md`: the results table (one row per item per lane, engine and OS versions), each fail with its consequence and fallback, a go/no-go per design choice, the proxy settings from item 12, the date the note was finished (before the part host work starts), and a short "needs real-device confirmation" list that the human-checks bead picks up.

## Plan refs
§5 Maturity check before P0 freezes (spike items 1-13), §2 Serving a part (canonical CSP, `Origin: null`, framed expiry, known losses), §2 The link to post (first-open flow, chrome actions, CORS), §3 Isolation of agent-written JS, §3a Admin (rp.id = apex), §6a Spikes, decisions 10, 25, 36, 52.

## Considerations
- Known risk areas: WebKit blob workers, WebKit tracking prevention on credentialed same-site fetches, WebAuthn in webviews. Fallbacks the plan already names: list the part host explicitly instead of `'self'` (item 1); a wrapper-flow failure reopens the hand-off design; a WebAuthn fail in a webview feeds decision 36 (set Telegram to open links in the normal browser; Hermes hints "open in browser"; the person-bound-link fallback stays rejected).
- Real phones never block anything (decision 52): the iOS Simulator and Playwright's mobile profiles are the gate; the real iPhone, Android and Telegram checks live in the non-blocking human-checks bead, which files any failure as a `bug` bead for the swarm.
- The simulator shares the Mac's network: resolve the rig hosts through `/etc/hosts` on the Mac and trust the rig CA in the simulator keychain, never with certificate-error flags. `simctl openurl` opens Safari; `simctl io <device> screenshot` records the page. Boot one device per iOS runtime that matters (the installed iOS 27 runtime first).
- `/_rt` deliberately has no `Sec-Fetch-Site` check: opaque-origin requests are `cross-site` even to their own host. Item 2 confirms the exact values the part host must accept.
- The no-cap hop must be client-side: the server never sees the fragment.
- The rig is throwaway and stays outside the shipped crates; the part host bead re-implements what it proves, and keeps the item pages as regression fixtures where useful.
- The rig is its own npm package (`tests/sandbox-spike/package.json`, Playwright pinned) and needs nothing from the Cargo workspace, so it starts on day one; its CI `spike` job joins the workspace bead's workflow once that exists (reserve `.gitea/workflows/` and `ci/`). The simulator lane runs only on the Mac (the iOS 27.0 runtime is installed there), so the agent that closes this bead runs on the Mac.

## Tests and logging
- `tests/sandbox-spike/run.sh` / `run.ts` drives items on the five Playwright projects; `wrapper_flow.ts` (virtual authenticator for item 13 on Chromium); `longlived.ts` (WS + SSE for 60 s, logs disconnect reasons); `tests/sandbox-spike/ios-sim.sh` drives the simulator lane and collects its posts and screenshots under `target/sandbox-spike/ios-sim/`.
- Each item page posts `{item, browser, ua, result, detail}` to the collector, which appends `target/sandbox-spike/results.jsonl` (an `event="spike.result" item=<n> lane=<l> outcome=<pass|fail|not_assertable>` line each); a script renders the markdown table from it and fails if any lane × item is missing.

## Verification gate
- `docs/spikes/sandbox.md` merged with a go/no-go for the serving model and the wrapper flow, the results table, the "needs real-device confirmation" list, and a runnable rig (`tests/sandbox-spike/run.sh`, `ios-sim.sh`).
- Observed on every lane: the five Playwright projects (Chromium desktop and mobile emulation, WebKit desktop and mobile, Firefox) and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator each have a result for every item, with engine, OS and runtime versions and screenshots; item 13 has a virtual-authenticator result on Chromium and a recorded simulator result.
