title: P5 Later, only if needed: WASM backends, S3 export upload, semantic search, built-in ACME
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Four independent additions, each built only if it turns out to be needed: WASM component backends as an alternative to containers, an optional S3-compatible upload of scheduled exports, semantic search alongside FTS5, and built-in ACME DNS-01 for hosts with no proxy. Each has its own "done when" and none blocks another.

## Scope
- [ ] WASM component backends: only with an ADR naming a part that containers serve badly; same grant model and routing under `/c/<cap>/api/*`; every §7 Backends line green for the WASM kind.
- [ ] S3-compatible upload of the scheduled export (R2 is one example), behind config, plus `import --from s3://...`, exercised in the drill.
- [ ] Semantic search: embeddings beside FTS5 with hybrid ranking, off by default; FTS5-only behaviour unchanged when disabled.
- [ ] Built-in ACME DNS-01: a wildcard cert via a DNS provider plugin, for hosts with no reverse proxy; renewal before expiry.

## Plan refs
§3e Search ("Later, additive"); §3f (WASM as a later alternative); §5c Layer 3 optional upload; §5f Ingress + TLS and Backups rows; §6 P5; §6a P5; §9 Non-goals (WASM backends in v1).

## Considerations
- WASM backends are a v1 non-goal; the ADR rule stops speculative work. Escape attempts, LAN reachability, identity-header forgery and write-only secrets must all hold for the WASM kind.
- S3 stays an upload of a finished export file: a sink outbox on the save path, Litestream (v0.5 has no age encryption) and R2 as a built-in were rejected (`docs/plan-history.md`). Encrypt with age off-site; recommended default: refuse to upload an unencrypted full export unless an `[unsafe]` key allows it. No save ever waits on the bucket.
- Semantic search: `part_find` over 10k parts is under 5 ms p99 with FTS5; measure and record what hybrid costs, keep the FTS-only path as fast. The embedding index is a new growing store: it needs a cap and a retention-test row, or `doctor` fails.
- ACME is an adapter, never required; the default stays a reverse proxy. A failed renewal must never take the site down while the old cert is valid; alert at 14 days left.

## Order inside the phase
Each item on its own, after what it extends: WASM after P2a backends, S3 upload after export and the drill, semantic search after FTS5 search (the rest of P1) and agent notes and `part_find` (the rest of P2), ACME after `provision` and the portability lane (§6a).

## Verification gate
Per item, before closing it:
- Observed on a running build: the item's own "done when" (WASM part served under the cap with the Backends suite green; an export restored with `import --from s3://...` in the drill; hybrid beating FTS5 on the labelled query set; the portability lane passing with no proxy in front).
- CI green on `main` with the item's tests in the e2e or portability job.
- Logs checked: at least one asserted log line or metric per item (e.g. the upload's `event="export.uploaded"`, the cert expiry gauge).
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run id, gate output; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An ADR names a part that containers serve badly; a WASM component serves it behind `/c/<cap>/api/*` with the §7 Backends lines green
- [ ] Behind config; an export lands in a test bucket and `import --from s3://...` restores it
- [ ] Hybrid ranking beats FTS5 alone on a labelled query set; FTS5-only behaviour is unchanged when disabled
- [ ] The portability lane passes with no proxy in front; the cert renews before expiry in a test with a short-lived ACME staging cert; a failed renewal never takes the site down while the old cert is valid, and an alert fires at 14 days left
- [ ] Any new growing store an item adds (the embedding index, upload state) has a cap and a fill-past-cap retention-test row.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build, per item: its own "done when" holds (WASM part served under the cap; S3 restore in the drill; hybrid beats FTS5 on the labelled set; portability lane with no proxy).
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with each item's tests in the e2e or portability job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: at least one asserted log line or metric per item.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, gate output) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.

title: MCP, discovery, /skill.md and cross-surface conformance
description:
## Goal
An agent told only `https://parts.<domain>` finds and uses everything, on any surface. MCP is one of four front ends, all generated from the one registry, and `docs/agent-contract.md` is the single guide: the MCP `instructions`, the body of `/skill.md`, the top of `/llms-full.txt` and the OpenAPI `info.description`. One conformance scenario then proves MCP, HTTP, the CLI and the skill file behave identically with device-code and personal tokens (definition of done items 3 and 7), and that no agent token can make a public link on any surface (item 4).

## Scope
- [ ] MCP at `POST /mcp` on the workspace listener: `rmcp` (version pinned exactly from the rmcp spike), Streamable HTTP, stateless (spec 2026-07-28, compatible with 2025-11-25: `server/discover`, `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name`; no session id needed); `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/*`.
- [ ] Tools generated from the registry: name, description, `inputSchema`, object-rooted `outputSchema` (non-objects wrapped), annotations from hints; `structuredContent` + a one-line text rendering; errors as `isError: true` with the catalogue JSON; `unknown_field` with "did you mean".
- [ ] `ImageOutput` fields render as an image content block (PNG <= 1 MB, downscaled): `part_check`'s screenshot, asserted against the real renderer.
- [ ] Auth: the bearer middleware from agent connections; failures are HTTP 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` + a JSON body naming the ways to get a token (device code, personal token), never a tool result; scope errors are `forbidden {scope_needed}` results. PATs and device-code access tokens both work.
- [ ] `instructions` = the contract embedded at build time; `part://<name>` resources as projections of `part_get` (`part://recent` waits for `part_find`); `<untrusted_content>` wrapping when `contains_untrusted: true`.
- [ ] Discovery: Markdown `GET /` (`Vary: Accept`), `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` (the contract, then every op's description, schema summary and examples), `/.well-known/mcp/server.json` (served, not published), `/agents.md`, `/skill.md` (frontmatter `name: partifactory` and a triggering `description`, body = the contract), the OpenAPI `info.description` = the contract, `part skill install [--claude | --codex | --path]`. No spaces, parts or people in any of them; no A2A card.
- [ ] The op-section regeneration test (generator owns each section's field table and `Errors:` line; examples parsed against the schema) and the GPT Actions lint (every op has an `operationId`, descriptions ≤ 300 chars with `x-pf-description` for the rest, ≤ 30 operations).
- [ ] Conformance: `tests/agent_surfaces/scenario.yaml` over the Slice 1 ops (create → get the link → edit with a stale base (auto-rebase) → a conflicting edit (`anchor_not_found` with a hint) → `part_link_for` → `part_data set` → `part_check` → restore v1), inputs taken from the contract's examples, run by four drivers (rmcp client, a client generated from `/openapi.json`, the CLI with `--json`, commands extracted from `/skill.md` and `/llms-full.txt`) x device code and PAT; normalised results, errors and audit rows identical; the suite also validates `/openapi.json`, runs the GPT Actions lint and fetches every discovery URL.
- [ ] Outward-sharing refusal: with a full-scope token, every op and every `/api` and `/mcp` route is tried and none creates a public link, a `link:` grant or any request row (§7 Agents).

## Plan refs
§4b One operation registry, Adapters, the shared guide, Discovery, Auth for each kind of client, Errors, Conformance; §3b auth failures are 401, Agent sharing (outward never); §3c resources, prompt-injection hygiene; §4c `part_check` image block; §5 rmcp; §7 Agents; decisions 11, 38; Slice 1 definition of done 3, 4, 7; agent contract Discovery, Connecting, MCP.

## Considerations
- No operation depends on an MCP-only feature (no sampling, elicitation or notifications); instructions and resources add nothing the registry lacks. Every adapter iterates the registry, so a divergence is an adapter bug the suite must catch.
- The HTTP 401 is load-bearing: it is what triggers a client's OAuth flow once authorization code lands after Slice 1. Until then Claude Code and other MCP clients use a personal token as a static header (`claude mcp add --transport http partifactory https://parts.<domain>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $PARTIFACTORY_TOKEN"`).
- `server.json` is served, not published: the public MCP registry doesn't support private servers.
- `/mcp` registers its row in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead), keyed on the principal; the rmcp version is pinned exactly from the rmcp spike note.
- Lines moved here because they need real connections: the screenshot URL is per connection, and no agent token can make a public link on any surface. The admin-side public-link lines (session only, fresh step-up, non-admin 403) are the public links bead's.
- The token-service lines (refresh reuse, part-host and `/oauth/*` rejection, metadata validation, `/api` 401s) are the agent connections bead's; this bead checks only their `/mcp` side.
- `update` on `part_edit` and `advisories` on `part_get` are not in Slice 1; the contract gains both in the change that ships them.

## Tests and logging
- MCP: `tools_list_snapshot.rs`, `error_mapping.rs`, `stateless.rs`, `part_check_image_block_real.rs`, `auth_http_401.rs`, `instructions_equal_skill.rs`, `resources_projection.rs`, `untrusted_wrapper.rs`, `screenshot_per_connection.rs`, `mcp_pixel_smoke.rs`.
- Discovery: `contract_sections.rs`, `discovery.rs`, `skill_install.rs`, `tests/agent_surfaces/blind_agent.rs`; CI job `gpt-actions-lint`; an optional non-gating nightly small-model run.
- Conformance: `tests/agent_surfaces/run.rs` (four drivers), `normalise.rs`, `coverage.rs`, `no_outward_share.rs`; per run `target/e2e-logs/conformance/<driver>-<auth>.jsonl`, diff printed on failure.
- Logs asserted: `surface="mcp" op=... outcome=...` with `request_id`, `event="auth.reject" surface="mcp"`, no content or token canaries.

## Verification gate
- In the e2e harness against the binary from `main`, a real MCP client (`claude mcp add` with a personal token, or the rmcp test client) connects to `https://parts.pf.test/mcp` and runs create -> `part_check` (image block returned) -> edit -> `part_data list`; a missing token gets HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`.
- `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://parts.pf.test/` and `/skill.md` are served; the regenerated contract sections show no diff.
- The conformance suite passes with 4 drivers x device code and PAT; a deliberate divergence fails with a readable diff.
- CI green on `main` with the MCP, discovery and conformance tests in the nextest and e2e harness jobs, plus `gpt-actions-lint`.
- Logs: the run asserts `surface="mcp"` op lines and `event="auth.reject"`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Close with evidence: SHAs, CI run id, the MCP client transcript excerpt and client version.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An MCP client connects with a bearer token (a PAT, or a device-grant access token) and works with no session id; `server/discover` answers; a 2025-11-25 client's `initialize` works.
- [ ] `tools/list` is derived from the registry; its schemas byte-equal the snapshots and the annotations match each op's hints.
- [ ] Errors are `isError` results with the catalogue JSON as `structuredContent`; the error mapping covers every catalogue code (table test).
- [ ] A bad, missing or revoked token on `/mcp` gets HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` and the JSON body, never a tool result; a scope error is a `forbidden {scope_needed}` result.
- [ ] A PAT works on `/mcp` with the same scopes and decisions as on `/api` and as a device-code token; revoking it takes effect on the next `/mcp` call.
- [ ] An op output with an `ImageOutput` field renders as an MCP image block (fake renderer), and a real `part_check` against the running sidecar returns its screenshot as an image content block (PNG, <= 1 MB, downscaled) with the rest as `structuredContent`.
- [ ] The screenshot URL returns 200 for the owner connection within 10 minutes, 404 for any other connection's token, and 404 after 10 minutes.
- [ ] `instructions` byte-equal the served `/skill.md` body; resource reads equal the corresponding op outputs; untrusted content is wrapped in `<untrusted_content>` in text output.
- [ ] `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://parts.<domain>/` returns Markdown with `Vary: Accept`; a browser gets HTML; `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/.well-known/mcp/server.json` and `/agents.md` are served, and `/llms-full.txt` and the OpenAPI `info.description` start with the contract.
- [ ] `/skill.md` body byte-equals the contract (modulo the domain substitution rule) and documents only the Slice 1 ops; `part_edit {update}` and `part_get` `advisories` are absent (unknown fields rejected) until the advisories work ships with its contract sections.
- [ ] `part skill install --claude` writes `~/.claude/skills/partifactory/SKILL.md` and `--codex` appends the `/agents.md` snippet to `AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Grep of every discovery response for fixture part names, space slugs and usernames finds none.
- [ ] A test regenerates each op section's owned lines (the field table and the `Errors:` line, from its `<!-- pf:op <name> -->` marker to the next marker or `## ` heading) and fails if `docs/agent-contract.md` or `/skill.md` differs, and parses each example against the op's input schema; changing a field's description in Rust without updating the contract fails CI.
- [ ] A scripted agent given only the workspace URL and a PAT creates and edits a part through discovery.
- [ ] Normalised results, errors and audit rows are identical across the four drivers and both auth kinds (device code and PAT); 4 × 2 green in CI; a deliberate divergence (e.g. an adapter renaming an error code) fails with a readable diff.
- [ ] Adding a new op without scenario coverage fails a coverage check.
- [ ] With a full-scope token, no op and no `/api` or `/mcp` route on any surface creates a public link, a `link:` grant or a request row.
- [ ] The contract's hand-written parts are checked as well: the scope table against each op's `SCOPE`, the error table (code, HTTP status and the §4b CLI exit code) against the `OpError` catalogue, and every example output (`→ {…}`) against its op's output schema; Rule 5 and "After Slice 1" name only actions and fields that are really absent in Slice 1.
- [ ] GATE: In the e2e harness on the binary from `main`, a real MCP client (`claude mcp add` with a personal token, or the rmcp test client) connects to `https://parts.pf.test/mcp` and runs create -> `part_check` (image block returned) -> edit -> `part_data list`; a request without a token gets HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` and the JSON body.
- [ ] GATE: `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://parts.pf.test/` and `/skill.md` are served from the running server, and the contract regeneration test shows no diff.
- [ ] GATE: The conformance suite passes with 4 drivers x device code and PAT, and a deliberate divergence fails with a readable diff.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the MCP, discovery and conformance tests in the nextest and e2e harness jobs, plus `gpt-actions-lint`.
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `surface="mcp"` op log lines and `event="auth.reject" surface="mcp"`.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, every earlier bead's gate tests included, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence: commit SHAs, CI run id, MCP client transcript excerpt and client version; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.

comments.text:
From spike pf-twz8 (docs/spikes/mcp.md, spikes/spike-mcp): rmcp is a GO, all 8 checks pass, and Claude Code 2.1.310 and the rmcp client both list and call the tools. What this bead must do:
(1) Pin rmcp =3.7.0 with features server + transport-streamable-http-server; macros aren't needed. rmcp shipped 3.3 to 3.7 in six weeks with stateless behaviour changes, so let the conformance suite gate every bump.
(2) Implement ServerHandler by hand over the pf-ops registry (list_tools, call_tool, list_resources, read_resource), with no #[tool_router]. Pattern: entry::<O>() in spikes/spike-mcp/src/lib.rs. Schemas come from rmcp::handler::server::common::{schema_for_input, schema_for_output}.
(3) StreamableHttpServerConfig: legacy_session_mode(false), json_response(true), sse_keep_alive(None), allowed_hosts = the parts host (the default is loopback only and would reject production), plus enforce origin validation. Leave stateless_protocol_metadata_required off, or 2025-11-25 clients break. Advertise [2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18]. A 2025-11-25 initialize gets no Mcp-Session-Id.
(4) Auth is axum middleware in front of nest_service("/mcp"): it returns 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=... + a JSON body, and inserts the Principal into the request extensions. call_tool reads it via ctx.extensions.get::<http::request::Parts>().extensions.
(5) Errors: CallToolResult::error(one text line), then set structured_content = {error:{...}}. Don't use structured_error, because it dumps the JSON into the text. Serde unknown-field errors go in band as unknown_field.
(6) Wrap non-object outputs as {"result": ...}. rmcp 3.7 no longer requires an object root (SEP-2106), but 2025-11-25 clients need an object structuredContent.
(7) Strip schemars' non-standard format values (uint64/uint32): Claude Code warns 'unknown format uint64 ignored'.
(8) Image blocks work: a 661 KB PNG reached Claude Code. Keep the 1 MB cap.
(9) Test clients need reqwest 0.13, not 0.12.
Port the 5 tests in spikes/spike-mcp/tests/mcp.rs into the conformance suite.

title: tsx kind and the rest of P0: oxc + rolldown, the library set, svg and code kinds, the compat corpus, the regression bench
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Finish P0 right after Slice 1: make Claude-written React/TSX run unchanged (oxc transform + rolldown bundle in the build child, one shared library set, import maps frozen per build), add the `svg` and `code` kinds, rebuild live parts in the background on a toolchain upgrade without ever switching what's live, keep a sandbox compat corpus in CI, and ship the same-machine regression bench. Closing it meets P0's "Done when".

## Scope
- [ ] `tsx` kind: `App.tsx`/`.jsx` default export, oxc (umbrella crate, `transformer` feature) + rolldown with in-memory inputs inside the build child, generated `#root` shell with the prelude inserted at serve time, errors as `{file, line, col, message}`, compile perf logging. esbuild-as-subprocess fallback behind the same child protocol.
- [ ] Library set `libset.toml` (`library_set_version` in the build cache key): react and react-dom 18.3, lucide-react, recharts, d3, lodash, papaparse, mathjs, three, chart.js, tone, plotly.js, xlsx (shartifacts' compatibility matrix, credited in `NOTICE`), seeded as shared blobs (`source = 'seed'`); CDN-URL aliasing to the set for the same major; `duplicate_library` warning otherwise.
- [ ] Frozen `import_map` in the build manifest, merged with the cap-prefix entries at serve time (author entries win except `/` and `/c/`); `part_edit {rebuild: true}` opts a part into the current set.
- [ ] Golden compile corpus `tests/golden/tsx/` (compat matrix + Claude samples) with a runner, and `tests/e2e/tsx_corpus.spec.ts` on Chromium and WebKit.
- [ ] `svg` kind (served as a sandboxed document with the canonical CSP; build work none beyond brotli) and `code` kind (syntect highlight into a read-only viewer shell with `#L<n>` anchors); bin codes `SVG`, `CODE`; golden `tests/golden/render/{svg,code}/`.
- [ ] Toolchain upgrade: on a new `toolchain_version` rebuild every live part in the background at low priority (a `library_set_version` bump only parts whose frozen map would change), never switch `live`; `partifactory toolchain report --json`, `pf_toolchain_rebuild_total{outcome}`, a `kv` summary Health reads.
- [ ] Sandbox compat corpus `tests/golden/sandbox-corpus/`: 30 Claude-written artifacts + 10 Vite builds rendered under the sandbox on Chromium and WebKit, explicit per-sample expected-failure lists.
- [ ] Same-machine regression bench: `partifactory bench` (blob warm p99, 304, entry document, shared blob, cap verify, `/grant`, small `part_edit`), results JSON, `--compare` fails on > 10 % regression; feeds the nginx/HAProxy comparison in the rest of P1.
- [ ] Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `tsx`, `svg` and `code` (kind enum, kinds table rows, `duplicate_library` and `cdn_unpinned` warnings) and drops them from "After Slice 1", in the same change; the `/skill.md` regeneration test stays green.

## Plan refs
§2 Kinds, Mirror-on-build (One library set, Import maps), Part version (Why build records); §3d The build worker; §5 Stack (TSX/JSX, Tests row: sandbox compat corpus); §5a Performance; §6 P0; §6a Right after Slice 1; decisions 20, 39.

## Considerations
- Pin oxc and rolldown exactly and vendor them: oxc is 0.x with breaking releases, and rolldown's semver promise covers its JS API, not the Rust crate. Renovate never automerges them. The Slice 1 compiler spike note decides the details and the fallback.
- The `FROM scratch` image has no esbuild; the fallback is dev/CI only unless the release image deliberately ships it (say which).
- Frozen import maps are the reproducibility guarantee: a server upgrade must never change which React an old part loads. Toolchain rebuilds only create build records; a person or agent opts in with `rebuild: true`.
- An SVG can carry `<script>`; it is safe only under the canonical sandbox CSP. Part SVGs are part blobs, never in `shared_blobs`. The prelude is injected into HTML only, so don't expect `blocked_load` rows from an SVG. External SVG references are CSP-blocked, not mirrored.
- syntect runs server-side so the viewer needs no JS; its syntax set version is part of `toolchain_version`.
- Bench numbers are tracked, not gated, on shared CI runners; release gates compare against the previous release on the same machine. The blob scenario asserts zero DB queries (reuse the content hot path's query counter).
- Toolchain-upgrade results go to the CLI and metrics; Health reads the `kv` summary.
- P0's other spike, the Authentik adapter spike, is not here: it sits with the Authentik adapter in the rest of P1, next to the adapter it decides, and P0's "Done when" doesn't need it.

## Order inside the phase
tsx compiler in the child → library set and aliasing → frozen import maps + golden corpus + contract; svg/code and the compat corpus in parallel; the toolchain-upgrade rebuild after the corpus; the bench beside them. Tailwind and shadcn (P3) wait for `tsx`.

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build in the e2e harness: `part put x.html --name packing` opens at `packing-part.pf.test/c/<cap>/` under the canonical CSP, a Claude-written page using `localStorage` and a CDN `<script>` runs unchanged, an `App.tsx` part renders, and the TSX and sandbox corpora pass on Chromium and WebKit.
- Each child bead's own gate observed, CI green on `main` with the golden and corpus jobs; logs checked: `event="build.finished" kind="tsx"`, `event="serve.entry"`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, `communal_pixel_editor` included, still passes.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run ids, corpus reports, bench JSON; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] P0 "Done when": `part put x.html --name packing` opens at `packing-part.localhost:8081/c/<cap>/` under the sandbox; a Claude-written page using `localStorage` and a CDN `<script>` runs unchanged; the TSX corpus compiles.
- [ ] A 50-line `App.tsx` with a default export builds to an ESM bundle + shell and renders in the sandbox e2e harness.
- [ ] A syntax error yields `build.status: failed` with `{file, line, col, message}` pointing at the source line; `live` unchanged.
- [ ] Compile + bundle p50 < 150 ms on the bench fixture (logged, tracked).
- [ ] A page importing React from a cdnjs URL and bare `react` loads **one** React (one network request to the shared blob, no duplicate module in the bundle).
- [ ] A different React major is mirrored as is and the build carries `duplicate_library`.
- [ ] Changing `libset.toml` changes `library_set_version` and therefore the cache key (golden).
- [ ] A library upgrade (new `libset.toml`) leaves every old build's import map byte-identical; a `rebuild: true` picks up the new one.
- [ ] The golden tsx corpus (compat matrix + Claude samples) compiles, and `tests/e2e/tsx_corpus.spec.ts` passes on Chromium and WebKit.
- [ ] Golden render corpus passes for `svg` and `code`; an SVG carrying a script runs only under the canonical sandbox CSP; `code` keeps stable `#L<n>` anchors.
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` gains `tsx`, `svg` and `code` (kind enum, kinds table rows, `duplicate_library` and `cdn_unpinned` warnings) and drops them from "After Slice 1", in the change that ships each; the `/skill.md` regeneration test stays green.
- [ ] After bumping the toolchain id, live parts get new build records with `live` unchanged; `partifactory toolchain report --json` and Health list the differing parts, and `pf_toolchain_rebuild_total{outcome}` counts the rebuilds.
- [ ] `part_edit {rebuild: true}` moves that part's live to the new build.
- [ ] Sandbox compat corpus: 40 samples (30 Claude-written artifacts + 10 Vite builds) render with zero uncaught errors (beyond each sample's listed expected failures) on Chromium and WebKit in CI on every PR.
- [ ] A deliberately broken prelude (e.g. no `localStorage` shim) fails the sandbox-corpus job.
- [ ] `partifactory bench` writes a results JSON; a >10 % regression on the fixture fails the bench job; the blob scenario makes zero DB queries.
- [ ] oxc and rolldown are pinned to exact versions with vendored sources, and Renovate never automerges them.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build in the e2e harness: the P0 demo (`part put` an HTML page with `localStorage` and a CDN `<script>`, open it under the canonical CSP) works unchanged, an `App.tsx` part renders, and the TSX and sandbox corpora pass on Chromium and WebKit.
- [ ] GATE: Every bead this epic is broken into is closed with its own observed gate.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the golden tsx, render and sandbox-corpus jobs and the bench job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the corpus runs assert `event="build.finished" kind="tsx" outcome="ok"` and `event="serve.entry"` per sample.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, `communal_pixel_editor` included, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run ids, corpus reports and bench JSON in `br close --reason`, with `ci_green` and `verified` reported.

title: P3 Claude compatibility: claude.use, Tailwind and shadcn, viewer uploads, the agent inbox
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Make anything Claude writes run here unchanged: `claude.use("db" | "user" | "comments" | "artifact")` in the prelude (including pages that save themselves), Tailwind and shadcn for Claude-written parts, viewer uploads, and an agent inbox so a comment addressed to the agent reaches the right one. The spec is shartifacts' compatibility matrix (credited).

## Scope
- [ ] `claude.use("db")` and the `/_rt` `db.*` ops over `data_docs` (collection ≠ `__storage`), with per-document `rev` compare-and-set and data leases (`data_leases`), exactly like Claude's `db`.
- [ ] `claude.use("user")` (the viewer only; guests answered locally as "Guest 4f2a" with no network call) and `claude.use("comments")` for page code, with `provenance`.
- [ ] `claude.use("artifact").publish(...)`: self-publish with compare-and-set against the running version, which must be head and live; `via = self_publish`; idempotent by `request_id`.
- [ ] Tailwind + shadcn: a spike measures prebuilt utility CSS vs the mirrored Tailwind v4 browser build vs build-time class extraction on a corpus, writes `docs/decisions/tailwind.md`, then the chosen mechanism ships; shadcn joins `libset.toml`; `cdn.tailwindcss.com` script tags alias with a `cdn_aliased` warning; goldens and reference screenshots.
- [ ] Viewer uploads: `assets.put` over `/_rt` (25 MiB each, capped before auth, counted against the space quota), served at `/_a/<id>` behind the cap, listed and deletable by agents via `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`, an `asset.added` event.
- [ ] Agent upload URLs: `part_create`/`part_edit {upload: [...]}` returns 10-minute URLs bound to the connection; `{path: {blob: sha256}}` wiring; the Slice 1 rejection of `upload` removed.
- [ ] Agent inbox and steward: `part_inbox` op, `to_agent` routing to the steward, states `open -> claimed -> answered -> resolved`, "stalled" after 15 minutes with no new version, runtime-error spikes as inbox items; the steward changeable in the share sheet.
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` sections for every new op and field, in the same change.

## Plan refs
§1 (Claude-artifact compatibility), §2 Runtime calls `/_rt`, §3a role x runtime matrix and guests, §3c In place (persistent state, self-editing parts, assets, agent inbox), §3d Data CAS + leases, §4 ops (`part_data`, `part_inbox`), §4b shared guide, §5e `data_docs`, `data_leases`, `assets`, §6 P3, §6a P3.

## Considerations
- One storage model: a `claude.use("db")` document is the same `data_docs` row `part_data {collection, doc_id}` reads. No second store. `db.*` was settled here, not in Slice 1 (`window.storage` is the Slice 1 data API).
- Guests are web consumers only: a guest cap calling any non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) gets 403. Don't invent a `partifactory.user()`.
- Self-publish is CAS, not rebase: a page publishing itself has no anchors, so a stale publish is refused and handed the newer version.
- Tailwind options fail differently: (a) prebuilt CSS is huge and can't do arbitrary values; (b) the browser JIT works with runtime class names but costs JS on phones; (c) build-time extraction is smallest but misses runtime classes and must fit the build child's 10 s budget with no network. A stated hybrid is fine. Any generator is pinned and vendored, like oxc and rolldown; Tailwind and shadcn (MIT) go in `NOTICE`.
- `storage_full` at 95 % of the disk budget refuses `/_rt` writes, never reads or deletes. Failures reject with `PfError` using catalogue codes.
- Asset names are untrusted (provenance-labelled); assets belong to the part's data, survive edits and are in exports. Assets are a new growing store: add it to the retention registry and the fill-past-cap test.
- The inbox is work addressed to an agent, never something waiting on a person (decision 34). A revoked steward connection falls back to "no steward", shown. Recommended spike threshold: a new error fingerprint seen 3 times in 10 minutes.

## Order inside the phase
`claude.use` after shared data, comments and `/grant`; Tailwind and shadcn after `tsx`; viewer uploads; the agent inbox after comments and the event log (§6a).

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build in the harness: a page copied from a claude.ai artifact (using `claude.use("db")`, state persistence and self-publish) runs unchanged on chromium-desktop and webkit-mobile; a viewer's photo upload reaches the agent's inbox and `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`.
- CI green on `main` with the P3 specs in the e2e job, the Tailwind corpus goldens, and the conformance scenario extended to the new ops on all four drivers.
- Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="rt" op="db.set"`, `event="asset.added"` and the self-publish `outcome` lines.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command output, screenshot paths; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The decision note has every measurement for all three options and a decision line.
- [ ] Corpus pages using Tailwind utilities and shadcn `Button`/`Card` match the reference screenshots within the threshold; a `cdn.tailwindcss.com` HTML part renders with `cdn_aliased`.
- [ ] A `claude.use("db")` document is the same row `part_data {collection, doc_id}` reads.
- [ ] A poll part works for every viewer while `shared_data_writers: viewers`.
- [ ] CAS conflict returns `if_match_failed` with `current_rev`; lease held by another holder is reported, then acquirable after expiry.
- [ ] Guests write only via Can contribute links and within limits; Can-view never writes.
- [ ] Signed-in viewer gets their identity from `claude.use("user")`; guest gets "Guest xxxx" with no network call (asserted via request log).
- [ ] `comment`-role viewer can add a comment from page code; `view` can't (`forbidden`); guest gets 403.
- [ ] A guest cap calling any non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) gets 403; `claude.use("user")` for a guest is answered locally.
- [ ] Comments added from page code carry `provenance: person` (or `link_viewer` for opted-in link viewers).
- [ ] Self-publish with a stale version is refused with the newer version.
- [ ] An `edit` viewer's publish creates v(n+1) with `via = self_publish`; a `view` viewer gets 403.
- [ ] A retried publish with the same `request_id` returns `replayed: true`.
- [ ] A `comment`-role viewer uploads a photo from a part; a `view` viewer and a guest get 403; 25 MiB + 1 → 413 before auth.
- [ ] The agent lists the upload via `part_data {collection: "_assets"}` with `provenance` and deletes it; `/_a/<id>` needs a valid cap.
- [ ] An MCP agent gets an upload URL, PUTs a PNG, and the next `part_edit` references it by hash; the URL is dead after 10 minutes and for another connection.
- [ ] A comment for the steward appears in its inbox; claiming shows 'Hermes is on it'; no version after 15 min shows 'stalled'; the steward can be changed in the share sheet; a revoked steward connection falls back to "no steward", shown; a runtime-error spike (a new fingerprint seen 3 times in 10 minutes) becomes an inbox item
- [ ] Assets are registered as a capped store and pass the fill-past-cap retention test; `storage_full` refuses `db.*` and `assets.put` writes while reads continue.
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` documents `claude.use`, `upload` and `part_inbox` in the same change that ships them, and the /skill.md regeneration test passes.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build in the harness: a page copied from a claude.ai artifact (with `claude.use("db")`, state persistence and self-publish) runs unchanged on chromium-desktop and webkit-mobile, and a viewer's photo upload reaches the agent's inbox.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the P3 e2e specs, the Tailwind corpus goldens, and the conformance scenario covering the new ops on all four drivers.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts the `db.set`, `asset.added` and self-publish log lines.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, gate output, screenshot paths) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.

title: communal_pixel_editor: the Slice 1 acceptance test, in CI on emulated and simulated devices
description:
## Goal
`communal_pixel_editor` is the Slice 1 acceptance test, and this bead is the Slice 1 exit. The pixel board exercises every risky layer at once (sandbox, caps, builds, agents, guests, live shared data, data rollback), so passing it end to end in CI on every PR, on the simulated device matrix (decision 52), proves the core before anything is built on top. The bead closes when the plan's definition of done holds for everything a machine can observe. The by-hand run on the example deployment and the Telegram passkey test are definition-of-done item 8 ("not in the gate"), so they belong to the non-blocking human-checks bead, and nothing here waits on them.

## Scope
- [ ] Fixture `tests/e2e/fixtures/pixel.ts`: boots the e2e harness (Dex, Caddy, internal-CA wildcard cert for `pf.test`, render sidecar on), seeds Dex users (the admin, one household user), resets `/data`, captures logs to `target/e2e-logs/communal_pixel_editor/`. The board HTML is extracted from `docs/agent-contract.md`'s worked session, and the fixture is that v1 board with the contract's own fix applied (its `part_edit` replacing `loadBoard().finally` with `load().finally`); a test does the extraction and the edit and diffs the result against the fixture, so contract and test can't drift.
- [ ] Agent half (MCP via the rmcp client and HTTP, parametrised): device grant with `client_id=part-cli`, `agent_name="Pixel test agent"`; the admin's Chromium context taps Allow + virtual passkey; `part_create {name:"pixel", kind:"html", live:"after_check"}` in one call; `part_check` with click + `wait_ms` + `eval_return`; `part_data list prefix "px:"` stays empty (the check's overlay is discarded); the agent's posted link equals the `url` field, `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`.
- [ ] Admin half on `chromium-desktop` with a CDP virtual authenticator (`rp.id` = the apex), and again on `chromium-mobile` (phone viewport, bottom sheets): sign in, open the part host (address bar clean, no `#pf=`), Share → Anyone with the link → Can contribute → Copy with in-sheet step-up; later Roll back data (newest snapshot preselected, the `reason: contribute` one) and Freeze; the shared budget helper `tests/e2e/lib/budget.ts` counts clicks, presses and WebAuthn ceremonies. A variant starts from the agent's `part_link_for {action: "contribute"}` link: tap → confirm = 2 (+1 biometric).
- [ ] Guest half signed out on `webkit-mobile` (the definition-of-done profile) and again on `firefox-desktop` and `chromium-mobile` (the rest of the device matrix): open `/l/<token>`, `POST /l/<token>/go` returns a guest cap, tap a cell, the admin tab repaints within 1 s; after Freeze the guest's next write rejects with a `PfError` and the cell reverts. The same guest half runs in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh pixel-guest`: `simctl openurl` the `/l/` link, the page self-reports the paint, the harness asserts the admin tab's repaint, screenshot after Freeze); its output is attached to `verified`.
- [ ] Required CI job on every PR (`ci/e2e.sh` runs the same steps locally), runnable from the published compose file with `_FILE` secrets.
- [ ] The definition-of-done roll-up (items 1–7): every Slice 1 bead closed with evidence, the conformance, security, retention and drill reports attached, and the human-checks bead's items (item 8) listed as "pending the admin, non-blocking".

## Plan refs
"Slice 1: what ships first" (scope, decided for the slice, definition of done); §6 P2 Done when; §3a Can contribute links, UX click budgets; §4a.7 click budgets; §4c `part_check`; `docs/agent-contract.md` worked session; decisions 31, 35–43, 52.

## Considerations
- No browser OAuth flow anywhere: the agent connects by device code (decision 37); approval happens in the admin's Chromium context.
- Live-update latency is measured from the guest's `/_rt` write response to the admin tab's repaint (polling the cell's computed style), with timestamps in the logs. Contexts are coordinated by explicit test barriers, never sleeps; the simulator guest reports through the collector, and the barrier waits on that post.
- Rolling back to the `contribute` snapshot (taken when the link switched) makes the board end empty: a deterministic assertion.
- Passkeys run only where they can be simulated: Chromium's virtual authenticator for the admin, and the iOS Simulator only if the sandbox spike's item 13 found a software authenticator there. Guests never need one.
- Real phones never block anything (decision 52): definition-of-done item 8 (the by-hand run on the example deployment, on the admin's phone and a signed-out phone on mobile data, and the Telegram passkey test) lives in the human-checks bead. A failure there is filed as a `bug` bead for the swarm; it never reopens this one.
- The portability-lane run of this test arrives with the portability lane after Slice 1; the two old lines that require it are verified in the rest-of-P1 epic. The backend variant is P2a.

## Tests and logging
- `tests/e2e/communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts` (projects `chromium-admin`, `chromium-mobile-admin`, `webkit-mobile-guest`, `firefox-guest`, `chromium-mobile-guest`) and `tests/e2e/agents/pixel_agent.rs`; `tests/device/ios-sim.sh pixel-guest`; traces, HAR and screenshots on failure.
- Asserted in order, with the names the owning beads log: `event="op" op="part_create" outcome="ok"`, `event="render.job" purpose="gate" outcome="ok"`, `event="live.switch"`, `event="stepup.verify" outcome="ok"`, `event="link.create"`, `event="link.mode" mode="contribute"`, `event="link.go"`, `event="rt.op" principal="guest:…" op="storage.set" outcome="ok"`, `event="data.changed"`, `event="snapshot.restore" outcome="ok"`, `event="epoch.bump" key="minter:link:…"`, `event="rt.op" principal="guest:…" outcome="stale_epoch|forbidden_view_only"`.

## Verification gate
- Observed in CI on `main`: the whole flow on the harness, agent by device code, admin on Chromium (desktop and mobile emulation) with the virtual authenticator, guest on mobile WebKit, Firefox and mobile Chromium, budgets exact.
- Observed on the Mac: the guest half in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator paints, the admin tab repaints within 1 s, and the post-Freeze write is refused; posts and screenshots attached to `verified`.
- CI green on `main` with `communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts` as a required check in the e2e job; logs checked: the ordered event list above.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, every Slice 1 gate included, passes on the same run.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, the run's `server.jsonl` and budget counts, the simulator lane output, links to the conformance, security, retention and drill reports, and the human-checks bead listed as pending and non-blocking; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Agent: device grant approved by the admin (Allow + virtual passkey); one `part_create` → `head: 1`; `live` moves only after the gate check passes; `part_check` passes with `errors: []`, `blank: false`, and a click + `eval_return` returns the colour while the real data stays empty; the posted link equals `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`.
- [ ] The agent half passes on both the MCP and the HTTP driver.
- [ ] The board fixture equals the contract's worked-session board with the contract's own `part_edit` fix applied, byte for byte (diff test).
- [ ] Admin budgets met exactly on chromium-desktop and chromium-mobile: Can-contribute link 4 interactions + 1 biometric; Freeze 2; Roll back 3; the `#share=contribute` deep-link variant 2 + 1 biometric; a failure prints the recorded interaction list.
- [ ] Guest paint visible in the admin tab within 1 s (p100 over 3 retries) from webkit-mobile, firefox-desktop and chromium-mobile; `part_data list` shows the doc with `provenance: "link_viewer"`.
- [ ] After roll back the board is empty in both tabs; after Freeze the guest's next `storage.set` rejects (`PfError`) on the next request and the cell reverts.
- [ ] DoD 1: `communal_pixel_editor` is a required check and passes in CI on every PR on the e2e harness (Dex and Caddy with an internal-CA wildcard cert for `pf.test`; the admin's sign-in, step-up, share, roll back and freeze on Chromium with the virtual authenticator; the signed-out guest on a mobile WebKit profile): an agent connected by device code creates the board in one `part_create`, runs `part_check`, posts `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`; the admin does Share → Anyone with the link → Can contribute → Copy (4 interactions + 1 biometric); a signed-out browser paints and the admin's open tab shows it within 1 s; the admin rolls back one snapshot and freezes the link, and the guest's next write is refused.
- [ ] DoD 2: the same flow passes on the device matrix: Playwright Chromium (mobile emulation), WebKit (mobile profile) and Firefox in CI, and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator run locally on the Mac with its posts and screenshots attached to `verified`.
- [ ] DoD 3: every acceptance test of the work in Slice 1 passes (they live in its beads), including cross-surface conformance over MCP, HTTP, the CLI and `/skill.md` with device-code and personal tokens.
- [ ] DoD 4: the §7 lines for what exists pass from outside, the guest, agent and render-sidecar lines included; no agent token, scope or op can make a public link (the Shipping bead's security report).
- [ ] DoD 5: export and import round-trip: the nightly export imported into a fresh container brings back every part, version, data document and snapshot, and every cap minted before it is dead.
- [ ] DoD 6: every store that exists is capped and passes its fill-past-cap case; the Health page shows each one, the backup layers and the disk budget; no `[unsafe]` key is set.
- [ ] DoD 7: `/skill.md` is `docs/agent-contract.md`, and the test that regenerates its op reference from the registry passes.
- [ ] DoD 8 is not in the gate: the by-hand run on the example deployment and the Telegram passkey test are listed as pending in the human-checks bead, together with the sandbox spike's "needs real-device confirmation" list; no edge from this bead to it.
- [ ] Every Slice 1 bead is closed with evidence and its `ci_green` and `verified` gates passed.
- [ ] GATE: Observed in CI on `main`: the full pixel flow on the e2e harness (device-code agent, admin on chromium-desktop and chromium-mobile with the virtual authenticator, guest on webkit-mobile, firefox-desktop and chromium-mobile), with exact click budgets.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on the Mac: the guest half from Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh pixel-guest`) paints, the admin tab repaints within 1 s and the post-Freeze write is refused; the posts, screenshots and simulator runtime version are attached to the `verified` report.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with `tests/e2e/communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts` a required check in the e2e job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the spec asserts the ordered events from `event="op" op="part_create" outcome="ok"` through `event="epoch.bump" key="minter:link:…"` and the guest's refused write.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, every Slice 1 gate test included, passes on the same run.
- [ ] GATE: Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, the run's `server.jsonl` and budget counts, the simulator lane output and the conformance, security, retention and drill reports, with the human-checks bead listed as pending and non-blocking, in `br close --reason`, with `ci_green` and `verified` reported.

title: The part host: caps, the content listener, the shared blob host, the prelude and /_rt
description:
## Goal
Serve every part sandboxed in an opaque origin with no cookies, on its own host `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, authorised by a host-bound capability in the path, with blob paths that never touch the database. Also serve the shared blob host and the prelude, partifactory's small runtime that makes Claude-written pages (`localStorage`, `fetch('/x.json')`, workers) run unchanged, plus `/_rt/v1`, its one server endpoint, and the `runtime_errors` loop that tells agents their page is broken. This is the security model and the hot path; the pixel test, retention and conformance all run through it.

## Scope
- [ ] Caps per §2 on the content listener, with the store bead's `pf-caps` crate (`v1.<kid>.<payload>.<mac>`, canonical CBOR payload, ≤ 300 bytes, MAC truncated to 16 bytes, daily HKDF keys accepting `kid` and `kid − 1`, deterministic 12 h windows with the last-hour roll-forward, 60 s for `render`), DB-free verify in the §2 order, `EpochStore` (part, minter, global, boot floor bumped on every start), and `partifactory dev cap <name>` (dev feature) for gates before `/grant` exists.
- [ ] Content listener `:8081`: only `-part` labels (anything else 404 + `pf_nonpart_host_hits_total`); `/c/<cap>/` content with the §2 navigation/subresource re-grant rule (302 to `/grant?mode=direct` or 401 `X-PF-Reauth: 1`), 404 for an unknown `kid` or bad MAC, Origin rules; route slots for the wrapper (`/`, `/_pf/`) and `/l/`.
- [ ] One header set: the canonical CSP on every part document (HTML entry, any navigable HTML file, SVG as a document; `unsandboxed` drops only `sandbox`), `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Robots-Tag`, `nosniff`, ACAO `null` + `Vary: Origin` for `Origin: null`, never ACAC/CORP/`Set-Cookie`; part blobs `private, immutable`; `?dl=1` → `Content-Disposition: attachment`.
- [ ] Serve-time entry: prelude tag first in `<head>`, cap-prefixed import map (`"/": "/c/<cap>/", "/c/": "/c/"`), `pf-boot` (≤ 256 KiB of the person's `__storage` personal docs, one indexed read cached per cap and invalidated on personal writes; empty for link/render/guest), and the current `pf-shell.css` link in the built-in shell; the same prelude tag on every other HTML file; on-the-fly compression.
- [ ] Hot path: live and build-manifest caches invalidated from the build events broadcast (`part.live_changed`, from the builds bead), ETag/304, brotli variants, mmap LRU, a test query counter.
- [ ] Shared blob host `blobs-part`: only hashes with a `shared_blobs` row, `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, ACAO `*`, never `Set-Cookie`; seeds the prelude into `shared_blobs` at start (mirrored libraries and `pf-shell.css` come from the builds bead, the wrapper bundle from the wrapper bead).
- [ ] Prelude (≤ 12 KiB brotli): synced `localStorage` shim seeded from `pf-boot` with debounced write-behind and a `pagehide` CORS `fetch` keepalive flush, memory `sessionStorage`, inert `document.cookie`, `indexedDB`/`caches` `undefined`, `fetch`/XHR/`EventSource` URL prefixing, `Worker`/`SharedWorker` from `blob:` URLs, `crossOrigin = "anonymous"` on script-created `Image`s, `window.partifactory` (`ready()`, `basePath`; `on` is added by the shared data bead), `pf:regrant`; the message schema in `crates/pf-prelude/PROTOCOL.md`.
- [ ] `/_rt/v1` (`POST`, `Content-Type: text/plain` JSON `{op, args}`, no preflight): `Origin: null` (or the part's own origin when `unsandboxed`) only, any other non-null `Origin` → 403 before the body is read, `Sec-Fetch-Mode` must be `cors` when present, no `Sec-Fetch-Site` check; role checks from cap claims; the op dispatch the shared data bead extends; personal `storage.get/set/delete` behind the `localStorage` shim (collection `__storage`, key rules, the 256 KiB personal cap); `refresh`; `errors.report` → `runtime_errors` by fingerprint (`kind`, `count`, URLs stored without the cap), ≤ 10 inserts/min/part, 1,000 per part.

## Plan refs
§2 Serving a part (canonical CSP, capabilities, errors on the part host, framed expiry, leaked URLs, runtime calls, entry templating, the prelude, known losses, unsandboxed, why one hostname per part); §2 The core idea (shared vs part blobs); §2 The link to post (DB reads under `/c/`); §3 Topology; §3a role × runtime matrix (personal state column); §3c errors close the loop; §3h layer 1; §5a lean hot path; §5e `epochs`, `shared_blobs`, `runtime_errors`, hot-path rules; §7 Part hosts, Caching and blobs; decision 10.

## Considerations
- Starts only after the sandbox spike's go/no-go: read `docs/spikes/sandbox.md` first. Items 1 (`'self'` in a sandboxed document; hence `frame-ancestors` spells the host out), 2 (the exact `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-*` values to accept), 4 (`defineProperty` on `localStorage` before page scripts), 5 (WebKit blob workers), 9 (CSP from the header) and 10/12 decide details.
- `'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` are deliberate: CSP here is an egress policy; the opaque origin protects the viewer. Never add `allow-same-origin`.
- Bad MAC → 404 so caps are not an existence oracle. Verify checks `e ≥ epoch[part]`, `me ≥ epoch[minter]`, `b ≥ boot_floor` and the global epoch. Constant-time MAC compare. The cap string never reaches a log (redaction by route and pattern, from the observability bead).
- The only DB read under `/c/` is the entry's `pf-boot`. The response never depends on the User-Agent.
- `refresh` for `user:` subjects re-checks access with fixture users until the policy engine lands in the identity bead, then calls its decision API.
- The wrapper side of `pf:regrant` (the framed-expiry flow) is verified in the wrapper bead.
- `pf-caps` (format, keys, `EpochStore`, mint and verify, its property tests) is the store bead's, so this bead and the identity bead share one crate with no race; this bead owns the listener side: the 404-oracle behaviour, the zero-query check under `/c/`, `partifactory dev cap` and the re-grant rule.
- `/_rt/v1` here is the endpoint, its auth rules, personal storage, `refresh` and `errors.report`. `window.storage` (shared scope, `getMany`, `list` paging, the full §3a limit set with `PfError`) and `/_rt/events` are the shared data bead, which builds on this dispatch rather than adding a second one.
- `/_rt/v1` reads and writes register their rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead) instead of hand-rolling one; the guest and per-IP numbers come from the public-links bead.
- The browser-level kind and mirror checks live here because they need a served page: `kinds_render.spec.ts` renders what the builds bead built, and `mirror_zero_third_party.spec.ts` uses the builds bead's fake CDN.
- The sandbox and prelude specs also run in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh`, a local lane whose posts and screenshots are attached to `verified`). Real phones never block anything.

## Tests and logging
- Property tests in `pf_caps` (host-bound, deterministic, last-hour roll-forward, epoch rejection, tamper, kid rotation); `pf_serve` unit tests; integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/{regrant,headers_all_routes,entry_template,prelude_no_rebuild,hot_path,blob_host,rt_personal,rt_errors}.rs`; benches `cap_verify`, `serve_blob`.
- E2E (`chromium-desktop`, `webkit-mobile`, `firefox-desktop`): `tests/e2e/{content_listener_sandbox,prelude_storage,prelude_network,runtime_errors,kinds_render,mirror_zero_third_party}.spec.ts`.
- Logs: `event="cap.verify" outcome=…` (`ok`, `expired`, `stale_epoch`, `bad_mac`, `wrong_host`), `event="serve.entry"`, `event="blobhost.serve"`, `event="rt.op" op=… outcome=…`, `event="runtime_error.recorded" kind=…`; no line contains a cap.

## Verification gate
- Observed on the binary built from `main` in the e2e harness: parts made with `partifactory dev put` and a cap from `partifactory dev cap`; `curl -si https://<name>-part.pf.test/c/<cap>/` → 200 with the canonical CSP and no `Set-Cookie`; with an expired cap and `Accept: text/html` → 302 to `/grant?mode=direct`, without → 401 `X-PF-Reauth: 1`; `curl -si https://blobs-part.pf.test/b/<prelude-hash>` → 200 `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- Playwright on `chromium-desktop`, `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop` renders an html, a markdown and a text part and a vite `files` bundle; a CDN fixture page's network log contains only the part host and `blobs-part`; a `localStorage` page keeps state across reload and a second browser for the same fixture user; the HAR has zero `OPTIONS` requests; a throwing page creates a `runtime_errors` row.
- CI green on `main`: nextest job (`ci/test.sh`) and the `e2e` harness job with the specs above.
- Logs: the e2e server JSONL shows `event="serve.entry"` and `event="cap.verify" outcome="expired"` and no cap substring anywhere.
- Simulator lane (evidence, not a CI check): the `content_listener_sandbox` and `prelude_storage` self-reporting pages pass in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator; posts and screenshots attached to `verified`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test still pass. Evidence on close (SHAs, CI run id, curl excerpts, browser versions) and `br gate report` for `ci_green` and `verified`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Property test: a cap for part A never verifies on host B; the same subject, part, epochs and window give the same cap; a cap minted in a window's last hour uses the next window; bumping a part, minter, global or boot epoch rejects older caps; a rotated key verifies for 25 h then fails; a cap is ≤ 300 bytes.
- [ ] Unknown `kid` or bad MAC → 404 byte-identical to a nonexistent part; editing any payload byte breaks the MAC; changing `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY` invalidates every outstanding cap; cap verify makes zero DB queries (query counter).
- [ ] A cap for part A presented on host B never serves content (re-grant path for a navigation, 401 for a subresource); a non-`-part` host → 404 and `pf_nonpart_host_hits_total` increments.
- [ ] Expired cap with `Accept: text/html` (no `Sec-Fetch-*`) → 302 to `/grant?part=…&path=…&mode=direct`; without it → 401 + `X-PF-Reauth: 1`; `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document` and `iframe` are treated as navigations, `Sec-Fetch-Dest: script` as a subresource.
- [ ] `Origin: https://evil.example` → 403; `Origin: null` → allowed with `ACAO: null` + `Vary: Origin` and never `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`.
- [ ] Golden header snapshots for a sandboxed and an unsandboxed part document (the canonical CSP verbatim with `<self-host>`, `<workspace>` and `<embedders>` filled; `unsandboxed` differs only by the missing `sandbox` directive), an SVG served as a document, and a part blob (`private, immutable`).
- [ ] No response from a `:8081` part host ever contains `Set-Cookie`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` or `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` (property over all routes); `?dl=1` adds `Content-Disposition: attachment` with the file name.
- [ ] Entry templating: the prelude tag is the first element of `<head>` in every served HTML document, the import map carries the cap prefix, `pf-boot` is ≤ 256 KiB and empty for link/render/guest caps; HTML without `<head>` and HTML with an existing import map are handled (golden); a markdown or text part's shell links the current `pf-shell.css` hash.
- [ ] Changing the prelude (or `pf-shell.css`) blob hash changes the served entry of an existing live part with no new build row.
- [ ] A blob path and a 304 on a matching ETag make zero DB queries (query counter = 0); the entry makes exactly one indexed read, cached per cap; a brotli variant is served when accepted; after `part.live_changed` the next request serves the new build.
- [ ] Blob host: a part-class hash returns 404; a shared hash returns `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `ACAO: *` and never `Set-Cookie`; the prelude is present in `shared_blobs` after start.
- [ ] The prelude is ≤ 12 KiB brotli; `document.cookie` writes never reach a request; feature-detect patterns (`'indexedDB' in window && indexedDB`) fall back cleanly.
- [ ] A Claude-written page writing `localStorage` then reloading sees its state, and a second browser for the same fixture person sees it after load; closing the tab within 100 ms of a write still persists (`sendBeacon`).
- [ ] `fetch('/data.json')`, XHR and `EventSource('/x')` hit `/c/<cap>/…`; `new Worker('./w.js')` and module workers run in Chromium, WebKit (or the documented fallback from the spike) and Gecko.
- [ ] `/_rt/v1` is a CORS-simple request (no `OPTIONS` in any HAR); a non-null foreign `Origin` → 403 without parsing the body; a `Sec-Fetch-Mode` other than `cors` is refused; a request with `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` from the part itself is accepted.
- [ ] Personal storage round trip over `/_rt/v1` (`__storage`, keyed by the cap's person); a bad key → `invalid_input`; personal data past 256 KiB → `quota_exceeded`; a link, render or guest cap has no personal scope.
- [ ] `refresh` returns a valid new cap for the same subject; after an epoch bump it returns `forbidden` if access was revoked.
- [ ] Throw, unhandled rejection, CSP block and blocked load are each recorded in `runtime_errors` with the right `kind`; repeats increment `count`; the 1,001st distinct error evicts the oldest; more than 10 inserts a minute per part are limited; URLs are stored without the cap.
- [ ] In a browser, an html, a markdown and a text part render, the text part byte-for-byte with stable line anchors, and a `vite build` (`base: './'`) uploaded as `files` loads every asset with no broken URL (`kinds_render.spec.ts`).
- [ ] A fixture page with the contract's cdnjs React UMD `<script>`s, Google Fonts CSS and a jsDelivr `+esm` module renders with zero third-party requests in the network log, and the source's anchors still match (`mirror_zero_third_party.spec.ts`).
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` in the e2e harness (parts from `partifactory dev put`, caps from `partifactory dev cap`), `curl -si https://<name>-part.pf.test/c/<cap>/` returns 200 with the canonical CSP and no `Set-Cookie`, an expired cap returns 302 to `/grant?mode=direct` with `Accept: text/html` and 401 `X-PF-Reauth: 1` without it, and `https://blobs-part.pf.test/b/<prelude-hash>` returns 200 `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- [ ] GATE: Playwright on `chromium-desktop`, `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop` renders an html, a markdown and a text part and a vite `files` bundle; a CDN fixture page's network log holds only the part host and `blobs-part`; `localStorage` survives reload and a second browser for the same fixture user; the HAR has zero `OPTIONS`; a throwing page creates a `runtime_errors` row.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with these tests in the nextest job (`ci/test.sh`) and the `e2e` harness job (`tests/e2e/content_listener_sandbox.spec.ts`, `prelude_*.spec.ts`, `runtime_errors.spec.ts`, `kinds_render.spec.ts`, `mirror_zero_third_party.spec.ts`).
- [ ] GATE: The e2e server JSONL shows `event="serve.entry"` and `event="cap.verify" outcome="expired"`, and no log line contains a cap.
- [ ] GATE: Simulator lane (evidence, not a CI check): the `content_listener_sandbox` and `prelude_storage` self-reporting pages pass in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh`), with posts, screenshots and the runtime version attached to the `verified` report.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite and every earlier bead's gate tests still pass.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, curl excerpts, browser versions) and `br gate report` passes for `ci_green` and `verified`.
