title: part_check: the render sidecar, actions and the after_check gate
description:
## Goal
Agents see and validate their own work before anyone opens it. `part_check` renders a version in a sandboxed headless browser exactly as a viewer would, optionally clicks and types through it, and returns a screenshot, a `blank` flag, uncaught errors, console lines and failed loads. The same check is the `live: "after_check"` gate, so a page that builds but throws never reaches people between an agent's create and its fix. The renderer is optional and never on the save path.

## Scope
- [ ] Sidecar `partifactory-render` as a `render` profile service (off unless `[render] enabled`), added to the e2e harness compose now and carried into `deploy/compose.yaml` by the Shipping bead: `chrome-headless-shell` pinned by digest + Noto fonts, non-root, read-only root, tmpfs `/tmp`, 768m / 256 pids / 1 CPU, `json-file` 10m x 3.
- [ ] Isolation: only a Docker `internal: true` network; `--host-resolver-rules` maps `*-part` and `blobs-part` to the gateway; partifactory serves the content handlers on an internal-only `:443` with a self-signed cert generated at start, SPKI-pinned; headers byte-identical to the public listener.
- [ ] Chrome over CDP (`chromiumoxide`): on demand, stop after 5 min idle, circuit breaker, `pf_render_up`.
- [ ] Renderer caps: subject `render`, 60 s, read-only, pinned `v`; `/_rt` reads real shared data only with `data:read`, personal storage empty, writes to a per-job overlay later reads see and that is dropped at job end; no `data.changed` from it; `errors.report` stored with `source: render`.
- [ ] Queue `render_jobs`: concurrency 1, coalesced per part (5 s debounce; requested check/gate jobs joined, not dropped), one retry, fresh context per job, hard 15 s.
- [ ] Driver: mobile 390x844@2x / desktop 1280x800; wait for `partifactory.ready()`, 500 ms idle or `wait_ms` (≤ 8000), whichever is first; `actions` (<= 20; `type` ≤ 1,000 chars, `wait_ms` ≤ 2,000, `eval_return` value ≤ 4 KiB; first failure stops; screenshot after the last); collect errors (`error`, `unhandledrejection`, `blocked_load`, `csp`), console (`error`/`warn`, first 50, truncated), failed requests, height, timing (`ready_ms` null without `ready()`), blank (body text empty *and* ≥ 98 % one colour); URLs with the cap removed. Chrome flags per §4c.
- [ ] Op `part_check` (`parts:read`, the contract's pixel example), `GET /api/v1/screenshots/<id>` (same connection, 10 min, `private, no-store`), 30 per hour per connection, `renderer_unavailable` (503, exit 7).
- [ ] The gate: `versions.live_gate`, `builds.gate_check`, a `gate` job after an `ok` build; live moves only on `passed`; renderer off -> `skipped` + `check_skipped`; `part_edit {check: true}` folds `check` in; a `part_check` on a gating version returns that same check.

- [ ] Gallery thumbnail source (decision 53): when a `check` or `gate` render of the live version passes, its screenshot (a part blob) is upserted as the part's `part_previews` row (`source: render`, poster only), replacing the old one; the replaced blob is left to GC.

## Plan refs
§4c Tier (b) and `part_check`; §3d `live`, the live switch and `wait`; §4 Slice 1 op fields; §5e `render_jobs`, `live_gate`, `gate_check`; §7 Render sidecar; decisions 16, 43; agent contract `part_check`, `part_edit`, Rule 3, the worked session.

## Considerations
- Production-identical URLs, CSP and secure context are the point: a check's result is what a viewer gets. Mirror-on-build means parts need nothing third-party, so the internal network suffices.
- Read-only real data + discarded overlay (decision 43): a painted pixel shows in the screenshot, and click + `eval_return` proves the write path without painting anyone's board. The overlay lives in the content listener, so the prelude has no special mode. It rides on the shared-data `/_rt` storage ops and `part_data`.
- A connection without `data:read` must not see shared data in a screenshot either.
- Concurrency 1 and 30/h keep RAM bounded on a household box and stop a looping agent; the 30-per-hour limit is a row in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead), keyed on the connection.
- Only the requesting connection may fetch a screenshot; that per-connection check and the MCP image content block are verified in the MCP, discovery and conformance bead, which has real connections.

## Tests and logging
- Unit: action limits, the 98 % blank rule, queue coalesce / retry / breaker, cap stripping from every output `url`.
- Integration: `crates/pf-render/tests/sidecar_isolation.rs` (egress and LAN canaries, header parity, idle shutdown), `rt_render_overlay.rs` + proptest `render_cap_never_writes`, `driver.rs` over `tests/golden/render/`, `part_check_e2e.rs`, `part_check_op.rs`, `screenshot_endpoint.rs`, `live_gate.rs`, `runtime_errors_render_source.rs`.
- Logs asserted: `event="render.job" purpose="check|gate" outcome`, `event="cap.mint" subject="render"`, `event="rt.op" principal="render" persisted=false`, `event="live.switch" gate="after_check" result="held|moved|skipped"`; never a cap. Artifacts under `target/e2e-logs/<test>/`.

## Verification gate
- Binary from `main`, sidecar up (`docker compose --profile render up`) in the harness: `part check` on a throwing page, a blank page and the pixel board returns the error, `blank: true` and a click + `eval_return` value, PNGs saved; `part_data list` is unchanged afterwards.
- An `after_check` version that throws stays off `live`; the fix goes live (worked session steps 3-5, against the running server). Profile off: 503 `renderer_unavailable`, `check_skipped`. Egress and LAN canaries from the sidecar fail.
- CI green on `main`: these tests in the nextest job, `part_check_e2e.rs` in the e2e harness job.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="render.job"` and `event="live.switch"` and finds no cap in the JSONL.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Close with evidence: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, screenshot paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docker compose --profile render up` starts the sidecar; `docker inspect` shows read-only root, non-root user, tmpfs `/tmp`, the 768m / 256 pids / 1 CPU limits, the internal network only and the log limits; without `[render] enabled` no sidecar runs.
- [ ] From inside the sidecar, `curl https://example.com` (egress canary) fails; a LAN canary fails.
- [ ] Chrome loads `https://<name>-part.<domain>/c/<cap>/` via the internal listener with the canonical CSP header identical to the public listener's (header parity over the golden routes).
- [ ] Idle 5 min → Chrome process gone and `pf_render_up` 0; the next job restarts it; repeated crashes open the circuit breaker, and jobs then get `renderer_unavailable` until it closes.
- [ ] A render cap cannot persist any `/_rt` write (proptest `render_cap_never_writes`, §7 Render sidecar line); a write then read in the same job returns the written value; after the job, `data_docs` is unchanged and the overlay freed.
- [ ] Without `data:read`, shared `list` returns empty in the check; personal storage always starts empty.
- [ ] No `data.changed` reaches an open viewer tab during a check.
- [ ] A throwing page yields the error with its stack (and a `runtime_errors` row with `source: render`); a blank page returns `blank: true`; a seeded shared doc shows in the screenshot; a click followed by `eval_return` reads the changed state, and the write is gone afterwards.
- [ ] Action limits: 21 actions, a `type` over 1,000 chars, a `wait_ms` action over 2,000 ms or a top-level `wait_ms` over 8,000 is `invalid_input`; the first failing step stops the list and is reported in `actions`.
- [ ] Every `url` in the output is a path within the part with no cap; `timing.ready_ms` is `null` for a page that never calls `partifactory.ready()`; `viewport: "desktop"` renders at 1280×800.
- [ ] Two checks queued for one part within 5 s → one runs, the other `superseded` (gate/check jobs explicitly requested are joined, not dropped).
- [ ] A page that never settles is cut at 15 s with partial results.
- [ ] `GET /api/v1/screenshots/<id>` serves the PNG with `private, no-store`; `include_base64: true` adds `base64`.
- [ ] The 31st call in an hour from one connection → 429 with `Retry-After`; sidecar absent → 503 `renderer_unavailable` (CLI exit 7).
- [ ] `part_check` on a version whose build is not `ok` returns `screenshot: null`, `blank: null` and the build's errors; on a running build it waits inside the 15 s limit.
- [ ] A `part_check` on a version whose `after_check` gate check is running returns that same check (one render, one answer).
- [ ] Contract worked session reproduces: v1 throws → `live: null`; v2 fix with `after_check` → `head: 2, live: 2, check.passed: true`.
- [ ] With the renderer off, `part_create`/`part_edit` with `live: "after_check"` behave as `always` and `build.warnings` carries `check_skipped`; `part_edit {check: true}` folds the result in as `check`.
- [ ] A passing `part_check` of the live version upserts `part_previews` (`source: render`) with its screenshot; a failing or `head`-only check doesn't; the old poster blob is unreferenced afterwards (GC test).
- [ ] End to end with the wrapper bead's `gallery_thumbs.spec.ts`: after a passing `after_check` gate on the live version, the gallery shows that render's screenshot for the part in place of the being-made frame, and a viewer without access gets 404 on the thumb URL.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` with the render profile up in the e2e harness, `part check` on a throwing page, a blank page and the pixel board returns the error, `blank: true` and the click + `eval_return` value, screenshots saved; `part_data list` is unchanged afterwards.
- [ ] GATE: Against the running server, an `after_check` version that throws stays off `live` and the fix goes live (worked session steps 3-5); with the profile off, `part_check` is 503 `renderer_unavailable` and `after_check` carries `check_skipped`; egress and LAN canaries from the sidecar fail.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the nextest job and `crates/pf-render/tests/part_check_e2e.rs` in the e2e harness job.
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="render.job"` and `event="live.switch"` log lines and finds no cap in the captured JSONL.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, every earlier bead's gate tests included, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence: commit SHAs, CI run id, gate commands with output excerpts, screenshot paths; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.

title: Identity: OIDC sign-in, the claims directory, the policy engine, /grant and admin step-up
description:
## Goal
People sign in with any OIDC provider, get the one cookie partifactory sets, and every request is decided by one provider-neutral policy engine. `/grant` turns "this signed-in person opens this part" into a cap for the part's host, and admin power comes only from a pinned subject plus a fresh native passkey assertion. This bridges the cookie world (the workspace) and the cookie-free part hosts, and underpins every sharing guarantee.

## Scope
- [ ] Generic OIDC client (`openidconnect`, discovery from `[idp] issuer`, confidential + PKCE S256, `state`/`nonce`); claim names from config; `/signin?return=<path>` (path-only), `/oidc/callback`, `POST /signout`, `POST /signout/everywhere`; users keyed by `(idp_issuer, idp_sub)`. A person's first sign-in creates their user row and their personal space (the store's space service), so a part an agent makes for them has somewhere to live.
- [ ] Sessions: `__Host-pf_session` (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`), stored as sha256, 30 days sliding (12 h without a refresh token), refresh token encrypted with `PF_SESSION_KEY`; sign out everywhere bumps each `minter:sess:<id>` epoch; audited.
- [ ] Claims re-read directory: groups claim at login, refresh-token re-read every 15 min, `invalid_grant` ends the session and bumps the person's minter epoch, unreachable IdP keeps last-known membership (`directory.stale_since`, alert `idp_unreachable_10m` after 10 min, no epoch bump); membership diffs bump only affected `part:<id>` epochs; local `pf-*` groups.
- [ ] Policy engine (`pf-policy`): roles view < comment < edit < manage; effective = max(part, space grants), inherited live; agents = person's role ∩ scopes within consented spaces; `everyone-signed-in` = audience group (`audience_group`) + active local accounts, with its live count; the role × runtime matrix incl. guests and `shared_data_writers`; grant API with one audit row per change, epoch bumps on revoke, expiry timer; denials logged as structured decisions.
- [ ] `/grant?part&path&mode=wrap|direct` (host derived from the name; `path` ≤ 2 KiB and must start with `/`), the signed-out sign-in page, `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` with no title (its **Ask for access** button comes after Slice 1 with the workspace extras), silent re-entry, and the regrant handler for `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant`.
- [ ] Admin pin (`[admin] subject`), `RequireAdmin`, `partifactory admin bootstrap`, `partifactory admin break-glass` (5 min, once; shown in the audit log, and on the Health page once it exists).
- [ ] WebAuthn step-up (`webauthn-rs` 0.5, `rp.id` = apex): `stepup` passkeys, assertions from the workspace and every active sandboxed part-host origin, `sessions.stepup_at`, 10-minute `RequireStepUp` on the admin action list, `step_up_status` for the UI chip.

## Plan refs
§3a (layers, how people sign in, spaces, audience ladder, role × runtime, who may write shared data, admin), §2 Serving (hand-off, errors, framed expiry), §2 The link to post (what each visitor sees), §5a (`/grant` p99 < 1 ms), §5e identity, access and `epochs` tables + hot-path rules, §5f, §7 Identity and admin, §7 Part hosts (`/grant` lines). Decisions 7, 13, 15, 23.

## Considerations
- The workspace is the only OIDC client: one redirect URI. Implicit consent lives in the IdP; people see no consent screen.
- Fail open on an unreachable IdP, fail closed on `invalid_grant`; a failed poll changes nothing.
- Never confirm what's behind a name: `not_found` outside a principal's view; the 403 page shows no title.
- The no-cap hop is client-side; framed parts never navigate to `/grant` (no Lax cookie from an opaque-origin subframe), hence the regrant endpoint.
- Pin, never a group. Native step-up makes the IdP's `max_age` irrelevant. One 10-minute window; inward sharing never asks. Unsandboxed origins are never accepted.
- Wrapper-origin assertion lines need the wrapper page, so they are verified in the trusted wrapper bead.
- This bead owns the sign-in and 403 decisions and routes and renders them as plain, content-free pages; the wrapper bead (which owns the two content-free card PNGs and the Stockroom workspace pages) restyles them and adds the private card's og tags. Tests here assert that neither page carries a title, name or any part-derived field, and is `noindex`.
- Every timer takes an injectable clock; e2e advances it through a dev-only endpoint. Parts and grants for e2e come from dev-only subcommands.
- This bead starts as soon as the store lands and runs in parallel with the builds and part host beads (§6a "Identity, in parallel once the schema lands"). `/grant` and the regrant handler mint caps with the store bead's `pf-caps` crate; never write a second copy. `grant_flow.spec.ts` asserts the 302 target and the `#pf=` fragment; following the redirect into a served part is the wrapper bead's spec once the content listener is live.
- `/grant`, `/signin` and the regrant handler register their rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead).

## Tests and logging
- `crates/pf-auth/tests/{oidc_mock,second_provider,sessions,signout,claims_reread,first_signin_space,grant_fuzz,webauthn,stepup_guard,admin_guard}.rs`, `crates/pf-policy/tests/{audit,expiry,everyone_signed_in}.rs`, `pf_policy::tests::prop_no_role_above_best_grant`, `rt_matrix_table`, `crates/partifactory/tests/admin_cli.rs`; bench `grant_decide` (`/grant` decision + 302 p99 < 1 ms, tracked, not gated).
- E2E: `tests/e2e/identity/{login_roundtrip,group_removal,grant_flow,stepup_workspace}.spec.ts`.
- Logs: `event="session.created"`, `event="session.ended" reason="signout|everywhere|invalid_grant|expired"`, `event="directory.refresh" outcome=…`, `event="epoch.bump" reason=…`, `event="policy.decide" outcome="deny"`, `event="grant.decide" mode=…`, `event="stepup.verify"`, `event="admin.break_glass"`; metrics `pf_directory_refresh_total`, `pf_directory_stale`, `pf_epoch_bumps_total`. Never a cap, code, cookie or token.

## Verification gate
- Running build in the harness: Dex sign-in on chromium-desktop and webkit-mobile (and with the second Dex config), the first sign-in creating the person's personal space; a group removal plus clock advance refuses the next `/grant` (no cap minted); `curl -si` of `/grant` shows the cap only after `#pf=`; an outsider gets the 403 page with no title; workspace step-up with the virtual authenticator; break-glass works once.
- CI green on `main`: nextest job and harness e2e job include the tests above.
- Logs: the e2e run asserts `session.created`, `grant.decide`, `directory.refresh`, `stepup.verify`, and no canary cap in any line.
- No regressions in the full e2e suite.
- Evidence on close plus the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Sign-in round trip in e2e against Dex on `parts.pf.test` over TLS, in Chromium and WebKit, creates a user, a session and the cookie with exactly `__Host-pf_session; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`; the person's first sign-in creates their personal space, and a second sign-in creates nothing new.
- [ ] A second provider config (different issuer, claim names) signs in with the same binary and no code change.
- [ ] Sessions slide to 30 days; a no-refresh-token IdP yields 12-hour sessions.
- [ ] Sign out everywhere revokes all the person's sessions and bumps their minter epochs (a cap minted before fails after); each sign-out is audited.
- [ ] `return` cannot redirect off the workspace host (fuzzed).
- [ ] Removing a user from a Dex group fails their next part request after the next re-read (test clock); deleting the user ends the session on `invalid_grant` and bumps their minter epoch; with the IdP down, existing sessions keep working and no epoch is bumped.
- [ ] With the IdP unreachable for 10 minutes the `idp_unreachable_10m` alert condition is raised and `directory.stale_since` is set; local `pf-*` membership changes bump affected part epochs at once, and a local group not named `pf-*` is rejected by the schema.
- [ ] Property test: no subject gets a role above its best matching grant; a `view` grantee can write shared data only while the part is `shared_data_writers: viewers`; a Can-view guest never writes; every grant change writes one audit row.
- [ ] Space grants are inherited live, agents never exceed their person or their consented spaces, the full role × runtime matrix (guest rows included) is table-tested, and an expired grant stops working at expiry (test clock).
- [ ] `everyone-signed-in` resolves to the `audience_group` members plus active local accounts, not every IdP account, and its count matches that set.
- [ ] Open-redirect fuzz: no input yields a Location outside the part's host; a `path` over 2 KiB or not starting with `/` is refused; `wrap` puts the cap only in the fragment; an expired cap on a navigation re-enters /grant silently; a signed-in person without access gets `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` with no title.
- [ ] Signed out, `/grant` shows the sign-in page (no title, name or part-derived field, `noindex`), never content, and returns to the part after sign-in; `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant` returns a fresh cap for an allowed session and 403 otherwise; logs never contain the cap.
- [ ] An IdP-admin-group user who isn't the pinned subject gets 403 on every admin route; a config check rejects a malformed `[admin] subject`.
- [ ] `admin bootstrap` registers a local admin passkey once; a second run refuses.
- [ ] Break-glass code works once within 5 minutes, fails after use or expiry, and writes an audit row with `actor='break-glass'`.
- [ ] Assertions from `Origin: null`, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, a redirecting old name or a foreign origin are rejected.
- [ ] An admin action without a fresh assertion → `step_up_required` (HTTP 403, CLI exit 3); within 10 min → allowed; at 10 min + 1 s after the last assertion it is `step_up_required` again.
- [ ] Household sharing never asks for step-up.
- [ ] `/grant` decision + 302 p99 < 1 ms on the bench fixture (tracked, not gated).
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` in the e2e harness, sign-in through Dex passes on chromium-desktop and webkit-mobile (and again with the second Dex config) and the first sign-in creates the person's personal space, a Dex group removal plus a test-clock advance refuses the next `/grant`, `curl -si` of `/grant` shows the cap only after `#pf=`, an outsider sees the 403 page with no title, admin step-up succeeds with the virtual authenticator, and break-glass works once.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the identity tests (`crates/pf-auth/tests/*`, `crates/pf-policy/tests/*`, `crates/partifactory/tests/admin_cli.rs`) in the nextest job and `tests/e2e/identity/*.spec.ts` in the harness e2e job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="session.created"`, `event="grant.decide"`, `event="directory.refresh"` and `event="stepup.verify" outcome="ok"`, and no captured line contains the canary cap.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command output excerpts) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports recorded.

title: Agent connections: the token service, the device grant and personal tokens
description:
## Goal
Agents get their own identity, not a shared admin key: one scoped, space-limited, revocable connection per (agent, person), labelled "<agent> for <person>", whose token works on every surface. This bead is the token side of partifactory's own OAuth 2.1 authorization server (issue, refresh rotation, revocation, metadata, 401s), the device grant with its `/device` page, personal tokens and Connected agents. It is built so authorization code after Slice 1 adds an endpoint, not a redesign. The pixel test's agent connects by device code.

## Scope
- [ ] Token store: opaque `pf_at_`/`pf_rt_`/`pf_pat_` + base32 of 160 random bits, stored only as sha256; access 3600 s; single-use refresh rotated in one writer transaction; reuse revokes the family (`invalid_grant`), suspended 24 h after an import; the family ends at the connection's `expires_at`; `POST /oauth/token` (refresh + device-code grants, form in, JSON out) and `POST /oauth/revoke`.
- [ ] Bearer middleware for `/api/*` (replacing the registry bead's dev-token authenticator; `/mcp` uses the same middleware when it lands): every token kind resolves to one `Principal {user_id, connection_id, kind, scopes, spaces, agent_name}`; checks `resource` = `https://parts.<domain>/`, expiry, revocation; any cache is invalidated on revoke. The content listener and `/oauth/*` never accept bearer tokens.
- [ ] Scopes: exactly the §3b list (`parts:read`, `parts:write`, `parts:delete`, `data:read`, `data:write`, `comments:write`, `share:household`, `backends:deploy`); no admin scope exists or can be requested (`invalid_scope`).
- [ ] Revocation cascade: revoking a connection revokes its refresh family, access tokens and PATs and bumps `minter:conn:<id>`; grants it made stay, listed with "Undo all".
- [ ] Metadata from one struct, listing only mounted endpoints: RFC 9728 protected-resource and RFC 8414 AS metadata (also at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, no `id_token`).
- [ ] 401 contract: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…"` plus a JSON `unauthenticated` body naming the ways to get a token that exist (device code, personal token); CLI exit 3.
- [ ] `agent_connections` and the shared consent sheet: "This device says it is *Hermes*" (unverified), plain-word scope toggles (share and backends off unless requested), spaces the person may consent (others' spaces need the admin with step-up), lifetime 30 d / 90 d default / 1 y, Allow (passkey when the person has one) / Deny; phone layout.
- [ ] Device grant: `POST /oauth/device_authorization`, built-in public client `part-cli`, `agent_name` (required, ≤ 40) + `software`; `user_code` `XXXX-XXXX` from `BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ`, 600 s, interval 5 s, `slow_down` +5 s, single use; `/device` with the big code, coarse origin and age, the stale (> 2 min) and different-network banners, manual entry 5/min/session; signed-out visits return with the code filled; `part login` (added to the registry bead's CLI) drives it (terminal QR), stores the tokens in the CLI's credential chain and serialises refreshes across concurrent invocations.
- [ ] Personal tokens from Connected agents (name, scopes, spaces, expiry 30 d default, 1 y max), shown once with the env lines and the `claude mcp add … --header` snippet; never refresh.
- [ ] Connected agents: each connection with scopes, spaces, last used, token type, grants made; Revoke with a 10 s undo toast (undo clears `revoked_at`, never the epoch bump; both audited).

## Plan refs
§3b How agents authenticate, Device grant, Personal agent tokens, Scopes, Revocation cascades; §4a.6 Connecting an agent; §4a.7; §4b Auth per client, Discovery (401 body), Errors; §5c import; §5e `oauth_tokens`, `agent_connections`, `oauth_clients`, `device_codes`; §5f device-connect origin; §7 Agents; decisions 8, 14, 37, 43; docs/agent-contract.md Connecting.

## Considerations
- Opaque, not JWTs: revocation is one row, no key distribution; a DB read per `/api` call is fine off the hot path. Keep an `AuthorizationServer` trait so an IdP with CIMD + RFC 8707 could take over.
- Two concurrent refreshes with one token: the loser triggers family revocation (spec-correct), so clients serialise refreshes.
- One connection per (agent, person) prevents the confused deputy.
- In Slice 1 a person with no passkey approves with their session alone; without an origin source only the age banner fires.
- Slice 1 has no agent sharing (`part_share` comes after it), so "grants made" is always empty here; the list and "Undo all" are wired now and exercised with agent sharing in the rest-of-P2 work.
- Needs the registry bead: `/api` and the `part` CLI are its, and `part login` and the bearer middleware plug into them. The `/device`, consent and Connected agents pages use the Stockroom shell from the wrapper bead.
- The `/mcp` lines (401 on `/mcp`, a PAT on `/mcp`) are verified in the MCP, discovery and conformance bead.
- `/oauth/*` and `/device` register their rows in the shared rate-limit layer (observability bead); the 5-per-minute manual code entry is one of them, keyed on the session.
- `comments:write`, `share:household` and `backends:deploy` exist and can be granted, but no Slice 1 op needs them; the contract's scope table says so, and the consent sheet leaves them off unless requested.

## Tests and logging
- Unit: token store (rotate, reuse, import suspension, expiry, cascade), device codes (test clock), PAT format and bounds, consent rules, scope parsing (`invalid_scope`), property `scope_never_exceeds_person_role`.
- Integration: `revocation_cascade.rs`, `concurrent_refresh.rs`, `bearer_middleware.rs`, `metadata_validate.rs`, `device_two_people.rs` in the oauth crate; `unauthenticated_401.rs`, `pat_parity.rs`, `pat_revoke_next_call.rs` in the api crate; `no_bearer_on_part_host.rs`; CLI `login_serialised_refresh.rs`.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/consent_sheet.spec.ts`, `device_grant.spec.ts` (virtual authenticator + mobile WebKit, `part login` subprocess, budget 3), `connected_agents.spec.ts`.
- Logs asserted: `event="device.authorize"`, `event="device.approve"`, `event="token.issue"`, `event="token.refresh"`, `event="connection.create"`, `event="connection.revoke"`, `event="auth.reject" reason`, `event="cap.verify" outcome="stale_epoch"`; canary tokens never logged.

## Verification gate
- On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness: `part login` is approved on `/device` (mobile WebKit; Chromium with the virtual authenticator) and the token runs `part get`; a PAT from Connected agents works on `/api` and gets 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` right after revoke; the AS metadata lists only mounted endpoints.
- CI green on `main`: the tests above in the nextest and e2e harness jobs.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="token.issue"` and `event="auth.reject" reason="revoked"`, and no canary token.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, `/device` screenshots at 360 px; `ci_green` and `verified` reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token in one transaction; presenting a used refresh token revokes the whole family (`invalid_grant`), and so does any refresh in the 24 h after an import; the family stops refreshing at the connection's `expires_at`; access tokens expire after 3600 s.
- [ ] A revoked token fails on the very next call (no stale cache).
- [ ] A token is rejected on part hosts and on `/oauth/*`; a token whose `resource` isn't `https://parts.<domain>/` is rejected.
- [ ] A token never appears in logs; only its prefix may (`pf_at_…`); the redaction canary covers all three prefixes.
- [ ] Requesting an unknown or admin-like scope is `invalid_scope`; no token ever carries a scope outside the §3b list.
- [ ] Both metadata docs (and `/.well-known/openid-configuration`) validate against RFC 9728/8414 JSON schemas, carry no `id_token` fields, and their advertised endpoints equal the mounted routes (test).
- [ ] Every 401 from `/api` carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…"` and the JSON `unauthenticated` body; the CLI exits 3.
- [ ] Creating a connection outside consentable spaces is refused (`forbidden {space}`), or needs admin step-up.
- [ ] Writes made through a connection record `actor_conn` and render as "<agent> for <person>".
- [ ] The consent sheet shows the unverified agent name and software, scope toggles in plain words (share and backends off unless requested), the space picker and the lifetime picker (90 days default); it passes the contrast test and the 360 px layout check.
- [ ] `part login` -> code -> approve on phone with a passkey -> token; `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `expired_token` and `access_denied` tested; two people pairing Hermes give two connections labelled 'Hermes for <person>'; a household member with no partifactory passkey approves with their session.
- [ ] Two concurrent `part` invocations whose access token has expired refresh once between them and the family survives.
- [ ] Revoking a connection revokes its access, refresh and personal tokens and bumps `minter:conn:<id>`; a cap minted through it fails on the next request; undo within 10 s clears `revoked_at` but never the epoch bump, and both are audited.
- [ ] Device codes expire at 600 s and are single use; manual code entry is limited to 5 a minute per session; the stale (> 2 min) and different-network banners appear when they should; a signed-out visit to `/device?code=…` returns to the page with the code filled after sign-in.
- [ ] A PAT is shown once, only its hash is stored, its expiry defaults to 30 days and is capped at 1 year, and it works on `/api` with the same decisions as a device token; revoke from Connected agents (3 interactions, undo toast) gives 401 on the next call.
- [ ] Connected agents lists each connection with scopes, spaces, last used, token type (`device` / `personal token`) and grants made.
- [ ] The token service is built as the OAuth AS token side: adding authorization code after Slice 1 needs only new endpoints and metadata fields, not a new token model.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness, `part login` is approved on `/device` (mobile WebKit and Chromium with the virtual authenticator) and the token runs `part get`; a PAT from Connected agents works on `/api` and returns 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` right after revoke; the AS metadata lists only mounted endpoints.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the token, device and PAT tests (nextest job) and `device_grant.spec.ts`, `connected_agents.spec.ts`, `consent_sheet.spec.ts` (e2e harness job).
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="token.issue"` and `event="auth.reject" reason="revoked"` lines, and no canary token value appears in logs.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, `/device` screenshots with browser versions) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.

title: Observability and the e2e harness: logs, metrics, request ids, the ingress contract, Dex + Caddy + pf.test
description:
## Goal
Give partifactory one observability backbone and one production-shaped test bed before any feature that needs a browser lands: redacted JSON logs, Prometheus metrics, `/healthz` and a `/readyz` skeleton, the core of the ingress contract (client address, request ids, the shared rate-limit layer) with the one shipped Caddy config, and the browser e2e harness (Dex, Caddy with an internal-CA cert for `pf.test`, Playwright on Chromium, WebKit and Firefox with mobile emulation, plus the Mobile Safari lane in the iOS Simulator). Every later bead's gate runs in this harness and asserts on these log lines, which is why it comes first.

## Scope
- [ ] Logging (the obs crate): `tracing` JSON to stdout, always on; one access line per request (`event="http.request"`) with `request_id, route_class, status, latency_us, principal, outcome, client_ip` (plus `op`, `surface`, `part_id` when known); the shared field convention `ts, level, target, msg, request_id, route_class, op, surface, part_id, principal, outcome, latency_us` + an `event` name, exported as helpers so later beads log in one shape.
- [ ] Redaction by type (`Secret<T>`, `CapToken`, `BearerToken`, `SessionId`, `RefreshToken` print `[redacted]`) plus a pattern layer: `/c/<…>/` -> `/c/[cap]/`, `pf_at_|pf_rt_|pf_pat_` tokens redacted, `Authorization`/`Cookie`/`Set-Cookie` never recorded, `Location` values with `#pf=` stripped. Runtime log-level reload handle (the admin-area control comes later; this bead exposes the handle and a dev-only route to drive it).
- [ ] Metrics on `:9090/metrics` behind `PF_METRICS_TOKEN` (401 otherwise): RED per route class (`workspace_ui, api, mcp, oauth, grant, content_entry, content_blob, rt, wrapper, blob_host, chrome_api, ops`) and per op via `record_op(op, surface, outcome, dur)`; skeleton gauges later beads fill, incl. `pf_nonpart_host_hits_total` and `pf_rate_limited_total`. No part names, principals or request ids as labels (enforced by a test over the registry).
- [ ] `/healthz` and a `/readyz` check registry: DB writable, blob store OK, disk headroom > 5 %; `degraded` rows (IdP, directory poll, backup freshness) never cause 503; `importing` field reserved for the import work. The Health/export bead (pf-q3p8) fills in the real backup probes and the `importing` state.
- [ ] Ingress contract core: `ClientAddr` layer on both public listeners (header from `[ingress] client_ip_header` trusted only from `trusted_proxies`; right-most untrusted `X-Forwarded-For` hop); request-id layer (`request_id_header` value if trusted, printable and ≤ 128 chars, else generated), echoed as a response header, shown on a minimal error page (§4a.6), and carried in a task-local so later beads attach it to API errors and propagate it as `X-PF-Request-Id` to the build child, `/_rt` and backends (§5d) without re-plumbing.
- [ ] The shared rate-limit layer (§5d, on by default): a `governor` tower layer keyed on the trusted client address, and on the principal once a later layer attaches one, with a route table `{route_class, key, limit, window}` that later beads register their routes in (`/grant`, `/oauth/*`, `/device`, `/l/*`, `/_rt` reads and writes, `/api`, `/mcp`, `part_check`); 429 + `Retry-After`, `event="ratelimit.trip" route_class key_kind`, `pf_rate_limited_total{route_class}`; a safe default that only `[unsafe] rate_limits = "off"` disables (the config bead's `[unsafe]` mechanism). Nothing is registered yet except a self-test route.
- [ ] `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` (the one Caddy config in the repo: two site blocks by Host, wildcard cert, `X-Forwarded-For`, SSE flush, 8 MiB bodies, 60 s streams, never exposes `:9090`, serves the maintenance page when the origin is down), `deploy/proxy/maintenance.html` (static `503 · DOWN FOR MAINTENANCE`, inlined CSS), and `deploy/proxy/smoke.sh`.
- [ ] `tests/e2e/harness/`: Dex (static users/groups matching the fixture identities in `tests/fixtures/identity.toml`, refresh tokens and groups claim on, plus a second Dex config with a different issuer and claim names that the identity bead's second-provider test signs in against), Caddy mounting the shipped Caddyfile with only the test cert paths overridden, a per-run internal CA trusted by the browsers (never `--ignore-certificate-errors`), host resolution (Chromium `--host-resolver-rules`, WebKit and Firefox via `/etc/hosts` or dnsmasq), Playwright projects `chromium-desktop` (virtual WebAuthn authenticator), `chromium-mobile` (phone viewport, touch, virtual authenticator), `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop`, and partifactory started from the harness's own `tests/e2e/harness/compose.yaml` with `_FILE` secrets (the shipping bead later points the harness at `deploy/compose.yaml`).
- [ ] The iOS Simulator lane, `tests/device/ios-sim.sh` (this bead writes it; if the sandbox spike's `tests/sandbox-spike/ios-sim.sh` and collector have landed, start from them, but never wait for them): boots a device on the installed iOS runtime (`xcrun simctl boot`), trusts the harness CA (`simctl keychain add-root-cert`), resolves `*.pf.test` through the Mac's `/etc/hosts`, opens a self-reporting page with `simctl openurl`, waits for the page's POST to the harness collector, takes `simctl io screenshot`, and writes `target/e2e-logs/ios-sim/<spec>/`. It runs locally on the Mac (or a macOS runner if one exists) and is never a required CI check: beads whose gate names it attach its output to their `verified` report.
- [ ] Click-budget helper; per-test artifacts (server JSONL, trace, screenshots, HAR) under `target/e2e-logs/<test-name>/`; failing request ids printed.
- [ ] Harness disk hygiene: `ci/e2e.sh` runs `scripts/disk-guard.sh` first; every harness container, volume, network and locally built image carries the label `pf.harness=1`; teardown is always `docker compose down -v --remove-orphans` (in a trap, so it also runs on failure or Ctrl-C); the harness reuses one image tag per commit instead of piling up untagged builds; artifacts are kept only on failure, and for the newest 5 runs.

## Plan refs
§5d Logs, Metrics, Health and alerting, Abuse prevention (rate limits); §3 Topology (ops listener, the ingress contract, hostnames); §2 Serving (leaked URLs: logs redact `/c/<…>/`); §5f the portability lane; §5h Safe defaults (`[unsafe]`); §3a and §4a.7 click budgets; §4a.6 error pages; §7 Operations; Slice 1 definition of done items 1 and 2; decision 52.

## Considerations
- `/readyz` never depends on the IdP: tying readiness to it would roll back deploys and show the maintenance page exactly when the product is fine.
- `:9090` is never routed through the ingress and still needs the token: local network is not trusted. The Caddyfile must not expose it.
- Fail closed on spoofing: a header from an untrusted peer is ignored entirely, not partially used. Rate limits key on that vetted address, otherwise everyone shares one bucket or anyone spoofs out of theirs.
- The rate-limit layer lives here so every later surface registers into one table instead of hand-rolling its own; the public-links bead owns the guest limits and the table-driven test across every registered route. The 8 MiB app-side body cap (413 `too_large` before auth) is the op-registry bead's; the Caddyfile's 8 MiB limit is the proxy's copy of the same number.
- The harness is vendor-free by construction; the later portability lane reuses it as is.
- The harness self-test needs no sign-in code: a dev-only stub route sets a `__Host-` test cookie. The Dex sign-in round trip (both Dex configs) is the identity bead's check; here the second config only has to boot and serve its discovery document.
- Real phones never block anything (decision 52): phones are Playwright's mobile projects and the iOS Simulator. The simulator shares the Mac's network and keychain tooling, so no certificate-error flags; the real-device checks are the non-blocking human-checks bead.
- Store-backed logs (`/data/logs/` segments, the log pipeline, Insights) come after Slice 1; stdout JSON is the only sink here, which is enough for every gate.
- `tests/fixtures/identity.toml` belongs to the store bead (`StaticDirectory`), which runs beside this one. The Dex static config is generated from that file (`tests/e2e/harness/gen-dex.sh`) so the two never drift; if it hasn't landed, reserve it through Agent Mail and write it exactly as the store bead specifies (the admin, two household members, an outsider, a disabled user; three groups).
- This bead owns the `/readyz` check registry and its three readiness probes (DB writable, blob store OK, disk headroom > 5 %); the Health/export bead adds `importing`, the backup rows and the Health page on top of them.

## Tests and logging
- `pf_obs::redact::tests::*` (unit + proptest: random caps and tokens in arbitrary strings never survive); obs crate tests `canary_logs.rs::canary_values_never_logged` (log kept at `target/test-logs/` on failure), `metrics_auth.rs`, `metrics_labels.rs::no_high_cardinality_labels`; `crates/partifactory/tests/health.rs` (`readyz_reports_failing_check`, `readyz_ignores_degraded`); `request_id_from_trusted_header`, `request_id_task_local_propagates`, `log_level_runtime_reload`.
- `pf_serve::ingress::tests::{xff_rightmost_untrusted, untrusted_peer_header_ignored, request_id_sanitised_or_generated}`; `crates/pf-serve/tests/ingress_contract.rs` asserts `event="http.request"` with `client_ip` and `request_id`; `crates/pf-serve/tests/ratelimit_layer.rs` (a registered self-test route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at threshold + 1, keyed per client address; `event="ratelimit.trip"` logged; `pf_rate_limited_total` increments; switching it off without the `[unsafe]` key fails `config check`).
- `tests/e2e/harness/self_test.spec.ts` (all four Playwright projects: TLS chain valid, `__Host-` cookie set, a `<name>-part.pf.test` host resolves, virtual authenticator attachable on the Chromium projects, click-budget helper fails an over-budget path), `tests/e2e/harness/second_dex.spec.ts` (the second Dex config boots and serves discovery), `tests/e2e/proxy_smoke.spec.ts` (Host routing, 60 s SSE hold, 8 MiB POST accepted and 8 MiB + 1 rejected, maintenance page with the upstream stopped, `:9090` unreachable through Caddy); `tests/device/ios-sim.sh self-test` opens the self-test page in the simulator and records its post and screenshot.

## Verification gate
- In the harness, on the binary built from `main`: `self_test.spec.ts` passes on `chromium-desktop`, `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop` against `https://parts.pf.test` with a valid TLS chain; `proxy_smoke.spec.ts` holds SSE 60 s through Caddy, accepts 8 MiB, rejects 8 MiB + 1, and shows the maintenance page with the origin stopped; `tests/device/ios-sim.sh self-test` on the Mac records the simulator's post and screenshot (attached to `verified`).
- On the running binary: `curl -s :9090/metrics` -> 401, with the token -> 200 with `pf_http_requests_total{route_class=...}`; a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` from an untrusted peer is ignored in the access line; the rate-limit self-test route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at threshold + 1.
- CI green on `main` with the nextest job and a new `e2e` harness job (`ci/e2e.sh`); the harness job uploads `target/e2e-logs/` on failure.
- Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="http.request"` lines carrying `request_id` and `client_ip`, and one `event="ratelimit.trip"` from the self-test route; the canary test finds no canary value.
- No regressions: every earlier gate test still passes. Evidence on close (SHAs, CI run ids, the smoke output, the simulator lane output, browser, simulator runtime and Caddy versions) with `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every request produces exactly one JSON access line (`event="http.request"`) with `request_id`, `route_class`, `status`, `latency_us`, `principal` (or null), `outcome` and `client_ip`; the log level changes at runtime without a restart.
- [ ] Canary token, cap and content values never appear in logs under the test suite (type redaction and the pattern layer, proptest over random caps and tokens).
- [ ] `/metrics` on `:9090` returns 401 without the token and exposes RED metrics per route class and per op with it; no metric carries a part name, principal or request id as a label.
- [ ] `/healthz` returns 200; `/readyz` returns 503 naming the failing check (DB, blobs or disk headroom), and a registered degraded check never causes 503.
- [ ] A spoofed client-IP header from an untrusted address is ignored; the right-most untrusted `X-Forwarded-For` hop is used from a trusted proxy; a trusted request-id header is kept when printable and ≤ 128 chars, else one is generated; the request id is echoed as a response header, appears in logs and on the error page, and is readable from the task-local for later propagation.
- [ ] A `governor` rate-limit layer keyed on the trusted client address (and on the principal once one is attached) exists with a route table later beads register into; a self-test route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at threshold + 1, logs `event="ratelimit.trip"`, increments `pf_rate_limited_total`, and switching the layer off without `[unsafe] rate_limits = "off"` fails `config check`.
- [ ] `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` is the only Caddy config in the repo, never exposes `:9090`, and the harness mounts it with only the cert paths overridden; it passes the smoke test (routing by Host, SSE survives 60 s, 8 MiB accepted and 8 MiB + 1 rejected, the maintenance page served with the origin stopped).
- [ ] Playwright projects `chromium-desktop`, `chromium-mobile` (phone viewport, touch, virtual authenticator), `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop` exist, and `harness/self_test.spec.ts` passes on all four over TLS at `https://parts.pf.test` with the per-run CA trusted (no certificate-error flags); a test part host `<name>-part.pf.test` resolves in every project.

title: Store core: SQLite, schema v1, blobs, versions, names, spaces and the part service
description:
## Goal
The storage foundation every later bead writes into: SQLite with one serialising writer, schema v1 exactly as the plan's data model, the content-addressed blob store, immutable versions, names, personal spaces and the part service, with idempotent writes. It also defines the provider-neutral identity traits and a static fixture directory, so every test signs in without a network. Constraints live in the database, so later beads can trust their invariants.

## Scope
- [ ] `pf-db`: rusqlite (bundled, FTS5), WAL, `foreign_keys=ON`, `synchronous=FULL` on the one writer task, `query_only` read pool, embedded forward-only migrations with a sha check (run at start inside a transaction), a second `Db` for `insights.db` with its own writer, `temp_db()` for tests.
- [ ] Schema v1: `0001_schema_v1.sql` (the §5e main DDL verbatim: identity, spaces, parts, names, tags, notes, versions, builds, blobs, `shared_blobs`, `mirror_cache`, `build_deps`, `advisories`, drafts, grants, public links, `epochs`, access asks, invites, audit, OAuth and agent connections, `idempotency`, leases, comments, data docs and snapshots, assets, `runtime_errors` and its keep trigger, the backend tables, events, webhooks, render jobs, `kv`, and `parts_fts` without triggers) and `insights/0001_insights_v1.sql`; `schema_test` with helpers and a golden snapshot.
- [ ] `pf-blobs`: `BlobStore` + local `/data/blobs/ab/cd/<sha256>`; temp -> fsync -> verify -> rename; idempotent concurrent puts; verify-on-read; stale-temp sweep; `DiskBudget` hook (a put asks the injected budget and returns `storage_full` when it reports full; the budget, 80 % of the volume by default with `full` at 95 % of it, is the retention bead's, so there is one disk rule, not two).
- [ ] Versions: JCS (RFC 8785) manifest whose hash is the version id; `commit_version` in the writer; head/live with `set_live_if_newer`; v0 placeholder; path rules (relative, normalised, no `..`, no duplicates) and the 2 MiB per source file cap (`too_large` with `details.limit`, §5d).
- [ ] Names: `[a-z0-9-]` 1-58, `blobs` reserved in code, `[names] reserved`, every name ever used reserved forever, `derive(title)`, deterministic ranked alternatives.
- [ ] Spaces: personal space per person, default space for a person or their agent, live-inherited space grants (`max(part, space)`), `effective_quota` (enforcement is the retention bead's), `move_part` bumps the epoch.
- [ ] Part service: create (all `part_create` fields, `check_only`, fork, `expires_in`, `snapshots`), the shared idempotency layer (contract Rule 1: replay returns the stored result with `replayed: true`; only a committed write uses up its id; different args under a committed id -> `request_id_reused`; rows kept 24 h, pruned by the janitor), get (version, <= 32 KiB content, `file`/`range`, history, diff), delete to the 30-day bin, undelete, restore as append, `expire_due_parts`.
- [ ] `pf-auth`: `Authn`, `Directory`, placeholder `Provisioner`; `StaticDirectory` from `tests/fixtures/identity.toml` (the admin, two household members, an outsider, a disabled user; three groups — the same identities the harness's Dex config seeds), `invalid_grant`/`Unreachable` switches, `TestSession::sign_in`.
- [ ] Dev-only subcommands (`dev` feature, never in release): `partifactory dev put|get|history|diff|delete|undelete|restore|fork|sign-in`, so the gate drives the running binary before the HTTP API exists.

- [ ] Preview columns in schema v1 (§5e, decision 53), so the preview work after Slice 1 needs no disruptive migration: `parts.preview` (JSON), `public_links.preview` (`video | image | card`, default `video`), `render_jobs.purpose` including `preview`, and the `part_previews` table.
- [ ] `pf-caps` (§2), here because both the identity bead (`/grant` mints) and the part host bead (the content listener verifies) need it and run in parallel: `v1.<kid>.<payload>.<mac>`, canonical CBOR payload ≤ 300 bytes, MAC truncated to 16 bytes, daily HKDF keys from `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY` accepting `kid` and `kid − 1`, deterministic 12 h windows with the last-hour roll-forward, 60 s for `render`, `EpochStore` over the `epochs` table (part, minter, global, boot floor bumped on every start), mint, and DB-free verify in the §2 order with a constant-time MAC compare. Property tests: host-bound, deterministic, last-hour roll-forward, epoch rejection, tamper, kid rotation (25 h).

## Plan refs
§2 The core idea, §3a Three layers and Spaces, §3d Creation contract, Idempotent, Durable when acknowledged, Linearisable writes, §3e Versions and the bin, §4 Names, §5c the `/data` layout, §5d Body and size caps, Disk pressure, Migrations, §5e Data model (principles, both DDL blocks), §5h; docs/agent-contract.md `part_create`, `part_get`, Rules 1 and 7.

## Considerations
- One writer makes `n` gap-free, rebase safe and "acknowledged = survives a power cut". No save waits on a backup target.
- Migrations run before the health-gated switch and must work with the previous binary; never edit `0001` once released. Bundled SQLite >= 3.45 (the plan's DDL is checked against 3.54); forward `REFERENCES` are fine.
- STRICT tables, prefixed ULID ids, unix-ms times, secrets only as sha256, JSON `json_valid`. No FTS triggers (search fills `parts_fts` in code). Backend tables exist now so P2a needs no disruptive migration.
- The blob store is filesystem-only; callers write `blobs` rows in their writer transaction. Shared vs part class belongs to the reference.
- The manifest includes `part_id`, `parent` and `n`: identical files in two parts never share an id. Every version is kept.
- Names are not secret; reserve forever because renames 301 forever. Never copy space grants onto parts. Slice 1 has personal spaces only.
- A part the caller can't see is `not_found`, never `forbidden`. Until the policy engine lands, tests use an allow-all fake.
- `config check` refuses the fixture identity in a release build. A failed refresh keeps the last membership; `invalid_grant` fails closed.
- This bead needs only the workspace and CI, so it runs beside the observability and harness bead. Its log lines use `tracing` JSON with the shared field names (`event`, `part_id`, `principal`, `outcome`); if the obs crate hasn't landed, `serve` installs a plain `tracing_subscriber` JSON layer that the obs crate replaces without changing any event.

## Tests and logging
- `pf_db::tests::{migrate_from_empty, migrate_from_n_minus_1 (a fixture 0002 proves the path), altered_migration_rejected, writer_gap_free_1000, pragmas_applied}`; `crates/pf-db/tests/schema_test.rs` (`ddl_matches_plan_snapshot`, per-block CHECK/FK/trigger tests, `insights_*`).
- `pf_blobs::tests::{concurrent_same_hash_idempotent, bitflip_detected_on_read, storage_full_from_budget_hook, stale_temp_swept}`; `pf_model::{manifest,version,names,spaces,create,read,lifecycle}::tests`; `crates/pf-model/tests/part_service.rs::lifecycle_end_to_end`; `crates/pf-auth/tests/no_network.rs`; `tests/e2e/store/durability.sh`.
- Logs asserted: `event="db.migrate" outcome="ok"`, `event="version.committed" part_id n`, `event="part.write" op replayed`, `event="blob.corrupt" hash`, `event="session.created" principal`.

## Verification gate
- On the `dev`-feature binary built from `main`, `tests/e2e/store/durability.sh` drives `partifactory dev` put/fork/restore/delete/undelete/history/diff against a running `partifactory serve` and shows the expected heads, history and diff; it then `kill -9`s the server mid-loop of acknowledged edits, restarts, and shows every acknowledged version present, `n` gap-free, every blob verifying.
- CI green on `main`: nextest job (`ci/test.sh`) with the pf-db, pf-blobs, pf-model and pf-auth tests, and the `store-durability` job (`ci/store-durability.sh`).
- Logs: `event="db.migrate" outcome="ok"` on first start, one `event="version.committed"` per acknowledged edit, no `event="blob.corrupt"`.
- No regressions: every earlier gate test still passes.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, script output before and after the kill, `ci_green` and `verified` reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Migrations apply from empty and from N-1 in a test; an altered released migration is rejected by its sha; 1,000 concurrent commits through the writer produce a gap-free sequence; the pragmas are applied on every connection.
- [ ] `schema_test` asserts every table, index, trigger and CHECK in both §5e DDL blocks exists (golden snapshot), using harness helpers for each block (identity, spaces, parts, names, tags, notes; versions, builds, blobs, grants, links, invites; agents, data, comments, assets, runtime errors; backends, events, webhooks, render jobs, `parts_fts`; insights), including the partial indexes `builds_queue`, `builds_cache`, `blobs_unref`, `grants_expiry`, `public_links_part`, `access_asks_open`, `invites_open`.
- [ ] CHECK rejections, identity and parts: `users` oidc without sub; `groups` managed non-`pf-` name; `groups` local unmanaged; `spaces` personal without owner; `parts` names `-a`, `a-`, `a--b`, `A`, 59 chars, `a_b`; `names` bad state; `part_notes` body > 16384.
- [ ] CHECK rejections, builds and access: bad `via`, bad build `status`/`method`/`target`/`gate_check`, invalid JSON in `warnings`/`errors`/`files`/`groups`/`before`/`after`, grant subject `link:x`, role 4, public link role 2 or mode `edit`, invite `uses > max_uses`, access ask note > 280 chars.
- [ ] CHECK rejections, agents and data: connection `person` without user; token kind `id`; shared doc with owner; doc body 262145 bytes; snapshot reason `manual`; asset size 26214401; comment provenance `guest`; lease scope `dir`.
- [ ] CHECK rejections, backends and the rest: `part_secrets` name `lower` and a 65-char name; container role `sidecar`; render purpose `screenshot`; webhook status `failed`; event payload invalid JSON.
- [ ] FK rejections: `version_files.blob_hash` to a missing blob; `builds.version_id` to a missing version.
- [ ] Trigger test: inserting 1,001 runtime errors for one part leaves 1,000 (the oldest by `last_at` dropped).
- [ ] `parts_fts` exists as an fts5 virtual table with the listed columns, and no trigger references it.
- [ ] The round-3 tables are asserted: `build_deps` (indexes `build_deps_build`, `build_deps_pkg`), `advisories` (the `ignored` state needs `ignored_by` and `reason`; `UNIQUE (build_id, ecosystem, package, version, osv_id)`), `builds.sbom_hash`, and both cascade when their build is deleted.
- [ ] `insights.db` loads from empty into a separate file with its own writer; `schema_test::insights_*` asserts every table, index and CHECK; no column in it is named like `ip`, `body`, `content` or `value` (supports the no-content-in-logs fuzz test's rule).
- [ ] Blobs: put/has/get round trip; concurrent put of the same hash is idempotent; a flipped byte on disk is detected on read (`event="blob.corrupt"`); a put returns `storage_full` when the injected `DiskBudget` reports full; stale temp files are swept.
- [ ] Golden manifest hashes are stable across runs; a one-line edit to a 40-file part writes exactly 1 blob + 1 manifest; a file over 2 MiB or a bad path is rejected (`too_large` with `details.limit`, `invalid_input`) and stores nothing.
- [ ] Names: the rule table test (length, hyphens, reserved list from site config); `blobs` is `name_taken` with no config; a retired name is rejected; `name_taken` returns >= 3 valid free suggestions.
- [ ] Spaces: a part created without `space` lands in the creator's personal space; a grant added to a space applies to its existing parts at once; `move_part` bumps the part epoch.
- [ ] Idempotency: a retried create with the same `request_id` returns the same part with `replayed: true`; with different args -> `request_id_reused`; a create rejected with `name_taken` stores nothing, and resending the fixed call with the same id succeeds.
- [ ] A fork writes zero new blobs and records `forked_from`.
- [ ] A no-files create returns `head: 0, live: null, build: null` in < 10 ms p99 (bench in test).
- [ ] Get: a 20 KiB single-file part returns its content; a 100 KiB part returns the file list, and a `range` returns exactly those lines; diff between v1 and v3 lists each changed file with correct `+/-` counts; an invisible part is `not_found`.
- [ ] Restore of v3 on a part at v5 creates v6 whose `version_files` equal v3's.
- [ ] Delete moves the part to the bin, bumps the part epoch and excludes it from list queries; undelete at 29 days works, at 31 days fails with `not_found`; `expire_due_parts` moves due scratch parts to the bin.
- [ ] Integration tests sign in as fixture users and groups without a network; `invalid_grant` fails closed and a failed refresh keeps the last membership.
- [ ] The fixture identity (`StaticDirectory`, `TestSession`) and the `partifactory dev ...` subcommands exist only with the `dev` feature: a release build has neither, and `config check` refuses the static directory.
- [ ] Schema v1 has `part_previews`, `parts.preview` (`json_valid`), `public_links.preview` (CHECK `video|image|card`, default `video`) and `render_jobs.purpose = 'preview'`; CHECK and FK cases tested like the other tables.
- [ ] `pf-caps`: a cap for part A never verifies for host B; the same subject, part, epochs and window give the same cap; a cap minted in a window's last hour uses the next window; bumping a part, minter, global or boot epoch rejects older caps; a rotated key verifies for 25 h then fails; a cap is ≤ 300 bytes; verify makes zero DB queries given a loaded `EpochStore`.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` (`dev` feature), `tests/e2e/store/durability.sh` drives `partifactory dev put/fork/restore/delete/undelete/history/diff` against a running `partifactory serve` and shows the expected heads, history and diff.
- [ ] GATE: The same script `kill -9`s the server during a loop of acknowledged edits, restarts it, and shows every acknowledged version present, `n` gap-free and every blob verifying.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the pf-db, pf-blobs, pf-model and pf-auth tests in the nextest job (`ci/test.sh`) and the `store-durability` script job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the run asserts `event="db.migrate" outcome="ok"` on first start, one `event="version.committed"` per acknowledged edit, and no `event="blob.corrupt"`.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: every earlier gate test still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence: commit SHAs, CI run id, the script output excerpt from before and after the kill, and passing `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.

title: The rest of P2: OAuth authorization code, comments, leases, blocks, notes, part_find, part_watch, agent sharing, Jig, the source editor and formatted view, live reload, Insights pages
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Finish P2, "agents + the household loop", on top of what Slice 1 shipped (tokens, device code, MCP, part_edit, part_check, shared data, contribute links). This epic adds what makes the loop daily: browser OAuth for MCP clients, comments for the agent, the event feed, inward sharing by agents, live reload, Jig, the source editor, renames, the Insights and debugging pages, and the Hermes skill. P2's Done-when (beyond the pixel test, which is Slice 1's exit) is reached here.

## Scope
- [ ] OAuth authorization code: `/oauth/authorize` with PKCE S256 only, `iss` (RFC 9207), `resource` = the workspace origin (RFC 8707); CIMD clients (fetched through the mirror egress guard), DCR (rate-limited, inert until consent, purged after 1 h), manual clients with a secret (admin area, step-up); consent sheet shows the redirect host and warns on a localhost CIMD redirect; joins conformance as the third auth kind.
- [ ] Leases (`part_edit {claim}`): part scope by default, file or block, TTL ≤ 10 min, checked inside the writer with rebase, released on commit or expiry; the person can always override (agents never force).
- [ ] Block ids for markdown: `.pf/blocks.json` in the manifest, three-pass carry-over (hash LCS, same-kind Jaccard ≥ 0.5, fresh id), block ops, `pf:pending` placeholders.
- [ ] Read path extras: agent notes (`part_notes`, ≤ 16 KiB, no new version), outline with symbols for large parts, `render: "text"`, `part_find` (FTS5 search from the rest of P1) with filters and "recent by me / this agent".
- [ ] Comments (`part_comments` + `/_rt comments.*`): threads, anchors, `to_agent`, resolve/reopen, `provenance`, `contains_untrusted`, MCP `<untrusted_content>` wrapper; link-viewer comments only with the per-part opt-in; the comments rail in the wrapper with "For the agent"; Details "Send to agent".
- [ ] Events for agents: `part_watch` long-poll (25 s default, 50 s max), `GET /api/v1/events` SSE with `Last-Event-ID` and 25 s heartbeat, `cursor_expired` after 30 days, HMAC-signed webhooks (config-only targets, retried).
- [ ] Agent sharing with `share:household`: inward grants and moves only, labelled "Hermes shared this", one-tap undo, "Undo all" on revoke; no outward path on any surface.
- [ ] The remaining `part_link_for` actions: `group`, `everyone`, `admin` (`invite` lands with P2b, `lan` with P2a).
- [ ] Jig: `jig.css` shared blob, `--jig-*` tokens, four presets, `@partifactory/jig`, Jig as a part in `system`, `design_system` op + contract section; markdown, text and code shells move from `pf-shell.css` to Jig.
- [ ] The workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6 (vendored shared blob), server drafts per (person, part), `d`-claim preview caps, diff3 merge with Resolve (Keep mine / Keep theirs / Edit), lease notice.
- [ ] The formatted view for Markdown and `text` parts (§4a.7, decision 54), after the source
editor: the default `Edit` mode for those kinds; ProseMirror + `prosemirror-markdown` vendored as a
shared blob; per-block editing islands so only touched blocks are re-serialised; an inline source
box for blocks it can't represent; autosave to the same server draft; commits as `replace_block` /
`insert_after` / `delete_block` with `if_hash` ("Edited in the page"); agent commits arriving in
place over `part_watch`; per-block Resolve; lease and `pending` placeholders; comment from a
selection; the editable text shell for `text`; the phone toolbar.
- [ ] Live reload: `pf:version` from the wrapper (or the prelude when standalone); silent reload, or a toast when personal state is unsaved.
- [ ] Renames: admin-confirmed with step-up, old host 301s forever with the query stripped, old name reserved, old caps die.
- [ ] Insights pages (Overview, Agents, Parts, People, Builds) over the Insights store; the debugging UI (trace waterfall, per-part Debug tab with denying decisions, per-agent call page, log viewer with live tail).
- [ ] Workspace activity feed and Shared with me.
- [ ] The Hermes skill: per-person pairing by device code, `part_check` before posting, comment relay, deep links.

## Plan refs
§3b (OAuth 2.1, agent sharing, revocation cascades), §3c, §3d (leases, long documents), §3e, §4 (ops table, events, no notifications), §4a.6 and §4a.7 (comments, editor, formatted view, budgets), §4a.8 Jig, §4b, §4c, §5g, §6 P2, §6a "The rest of P2", decisions 13, 14, 34, 36, 37, 54.

## Considerations
- Decision 37: auth code is after Slice 1; the slice's token service is already the AS token side, so this adds an endpoint, not a redesign. `share:household` is off by default for CIMD, DCR and manual clients; `backends:deploy` is off for every client.
- CIMD and mirror-on-build share one egress guard: https only, private/loopback/link-local refused after DNS resolution, ≤ 5 KiB, 3 s, no redirects.
- No CRDTs in v1; live co-typing is a deferred option (`yrs` inside one formatted-view session,
committing ordinary versions, decision 54), not part of this phase. Block ids live in the manifest so identity versions with content; anchors and lease refs hold ids as text, no FK.
- Comment bodies are content and never logged (the no-content fuzz test). "Untrusted for agents" is a reading aid shown to the owner.
- No approval queues: a deep link grants nothing and stores nothing pending; there is no request table (schema test).
- Jig must never look like the chrome (a part must never pass for the workspace); old parts keep loading their recorded `jig.css` hash.
- Insights and debug pages are admin-only. Non-admins get 403 (§7: only the pinned subject reaches admin), which supersedes an older 404 line. Guests appear only as counts; the per-agent page shows argument keys and sizes, never values. "Deep links acted on" = the matching share-sheet action by the admin on the same part within 7 days.
- Live reload coalesces events within 500 ms. partifactory never messages Telegram; Hermes treats `<untrusted_content>` as data.
- If the non-blocking Telegram passkey human check fails (decision 36), the Hermes skill's messages hint "open in browser" and the household sets Telegram to open links in the normal browser; the person-bound-link fallback stays rejected.
- The Agents page ships in the rest of P1; its "Undo all" is tested here, because agent sharing is what makes the grants it revokes.

## Order inside the phase
From §6a: OAuth authorization code; comments, leases, block ids, notes and `part_find` (after search in the rest of P1); `part_watch` and webhooks → the source editor → the formatted view; agent sharing → the Hermes skill; Jig; live reload; renames; the Insights pages (after the Insights store, traces and the log pipeline in the rest of P1) → the debugging UI; the remaining deep links.

## Verification gate
- P2's Done-when observed on the compose deployment, with a scripted Hermes and the phone steps on Playwright's mobile projects and in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (the by-hand run on the example deployment is the non-blocking human-checks bead's): a family member pairs with Hermes, asks for a packing list shared with the family, Hermes checks its render and posts the link, another family member opens it on a phone, comments, and watches the fix land; Claude Code connects with one passkey tap + Allow and edits a week-old part in one call.
- Formatted view: on the compose deployment, a person edits a Markdown part in the formatted view
(`chromium-desktop` and `webkit-mobile`) while a scripted agent fills a `pending` section with
`replace_block`; both land, the Compare view shows changes only in the blocks each touched, and the
e2e JSONL shows `event="editor.commit" mode="formatted"` with `blocks_changed`.
- Each child bead closes with its own gate; the e2e suite (including every Slice 1 gate test and `communal_pixel_editor`) is green on `main`.
- Logs: `event="op" op="part_watch"`, `event="live.switch"`, OAuth `event="oauth.token" grant_type="authorization_code"` asserted in the e2e runs.
- Evidence on close: the children's close evidence, the CI run id, and the engine and simulator runtime versions of the phone steps; `ci_green` and `verified` gates recorded.
