title: Public links and guests: admin-only links, Can view and Can contribute, part_link_for, guest limits, rate limits and freeze
description:
## Goal
Public links are the one way a part leaves the house, so only the admin makes them: unlisted, `noindex`, revocable, no expiry by default, counted. A **Can contribute** link turns each tab into a guest who writes the part's shared data and nothing else. This is how a signed-out phone paints the pixel board while the admin can roll back, reset or freeze, and how an agent hands its person the one tap it may not take itself (`part_link_for`).

## Scope
- [ ] `public_links` lifecycle: session-only handlers (no op, no agent surface), admin + fresh step-up, live version required; 128-bit token stored as sha256; expiry Never (default) / 1 / 7 / 30 days; `open_count` and `last_opened_at`; every create, mode change, revoke and undo audited.
- [ ] `GET /l/<token>` on the part host: the wrapper in public mode (title, no share or comments) with the content-free public card ("Anyone with the link") and a JS hop; no cap, no target URL, no `<meta refresh>`, `noindex` + `X-Robots-Tag`, byte-identical for every UA. While a link is active the part root carries the public card too. `POST /l/<token>/go` mints the `link:<id>` cap and is what counts an open.
- [ ] Revoke (minter epoch bump, then plain 404; 10 s undo re-grants), expiry (`410 · LINK EXPIRED`), and the admin **Public links** list (§4a.6: every live link, its part, created, expiry, open count, last opened, revoke) with the red "Revoke all public links" kill switch (hold to confirm 1 s, audited). `/p/<name>` on the workspace only 302s to the part host, the same for unknown names.
- [ ] Guests: `go` on a contribute link adds `dw` and a random guest id `g` ("Guest 4f2a"); with `dw`, shared `storage.*` reads and writes; without it, shared writes are `forbidden_view_only`; every non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) and any `/api` or `/mcp` request is 403; writes labelled `guest:<link>:<g>`; past the part's 5 MiB shared-data cap, `quota_exceeded`. A stale guest cap is never refreshed: the public-mode wrapper re-runs `go`, which after Freeze mints a view-only cap.
- [ ] Switching to Can contribute takes a `reason: contribute` snapshot (outside `keep`, via `take_snapshot` from the shared-data bead) and sets `shared_data_writers` to `viewers`; Freeze sets view mode and bumps the link's minter epoch (10 s undo restores contribute); `editors` while a contribute link is active freezes it (the shared-data bead's freeze hook). Roll back / Reset use the snapshot engine.
- [ ] Rate limits on the shared `governor` layer from the observability bead: register `/l/*`, the per-guest (60/min) and per-IP (300/min) `/_rt` write rows and the 600/min read row (the per-person write limit is the shared-data bead's), plus the §5d per-link request cap: one row keyed on the link across all its guests and IPs (the default is chosen here and documented in the route table); own the table-driven test over every route registered at the time it runs (`/grant`, `/api`, `/l/*`, `/_rt` here; `/oauth/*`, `/device`, `/mcp` and `part_check` join automatically when their beads land) at threshold + 1 with 429 + `Retry-After`; pre-auth body caps (§5d) on unauthenticated routes before any auth or DB work.
- [ ] Share sheet, Slice 1 rungs, inside the wrapper (480 px, a bottom sheet on phones): the ladder (inward rungs disabled), the amber admin-only public rung, live sentence, mode with the contribute copy ("Anyone with the link can use it. Only you and people you add can change it."), expiry, Copy, "opened N times · last …", Revoke with a 10 s undo toast, Roll back data (newest snapshot preselected) / Reset data / Freeze, "Data: view only", in-sheet step-up, guest edit counts ("14 guest edits today"). The audience chip shows `Public link` in amber once a link exists.
- [ ] `part_link_for {name, action: public_link | contribute}` -> `{action, url, who: "admin"}`; errors `invalid_input` (listing the actions that exist), `not_found`, `forbidden`; the sheet opens pre-filled from `#share=public` / `#share=contribute`, the fragment survives the `/grant` hop, nothing is saved until confirmed; no request table exists.
- [ ] The wrapper's "being made…" v0 placeholder cross-fades to REV 1 on the shared-data bead's `pf:version` event, with no reload (§4a.6). This is the first bead that has both the wrapper and the shared-data bead, so it owns the spec.

## Plan refs
§2 The link to post (public links, UA independence); §3a audience ladder, role x runtime matrix, who may write shared data, "Can contribute" public links, UX click budgets, admin step-up; §4 `part_link_for`, no approval queues; §4a.6 share sheet and admin Public links, §4a.7; §5d abuse prevention; §5e `public_links`; §7 Links and cards, Guests, Operations (rate limits); decisions 12, 31, 34, 43; agent contract `part_link_for`, "Who can write shared data", Rules 4-5.

## Considerations
- Public links are DB tokens, not HMAC caps: key rotation never touches them. Counting on the `go` POST keeps unfurlers from inflating counts.
- The guest id is a signed claim in the link cap: per tab, no cookie; a forged `g` fails the MAC and looks like not found (404).
- A guest never has more than a signed-in viewer, hence the `editors` -> freeze coupling. Freeze bumps the link's minter epoch, not the part epoch, so people's caps stay valid.
- Key limits on the client IP only from trusted proxies (ingress contract), else everyone shares one bucket or spoofs. The layer, and its `[unsafe] rate_limits` switch, ship with the observability bead (the retention bead's safe-defaults registry lists it); this bead adds the link and guest rows and proves the whole table.
- Lines that belong to neighbours stay there: the signed-out private card, clean address bar, reload without a hop, gallery open and chrome-API CORS fuzz are the wrapper bead's. This bead keeps the public-link variants of each (public card, `/l/` UA independence, public-link chip).
- The guest half also runs from Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (local lane, evidence attached to `verified`); real phones never block anything.
- Agent-token refusal on every surface needs agent connections and MCP; it is verified in the MCP, discovery and conformance bead, and again from outside in the Shipping bead's §7 run.

## Tests and logging
- Integration: `public_link_lifecycle.rs`, `admin_links.rs` (list, kill switch), `guest_wall.rs`, `guest_caps.rs` + proptest `guest_cap_never_grants_non_data`, `contribute_switch.rs`, `rate_limits.rs` (route x key x threshold, test clock), `preauth_body_caps.rs` (zero DB queries), `part_link_for.rs`, `schema_no_queue.rs`.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/share_sheet_public.spec.ts`, `share_sheet_contribute.spec.ts`, `contribute_link.spec.ts`, `deep_link_share.spec.ts`, `placeholder_crossfade.spec.ts`, with the shared click-budget helper (`tests/e2e/lib/budget.ts`) and light/dark/360 px snapshots; `tests/device/ios-sim.sh contribute-guest`.
- Logs asserted: `event="link.create|link.go|link.revoke|link.mode"` with `outcome` (and `mode` on `link.mode`), `event="stepup.verify"`, `event="epoch.bump" key="minter:link:<id>"`, `event="rt.op" principal="guest:..." outcome="forbidden"`, `event="ratelimit.trip"`; metric `pf_rate_limited_total`; never a cap or token.

## Verification gate
- Harness, binary from `main`: the admin on chromium-desktop (virtual authenticator) makes a Can-contribute link in 4 interactions + 1 biometric; a signed-out webkit-mobile guest opens it and paints, and the admin's tab shows it; the admin freezes and the guest's next write is refused; revoke gives 404.
- `curl` of `/l/<token>` with a bot and a browser UA gives byte-identical HTML with no cap; a guest cap gets 403 on `comments.*` and `/api`; the 61st guest write in a minute gets 429 with `Retry-After`.
- `part_link_for {name: "pixel", action: "contribute"}` over the CLI (`part <op> --json`) returns the `#share=contribute` URL, which opens the pre-filled rung after sign-in.
- CI green on `main`: these tests in the nextest job, the specs in the e2e harness job.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="link.go"`, `event="epoch.bump" key="minter:link:..."` and `event="ratelimit.trip"`.
- Simulator lane (evidence, not a CI check): the guest half in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator paints and is refused after Freeze.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Close with evidence: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, screenshot and trace paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A fresh browser with no session opens `/l/<token>` and sees the part; `open_count` increments by exactly 1 per `go` hop (an unfurler's GET counts nothing) and `last_opened_at` updates.
- [ ] The `/l/` HTML contains no cap, no hop-target URL and no `<meta refresh>`, carries `noindex` and `X-Robots-Tag`, and is byte-identical across bot and browser UAs; while a link is active the part root carries the public card ("Anyone with the link", no title, name or thumbnail), also byte-identical across UAs.
- [ ] Only the admin session with a fresh step-up can create a public link or switch one to Can contribute; without step-up `step_up_required` (403), in-sheet with no navigation (no `framenavigated` event on the top frame); a non-admin session gets 403 and never sees the `Anyone with the link` rung, even from a `#share=` deep link.
- [ ] Revoke: 2 interactions; the next `/l/` and `/c/` request with the link cap return 404 within seconds; Undo within 10 s restores the link (a fresh `go` works); with no undo it stays 404.
- [ ] The kill switch on the admin Public links list revokes every link and writes one audit row per link; the list shows each live link's part, created, expiry, open count and last opened.
- [ ] An expired link shows `410 · LINK EXPIRED`; `/p/<name>` on the workspace only 302s to `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, the same for an unknown name.
- [ ] Budgets (shared click-budget helper): Can view link + Copy 3 + 1 biometric; Can contribute link + Copy 4 + 1 biometric (step-up lapsed); Revoke 2; Freeze 2; Roll back data 3 (newest snapshot preselected); a failure prints the recorded interaction list.
- [ ] Switch to Can contribute → a snapshot row `reason=contribute` (not counted in `keep`) exists and `shared_data_writers='viewers'`; the sheet says so.
- [ ] Freeze → an already-open guest tab's next write fails, and a fresh `go` gets a view-only cap whose shared write is `forbidden_view_only`; Undo after Freeze restores contribute mode.
- [ ] Setting `editors` ("Data: view only") while contribute is active freezes the link and writes an audit row; the live sentence and data note update.
- [ ] A guest cap reads and writes shared data; each non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) and any `/api` or `/mcp` request from a guest gets 403; a Can-view cap's shared write is `forbidden_view_only`.
- [ ] 61st write in a minute from one guest → 429 with `Retry-After`; 301st from one IP across guests → 429; past the part's 5 MiB shared-data cap → `quota_exceeded`.
- [ ] Editing the `g` claim breaks the MAC → 404 (byte-identical to not found).
- [ ] The guest-edit count increments after guest writes; guest writes carry `guest:<link>:<g>` in events and come back `provenance: "link_viewer"`.
- [ ] A table-driven test over every route registered when it runs returns 429 with `Retry-After` at exactly threshold + 1 (routes added by later beads join the table automatically).
- [ ] Oversized unauthenticated bodies are rejected before any auth or DB work (no DB query, checked with the query counter).
- [ ] `part_link_for` returns `{action, url, who: "admin"}` for `public_link` and `contribute`; any other action is `invalid_input` listing the actions that exist; an unknown name is `not_found`; the link grants nothing (opened by a non-admin it shows the sheet without the public rung, and by someone without access the normal 403); there is no request table or queue to write to (schema test).
- [ ] Signed-out open of `#share=contribute` → sign-in → wrapper → the sheet opens on the contribute rung (the fragment survived the `/grant` hop); `#share=public` the same; nothing is saved until the admin confirms (2 interactions + 1 biometric).
- [ ] The audience chip shows `Public link` (amber, icon + words) once a link exists, and `Only me` again after revoke.
- [ ] The contrast test passes for the new states (amber and danger tokens), light and dark; 360 px snapshots of the sheet as a bottom sheet.
- [ ] `placeholder_crossfade.spec.ts`: a part opened while its first build runs shows the "being made…" placeholder, then cross-fades to REV 1 when `pf:version` arrives, with no reload and no second `/grant` hop.
- [ ] The per-link request cap (§5d) holds across every guest and IP of one link: past it, that link's requests get 429 with `Retry-After` while other links are unaffected.
- [ ] GATE: In the e2e harness on the binary from `main`, the admin (chromium-desktop, virtual authenticator) makes a Can-contribute link in 4 interactions + 1 biometric; a signed-out webkit-mobile guest opens it and paints, and the admin's tab shows it; the admin freezes and the guest's next write is refused; revoke then gives 404.
- [ ] GATE: `curl` of `/l/<token>` with a bot UA and a browser UA returns byte-identical HTML with no cap; a guest cap gets 403 on `comments.*` and `/api`; the 61st guest write in a minute gets 429 with `Retry-After`; `part_link_for {name: "pixel", action: "contribute"}` over the CLI returns the `#share=contribute` link and it opens the pre-filled rung after sign-in.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the guest, link, admin-links, rate-limit and part_link_for tests in the nextest job and the share-sheet, contribute and deep-link specs in the e2e harness job.
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="link.go"`, `event="epoch.bump" key="minter:link:..."` and `event="ratelimit.trip"` log lines, and no line contains a cap or link token.
- [ ] GATE: Simulator lane: a signed-out guest in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator opens `/l/<token>`, paints, and is refused after Freeze (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh contribute-guest`), with posts, screenshots and the runtime version attached to the `verified` report.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, every earlier bead's gate tests included, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence: commit SHAs, CI run id, gate command excerpts, Playwright screenshot and trace paths; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.

title: Health, export and import: the Health page, /readyz, nightly export, import with the boot-epoch bump, the regrant helper
description:
## Goal
One place where the admin sees whether the box is healthy, and a `/data` that restores: an hourly consistent DB copy, a nightly `partifactory export` with nothing configured, and `partifactory import` that brings it back anywhere and kills every cap minted before it. The server is left alone for years, so the backup must exist before anyone asks; **no save ever waits on a backup target**. The Health page is where definition-of-done item 6 becomes visible: every store against its cap, the backup layers and the disk budget.

## Scope
- [ ] `/readyz` on the ops listener (`:9090`), extending the observability bead's check registry from a skeleton to real probes: DB writable (a write through the single writer), blob store OK (probe put/has/get), disk headroom > 5 %, `importing=true` → 503; body `{ready, checks, degraded}`. IdP reachability, directory staleness and backup freshness are **degraded rows, never readiness**. That registry becomes the one `HealthCheck` trait shared by `/readyz`, the Health page, later `doctor` and the alert webhook. Probes < 50 ms.
- [ ] Admin Health page `/admin/health` (admin pin, no step-up to read; chips are icon + words): the `/readyz` checks, degraded rows (IdP, directory poll), backup layers (host snapshots on/off/unknown from `backup.host_snapshots`; newest export age, size, same-disk flag), disk use naming the biggest spaces and parts, the disk budget row and every store against its cap and the safe defaults switched off (rendered from the retention bead's store-cap and safe-defaults registries), quota hits (the retention bead's deduplicated entries), 5xx spikes, version, last drill (filled by the Shipping bead), break-glass uses, runtime log level (changed here through the observability bead's reload handle; audited).
- [ ] Hourly `VACUUM INTO backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite.tmp` → `integrity_check` → fsync → rename; failure keeps the previous copy and raises staleness.
- [ ] `partifactory export` → `partifactory-<ts>.tar.zst`: `MANIFEST.json` (format version, created, binary version, counts, a sha256 per entry), consistent `db.sqlite`, every referenced blob (from the retention bead's blob-GC mark function, so the two can't disagree), `--parts-only` (part manifests, files, notes, titles, spaces by slug and tags as JSON; no access records, tokens or people), `--encrypt` (age recipient; the box never holds the identity), `--include-insights`, `--include-secrets` (needs `--encrypt`). Temp file, fsync, rename.
- [ ] Nightly export on by default to `/data/exports`, keep 7 (`backup.export_schedule|export_dir|export_keep`); registers its rotation as a janitor job (keep `export_keep`, never delete the only export), its "Scheduled exports" row in the store-cap registry with a fill-past-cap case, and its "nightly export" entry in the safe-defaults registry (off needs `[unsafe]`); newest export time/size in `kv` and metrics; same-filesystem detection by `st_dev`.
- [ ] `partifactory import <file>`: verify every entry before writing anything, load `db.sqlite` + forward migrations, blobs temp → fsync → rename, **bump the boot epoch**, serve with `importing=true` until blobs verify; `--force` moves the old DB aside; records `kv.import_at` (the token service suspends refresh-reuse detection for 24 h after it). Parts-only import recreates history, author labels and timestamps (placeholder users), with no grants, tokens or sessions.
- [ ] `partifactory import regrant --plan` / `--apply plan.json`: proposes grants by stored audience names (groups by name, people by username or email); the one-screen UI comes later.

## Plan refs
§5c Backups, recovery and self-provisioning (layers, export, import, data snapshots in exports); §5d Health and alerting; §5h (Health rows, scheduled exports, safe defaults); §4a.6 Admin (Health); §2 Keys (boot-epoch floor); §3a (fail open on an unreachable IdP); §7 Identity and admin (IdP down), Operations (parts-only export); Slice 1 definition of done items 5 and 6; decisions 17, 33.

## Considerations
- Readiness never depends on the IdP, or an IdP outage would roll back deploys and show the maintenance page while the product works.
- `/data` + export, not git, Litestream or a streaming sink (round 2; Litestream v0.5 dropped age). `VACUUM INTO` reads a WAL snapshot without blocking the writer. Host rsync-style copies must take the hourly file, never the live `.db`.
- age to a public recipient: the identity lives offline with the site config.
- An export on the same disk as `/data` is amber, never green; no export in 48 h is amber too.
- The boot-epoch bump is what makes restoring an old DB safe; cost: one silent re-grant per open tab.
- Every condition the later alert webhook mirrors is already a Health row (budget 80 %, store 80 % of cap, no export 48 h, crash-loops, IdP down 10 min).
- Runs after the retention bead, so the page renders real budget and store rows (no reserved placeholders) and export reuses GC's mark function instead of a second walk. The `storage_full` wrapper check lives here because this bead is the first of the two that has the wrapper upstream.
- Moved to the Shipping bead: the drill (needs the image) and the refresh-reuse-after-import line (needs the token service deployed); this bead still records `kv.import_at`.

## Tests and logging
- `pf_obs::health::tests::*`, `crates/partifactory/tests/health_page.rs::{rows_cover_alert_conditions, store_rows_match_registry}`, `idp_down_readyz_200_degraded_row` (Dex stopped).
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/{hourly_copy.rs, export_during_burst.rs, nightly_default.rs, roundtrip.rs::full_export_import_identical, roundtrip.rs::old_caps_dead_after_import, parts_only_import.rs, regrant.rs}`; the `exports` case in the retention bead's `retention_table.rs`; `tests/e2e/health_page.spec.ts` (admin view, budget-full red row with the wrapper still opening a part).
- Logs asserted: `event="health.check" name="idp" outcome="degraded"`, `event="backup.copy" outcome=…`, `event="export.finished" outcome="ok" entries=<n> bytes=<b>`, `event="import.verify"`, `event="import.boot_epoch_bump" new_floor=<n>`, `event="import.finished"`, `event="cap.verify" outcome="stale_boot"`, `event="janitor.job" store="exports"`. Metrics `pf_ready`, `pf_backup_copy_last_success_timestamp_seconds`, newest export age.

## Verification gate
1. Binary from `main` in the e2e harness: the admin opens `https://parts.pf.test/admin/health` and sees readiness, backup-layer, disk-budget and per-store rows; with Dex stopped `curl :9090/readyz` is 200 with a degraded IdP row; with the loopback volume at 95 % of the budget the budget row is red while the wrapper still opens a part.
2. A test-clock nightly export imported into a fresh data dir brings back every part, version, data doc and snapshot; a pre-export cap gets 302/401 and a fresh `/grant` works.
3. CI green on `main`: the tests above in the nextest job, `health_page.spec.ts` in the e2e job.
4. The run asserts `event="import.boot_epoch_bump"` and `event="export.finished" outcome="ok"`.
5. The full e2e suite, every earlier gate included, still passes.
6. Close with SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts and the Health screenshot path; `ci_green` and `verified` recorded via `br gate report`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] DB unwritable, blob store unreadable, or disk headroom ≤ 5 % -> `/readyz` 503 naming the failing check; IdP down -> `/readyz` still 200 with a degraded row, existing sessions keep working and no epoch is bumped; the IdP is never a readiness check.
- [ ] Non-admin, including an IdP-admin user, gets 403 on `/admin/health`; the admin reads it without step-up.
- [ ] Health shows the backup layers (host snapshots on/off/unknown, newest export age, size and same-disk flag: amber when on the same disk, amber with no export in 48 h), quota hits, last drill and break-glass uses; a runtime log-level change takes effect without restart and writes an audit row.
- [ ] Every store in the retention bead's registry appears on Health with size against cap (amber ≥ 80 %, red ≥ 100 %) next to the disk budget row, and every safe default switched off shows as a warning; every condition the ops-alert webhook will cover already shows as a Health row.
- [ ] At 95 % of the disk budget (loopback volume) the budget row is red while the wrapper still opens a part.
- [ ] After an hour (test clock), the copy exists, opens, and passes `integrity_check`; a copy taken while the writer commits 1,000 versions is prefix-consistent (every version row has its `version_files`); a failed copy leaves the previous file intact and raises the staleness metric.
- [ ] Every manifest entry hash verifies; `db.sqlite` integrity ok; the export's blob set equals the GC mark set on a fixture with versions, builds, drafts, snapshots and assets.
- [ ] An export taken during a write burst imports to an identical part set.
- [ ] A parts-only export contains no grants, tokens, sessions or people (schema test over the forbidden keys).
- [ ] `--include-secrets` without `--encrypt` exits 2; an encrypted export decrypts only with the matching identity; without `--include-secrets --encrypt` no part secret is ever in an export.
- [ ] A fresh install with no `[backup]` section produces one export per night and exactly 7 files after 9 days (test clock), never deleting the only one; the `exports` fill-past-cap case passes in the retention test.
- [ ] `kv` and metrics reflect the newest export; the same-disk flag is true in the default layout.
- [ ] Removing the schedule without the `[unsafe]` key fails `config check`; with it, Health shows a warning.
- [ ] Import of a full export restores every part, version, data doc and data snapshot (row-for-row equality on a fixture; blob hashes verified), and records `kv.import_at`.
- [ ] A cap minted before the export returns 302 (navigation) / 401 (subresource) after import (`cap.verify outcome="stale_boot"`); a fresh `/grant` works.
- [ ] A corrupted member (flipped byte) aborts with exit 3 before anything is written to `/data`.
- [ ] `/readyz` reports `importing=true` (503) until blob verification completes, then 200.
- [ ] Parts-only import recreates history and author labels; no grants, tokens or sessions exist afterwards.
- [ ] `--force` is required over a non-empty `/data` and preserves the old DB file.
- [ ] On a fixture (3 parts, 2 people, 1 group, one unknown person) `--plan` proposes exactly the matching grants, lists the unknown label as unmatched, and creates no grant.
- [ ] `--apply` creates those grants with audit rows; re-applying is a no-op; the asker can open the part on the next request.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness, the admin opens the Health page and sees readiness, backup-layer, disk-budget and per-store rows; with Dex stopped `/readyz` is 200 with a degraded IdP row; at 95 % of a loopback volume's budget the budget row is red and the wrapper still opens a part.
- [ ] GATE: A test-clock nightly export imported into a fresh data dir brings back every part, version, data doc and snapshot, and a pre-export cap is dead (302/401) while a fresh `/grant` works.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with `crates/pf-backup/tests/*`, the health tests (nextest job) and `tests/e2e/health_page.spec.ts` (e2e job).
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="import.boot_epoch_bump"` and `event="export.finished" outcome="ok"`.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with commit SHAs, CI run id, gate commands with output excerpts and the Health page screenshot path; `ci_green` and `verified` recorded with `br gate report`.

title: P2a Backends: the runner, builds, lifecycle, routing, data and secrets, the backend contract and the backend pixel test
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
A part becomes a page plus, optionally, containers (decision 28): a Dockerfile, a registry image or an uploaded image in a small compose subset, built by the server, health-gated per version, routed under the cap with a signed identity header, and walled off from the LAN. Only a runner sidecar holds the Docker/Podman Engine API.

## Scope
- [ ] **Runner spike** (`docs/spikes/runner.md`, `docs/spikes/runner/run.sh docker|podman`): rootless BuildKit in a container; drop rules in `DOCKER-USER` and a runner-owned nftables table (netavark); the runner's privileges (`NET_ADMIN` + host netns); `postgres` under the template; a per-volume disk limit; the pinned SBOM scanner image running under the template (the Syft-or-Trivy choice itself is the advisories spike's, `docs/spikes/advisories.md`, §3h).
- [ ] **The runner**: `partifactory runner` (`bollard`), fixed API `build/deploy/start/stop/logs/stats/prune` with `PF_RUNNER_KEY`, containers only from one hardened template; behind the `backends` profile in `deploy/compose.yaml`, the only service mounting the socket.
- [ ] **Networks**: a bridge network per part; egress on and metered; private, CGNAT, link-local, ULA, `[backends] household_subnets`, host and sibling ranges dropped for containers and builds; allowlist accept rules; denied attempts counted; `docs/backends-network.md`; a `doctor` check.
- [ ] **Sources and builds**: the closed compose subset; op-time allowlist scan of `image:` and Dockerfile `FROM`; rootless BuildKit (10 min, 2 CPU / 4 GiB, 10 GiB LRU cache); digests pinned; `POST /api/v1/images` + `part put --image`; build records `target=backend`.
- [ ] **Backend SBOMs and base images (§3h)**: an image SBOM per build from the pinned scanner (`builds.sbom_hash`, 5 MiB cap); a nightly base-image tag re-resolve (`base_image_checks`).
- [ ] **Backends join advisories (§3h)**: the advisories epic's nightly matching extended to stored SBOMs; `update` re-resolving base-image tags; backend severity context and the critical-backend ops webhook; backend auto-update defaulting to `patch` with the automatic code-only rollback. The advisory source, matching engine and surfaces are the advisories epic's.
- [ ] **Lifecycle**: a container set per live version; 60 s health gate; 30 s drain; scale to zero (10 s hold, 15 min idle), `always_on`, cron; crash-loop detection (5 in 10 min); `restore: n` starts version n's images.
- [ ] **Routing**: `/c/<cap>/api/*` with the content verifier and role matrix; strip cap, `Cookie`, `pf_` tokens, incoming `X-PF-*`; add `X-PF-Identity` (HS256, per-part HKDF key, 60 s) and `X-PF-Request-Id`; HTTP, WebSocket, SSE.
- [ ] **Data, secrets, permissions**: volumes (`/data/parts/<id>/vol/<svc>`, 1 GiB) exported via hook or stop-copy-start; write-only secrets; `backends:deploy` (off by default); quotas; `part_edit {backend}`, `part_get {backend: true}`; LAN allowlist (admin, step-up) and `part_link_for {action: "lan"}`.
- [ ] **The backend contract** in `docs/agent-contract.md`, in the change that ships backends, with the identity verifier snippet.
- [ ] **Observability and retention**: log rings (50 MiB, 7 days), restarts, cold starts, CPU/memory, egress, denied LAN on the Backends page and Debug tab; image pruning (live + previous 2), cache prune, retention-test rows.
- [ ] **The §7 Backends suite** on Docker and Podman, and **`communal_pixel_editor_backend`**.

## Plan refs
§3f, §3g, §3h layer 3 and Phasing, §5e, §5f portability lane (Podman pass), §5g, §5h, §6 P2a, §6a, §7 Backends, decisions 28, 29, 34, 48, 49, 51.

## Considerations
- **Rollback is best effort; a backend's data is its own agent's business (decision 51).** Volumes belong to the part and every version shares them; a restore brings back code only. partifactory guarantees two things: the code is exactly what it was built from, and a version never goes live unless its health check passes (else `backend_unhealthy`, and the current set keeps serving). It runs no migrations, down-migrations or data rollbacks. Data snapshots never cover volumes; folder backups and exports do. Tests say so, so nobody "fixes" it into data rollback.
- **The backend contract**: migrate forward with additive changes; versions overlap during the 30 s drain (and a restored version meets the newest data), so read from storage per request and lock writes; back up before a non-additive change (e.g. `pg_dump` into the volume) and say so in the edit message; exit promptly on SIGTERM.
- The template is a code constant the runner enforces itself (UID ≥ 10000, no socket, host network, devices or extra mounts; optional `runsc`).
- The health wait runs outside the single writer; only the live flip commits inside it (§3d).
- Revocation is checked before any byte reaches the backend. Backend log text is untrusted: escaped, admin-only.
- Never prune an image a running set uses; older restores rebuild, re-pull by digest, or report the tarball is needed.
- Pin `postgres:<major>` by digest, mirrored into a local CI registry; fall back to a tiny `FROM postgres` Dockerfile if the template breaks it.
- Without a runner, backend parts fail with `backends_unavailable` (503); frontends are unaffected.

## Order inside the phase
Runner spike → runner (after the Slice 1 deliverable) → backend builds → lifecycle → routing (after Can-contribute links; request ids exist from the observability bead, their trace propagation from the rest of P1) and data, secrets and permissions → the backend security suite and `communal_pixel_editor_backend`. SBOMs and base-image checks come with the runner; joining backends to advisories comes after the advisories epic (it supplies the scanner choice and the matching engine). The backend Insights pages and the Debug tab lines need the P2 Insights and debugging UI (the rest of P2): they land when both exist, and §6a lets the runner lane start before that.

## Verification gate
- `communal_pixel_editor_backend` passes on the binary built from `main` in the compose deployment, on Docker and Podman and in the portability lane: one `part_edit` adds a Postgres leaderboard, guests' counts show live, a restore brings back the previous code with volume rows intact, and the backend reaches a public canary but not the LAN canary.
- CI green on `main` with the Docker and Podman backend jobs and the §7 Backends suite.
- Logs checked: `event="runner.refused"`, `event="runner.lan_denied"`, `event="backend.set"`, `event="backend.proxy"`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, every Slice 1 gate and `communal_pixel_editor` still pass.
- Every resulting bead closes with evidence and the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/spikes/runner.md` exists with a pass/fail row per item per host and the versions tested.
- [ ] A runnable example (script under `docs/spikes/runner/`) reproduces each result.
- [ ] An explicit go/no-go with the chosen mechanism for and against each option, feeding the network rules and the backend builds.
- [ ] Every template field is visible in `inspect` on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] Table-driven refusals: privileged, cap_add, host network, bind mount outside the part's volume, device, socket mount, root user override attempts.
- [ ] Bad or missing `PF_RUNNER_KEY` -> 401-equivalent refusal; no Engine call made.
- [ ] `runsc` runtime is used when configured.
- [ ] Public canary reachable from a part container and from a build; LAN canary, host, metadata IP and sibling part unreachable; on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] An allowlisted target is reachable and nothing else is.
- [ ] Denied attempts are counted per part.
- [ ] Rules restored after runner restart.
- [ ] `docker compose --profile backends up -d` (and the default shipped file) starts the runner; `docker inspect` shows log limits; only the runner mounts the socket.
- [ ] With the runner stopped, a backend op returns `backends_unavailable` (503) and frontends keep serving.
- [ ] Table test: every listed unsupported key and a random unknown key → `compose_unsupported_key` with the supported set.
- [ ] `FROM evil.example/x` and `image: evil.example/x` → `image_not_allowed` at op time; `image: postgres:16` passes with the default allowlist.
- [ ] A Dockerfile part builds and records its digest with `server_build`; the log is retrievable.
- [ ] A build still running at 10 min (shortened via config in tests) is killed → `build_timeout`; the same holds on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] A build cannot reach a LAN canary but can reach a public one.
- [ ] An allowlisted `image:` resolves to a digest and deploys as `prebuilt_image`.
- [ ] `part put --image app.tar` uploads (≤ 2 GiB, quota-counted) and deploys as `uploaded_image`; 2 GiB + 1 → `too_large`.
- [ ] `/openapi.json` lists the images route; the bijection test passes.
- [ ] Failing health check → `backend_unhealthy` with 50 log lines, `live` unchanged, old set still answers.
- [ ] Healthy new set → live flip; old set `stopped` after 30 s; writer commit latency unchanged during the 60 s wait (test).
- [ ] Idle 15 min → stopped; next request cold-starts < 3 s on the CI box; `cold_starts` incremented.
- [ ] `always_on` never stops; cron fires on schedule while scaled to zero and skips on overlap.
- [ ] 5 restarts in 10 min → `backend.crashloop` once (not per restart).
- [ ] Restoring the previous version brings its backend back with the same digest; volume data intact.
- [ ] Restoring a pruned `server_build` version rebuilds; a pruned `uploaded_image` version reports that the tarball is needed.
- [ ] Revoked/expired/foreign-host cap never reaches the backend.
- [ ] Header stripping table test passes (Cookie, Authorization with pf_ token kept/removed correctly, X-PF-*).
- [ ] Claims correct per subject kind; JWT signed with another part's key rejected by the example backend; a forged incoming header replaced.
- [ ] WebSocket echo and SSE stream round-trip through the proxy from a sandboxed page.
- [ ] A cold request is held and served once healthy (< 3 s on CI); > 10 s -> 503.
- [ ] Bodies > 8 MiB -> 413 `too_large`.
- [ ] Export of a running Postgres part imports with rows intact (hook path) and a hook-less service round-trips via stop-copy-start.
- [ ] A secret set by an agent is injected (the backend sees it) and no op, surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI, UI, chrome API) returns its value; canary value absent from logs, traces, `insights.db`, `/metrics`, versions and a default export.
- [ ] Agent without scope -> `forbidden {scope_needed}` on a `compose.yaml` edit; with scope, succeeds.
- [ ] A deploy past the global memory quota fails with `quota_exceeded {kind: "memory"}`.
- [ ] Admin adds an entry with step-up; the target becomes reachable; revoking closes it.
- [ ] Every surface refuses agent attempts; the deep link opens the sheet pre-filled; a non-admin sees the normal 403.
- [ ] A crash-looping backend shows its restarts and last log lines in the Debug tab and raises the ops alert; denied LAN attempts are counted per part
- [ ] Each backend row of the §5h table has a passing fill-past-cap case; the live version's image is never pruned
- [ ] Every §7 Backends line is an automated test, run on Docker and on Podman, against staging and in the portability lane
- [ ] `communal_pixel_editor_backend` passes in CI on Docker and on Podman, and in the portability lane: a leaderboard service on Postgres, built by the server, live for guests, rolled back (code only) with its version, and walled off from the LAN
- [ ] Rollback restores code only (decision 51): after a restore the volume still holds the newest data, partifactory runs no migration, down-migration or data rollback, and a version that can't run against today's data fails its health check with `backend_unhealthy` while the current set keeps serving (test).
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` gains the backend contract in the change that ships backends: migrate forward with additive changes; read from storage per request and lock writes, because versions overlap during the 30 s drain; back up before a non-additive change and say so in the edit message; exit promptly on SIGTERM.
- [ ] Each backend build stores an image SBOM from the runner's one pinned scanner image, the one the advisories spike chose (`docs/spikes/advisories.md`) (`builds.sbom_hash`, capped at 5 MiB per build, pruned with its build); the runner spike records that it runs under the template on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] A nightly runner job re-resolves each base-image tag a backend build used and records "a newer digest exists" (`base_image_checks`) without rebuilding or changing any live part.
- [ ] Backends join advisories (§3h): nightly matching over stored SBOMs writes `advisories` rows for backend builds; a backend advisory raises severity one level and a critical one fires the ops webhook; `part_edit {rebuild: true, update}` re-resolves base-image tags within the range.
- [ ] Backend auto-update defaults to `patch` (decision 49, provisional): it acts only on an advisory with `fixed_in`, through the `after_check` gate, is recorded as `system`, and rolls back automatically when the check fails.
- [ ] An auto-update rollback restores the backend's code only, best effort (decision 51): no volume, migration or data rollback happens, and a version that fails its health check against today's data stays off `live` with `backend_unhealthy`.
- [ ] GATE: `communal_pixel_editor_backend` passes on the binary built from `main` in the compose deployment on Docker and on Podman and in the portability lane: one `part_edit` adds a Postgres leaderboard, guests' counts show live, a restore brings back the previous code with volume rows intact, and the backend reaches a public canary but not the LAN canary.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the Docker and Podman backend jobs and the §7 Backends suite (`tests/security/backends/`) in them.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e runs assert `event="runner.refused"`, `event="runner.lan_denied"`, `event="backend.set"` and `event="backend.proxy"` lines.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test and `communal_pixel_editor`, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Every bead this epic becomes closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run, gate command output) and `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.

title: Shared data and live events: window.storage over /_rt, data.changed, snapshots and part_data
description:
## Goal
Give a part shared state that everyone allowed can write, with open pages repainting live when someone else writes, and a one-action undo for bad writes. `window.storage` (Claude's artifact API, plus paging and `getMany`) runs over `/_rt`; the append-only `events` log feeds `/_rt/events` SSE; per-part data snapshots are on by default; agents read, write and roll back the same documents with `part_data`. This is the pixel board's data layer, on the Slice 1 critical path.

## Scope
- [ ] `/_rt` `storage.get/getMany/set/delete/list` on the `/_rt/v1` dispatch the part host bead built (a direct dependency, since the registry bead no longer waits for the part host) (text/plain JSON over `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1`, never a preflight): it extends that bead's personal `get/set/delete` with `getMany` and `list` paging, and adds the shared scope (`owner = ''` in `data_docs`, collection `__storage`, key = `doc_id`). Link viewers and guests have no personal scope (memory only).
- [ ] Authorisation from the cap's role, `dw` claim and `parts.shared_data_writers` (`viewers` default; `editors` = "Data: view only"): `forbidden_view_only` (403) for view/comment grantees on an `editors` part and for a Can-view link always. Expose the freeze hook for a contribute link when a part goes `editors` (the public-links bead consumes it).
- [ ] The §3a limits with exact codes and statuses: `invalid_input` 400 (key 1–512 bytes of UTF-8, no control characters), `too_large` 413 (value > 256 KiB), `quota_exceeded {kind}` 429 (5 MiB shared per part; the 256 KiB personal cap is the part host bead's), `rate_limited` 429 + `retry_after` (600 writes a minute per signed-in person per part, 600 reads a minute per viewer per part, where a `getMany` or `list` page counts as one), `forbidden_view_only` 403, `forbidden` 403, `storage_full` 507. Rows go into the shared rate-limit layer; guest/IP write rows plug in from the public-links bead.
- [ ] Prelude `window.storage` with Claude's exact signatures (`get(key, shared?)` → `{key, value, shared}` or `null`; `list(prefix, shared?, {cursor, limit ≤ 1000, values})`, where the options object may stand in for `shared`; `getMany(keys ≤ 500, shared?)`), `PfError {code, message, retryable, retry_after?}` rejections, and `partifactory.on("data.changed", fn)` over one shared `EventSource`, self-echo suppressed by a per-tab writer id, reconnect with backoff through the regrant path.
- [ ] `/_rt/events` on top of the builds bead's `events` append and per-part broadcast: `GET /c/<cap>/_rt/events` cap-authenticated like `/_rt/v1` (`Origin: null` only), 25 s heartbeat, `pf:version {n, live}` when live moves and per-key `data.changed {key, op, by: {kind, name}}` appended inside the data write's transaction; a lagging consumer gets `pf:resync`. Events carry keys, never values. Pruning at 30 days is a janitor job (retention bead).
- [ ] Data snapshots of shared docs: no policy row = `daily` keep 7 from the first shared write, `hourly` keep 48, `off`; the scheduled taker skips unchanged days and stops taking after 90 days unopened; on-demand snapshots (`contribute`, `before_restore`, `before_reset`) via `take_snapshot(part, reason)`; snapshots are canonical-JSON part blobs; roll back and reset are atomic, snapshot first, one `data.changed` per affected key; the current shared data downloads as canonical JSON. Pruning by `keep` and the keep-the-last-one rule are janitor jobs (retention bead); the taker registers with the janitor when it lands.
- [ ] `part_data` op: `get/list/set/delete/snapshot_list/snapshot_restore/reset` with the contract's fields, outputs and errors; `if_rev` CAS (`0` = must not exist, `if_match_failed` with `current_rev`); `provenance` + `contains_untrusted`; `request_id` idempotency through the part service's layer; `data:read`/`data:write` for get/list and set/delete; snapshot actions need `parts:write` + the person's `edit` role and act on shared data only.

## Plan refs
§2 Runtime calls `/_rt`, the prelude; §3a role × runtime matrix, who writes shared data, "Can contribute" limits; §3c Persistent state, prompt-injection hygiene; §3d Data (`rev` CAS); §4 Events, Slice 1 op fields (`part_data`); §4b errors; §5c Data snapshots; §5e `data_docs`, `events`, `data_snapshot_policies`, `data_snapshots`; §5h; decisions 26, 31, 43; docs/agent-contract.md "Shared data from inside a part", `part_data`, Rule 6, the worked session.

## Considerations
- Claude's exact signatures are what let copied artifacts run unchanged; a missing key resolves `null`.
- Track shared bytes with a per-part counter in the writer, never `SUM()` per write.
- Per-key `data.changed` on roll back means pages repaint with no special path.
- Snapshots undo bad writes, they are not DR; never personal docs, never backend volumes. Their blobs are part blobs, so GC and export keep them.
- Under `storage_full`, roll back and reset are refused too (they snapshot first); say so in the hint.
- Read the sandbox spike's item 12 (SSE through Caddy with a 25 s heartbeat, the proxy settings needed) before building `/_rt/events`.
- The wrapper's "being made…" placeholder cross-fading to REV 1 consumes the `pf:version` event this bead emits; the wrapper bead draws the placeholder and the public-links bead (the first with both this bead and the wrapper) owns its cross-fade spec, so this bead doesn't wait on the wrapper.
- Can-view link, guest and render principals in tests use test-minted caps (`partifactory dev cap`); the real link and guest flows are the public-links bead. Agent calls use the dev token until agent connections land; scope checks are table-tested with constructed principals.

## Tests and logging
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_storage_ops.rs` (matrix, limit codes and statuses, paging, `getMany`, concurrent revs), `rt_events_sse.rs` (auth, heartbeat, `pf:version`, `data.changed`, resync); `part_data.rs` in the `pf_ops` crate; `crates/pf-backup/tests/rollback.rs` + snapshot taker unit tests on a test clock; `crates/pf-prelude/tests/storage_api.test.js`.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/shared_data_two_browsers.spec.ts`, `data_changed_live.spec.ts` (HAR: no `OPTIONS`), `board_256_keys_one_list.spec.ts`, `snapshot_rollback.spec.ts`.
- Logs asserted: `event="rt.op" op="storage.set" outcome`, `event="data.changed"`, `event="sse.deliver" type="data.changed"`, `event="snapshot.taken" reason=…`, `event="snapshot.restore" outcome=ok keys_changed=N`, `event="op" op="part_data"`; never a data value (canary).

## Verification gate
- On the binary from `main` in the e2e harness: the contract's pixel board in two browsers on `https://pixel-part.pf.test/c/<cap>/` (test-minted caps) repaints across tabs within 1 s; 256 keys load with one `list`; `part_data get` via the CLI (dev token) reads the same doc, and `snapshot_restore` repaints the open tab.
- CI green on `main`: the tests above in the nextest job and the e2e harness job.
- Logs: the run asserts `event="data.changed"` and `event="snapshot.restore" outcome=ok`, and a canary data value never appears in logs.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite and every earlier gate test pass.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, command excerpts, HAR/trace paths; `ci_green` and `verified` reported.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Two browsers on one part see each other's shared writes within 1 s; a 256-key board loads with one `list {values: true}`; the contract's pixel board (docs/agent-contract.md worked session) runs unmodified: paints, loads with paging, repaints on another tab's write.
- [ ] Matrix test covers owner, edit, view and comment (on `viewers` and on `editors` parts), Can-view link, render (test-minted renderer caps) and a guest cap with `dw`, for each op and scope: a `view` grantee's shared write is `forbidden_view_only` once the part is `shared_data_writers: editors`; a Can-view link never writes; a link, render or guest cap has no personal scope.
- [ ] Each limit yields its exact code and HTTP status: `invalid_input` 400, `too_large` 413, `quota_exceeded` 429 (shared past 5 MiB), `rate_limited` 429 with `Retry-After`, `forbidden_view_only` 403, `storage_full` 507; a `getMany` or `list` page counts as one read.
- [ ] `PfError` rejections carry `code`, `message`, `retryable` and `retry_after` when rate-limited; a missing key resolves `null`; `getMany` returns results in key order with `null` for missing keys; `list` pages with `next_cursor` until `null`.
- [ ] 1,000 concurrent sets from 10 principals: all committed, `rev` strictly increasing per doc.
- [ ] No `OPTIONS` request in any HAR.
- [ ] Two tabs on one part get `data.changed` within 1 s of a write; it never echoes to the writing tab; a delete arrives as `op: "delete"`; a v0 part's `/_rt/events` stream gets `pf:version {n: 1, live: 1}` when v1 goes live.
- [ ] Event append is atomic with its change (a failed write appends nothing); `/_rt/events` rejects missing or foreign caps and a non-null foreign `Origin`; heartbeat every 25 s; a consumer that falls behind the broadcast gets `pf:resync`.
- [ ] `part_data get` of a `window.storage` key returns the contract's `doc` shape; `if_rev: 0` on an existing doc → `if_match_failed` with `current_rev`; a replayed `set` with the same `request_id` returns `replayed: true`.
- [ ] Guest-written docs come back `provenance: "link_viewer"`, `contains_untrusted: true`; `get`/`list` without `data:read`, or `set`/`delete` without `data:write`, are `forbidden` with `scope_needed`.
- [ ] The contract's `snapshot_list` and `snapshot_restore` examples run as written (the conformance scenario uses them); snapshot actions without `parts:write` or the person's `edit` role are `forbidden`.

- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with `rt_storage_ops.rs`, `rt_events_sse.rs`, `part_data.rs`, `rollback.rs` (nextest job) and `shared_data_two_browsers.spec.ts`, `data_changed_live.spec.ts`, `board_256_keys_one_list.spec.ts`, `snapshot_rollback.spec.ts` (e2e harness job).
- [ ] GATE: The e2e run asserts `event="data.changed"` and `event="snapshot.restore" outcome=ok` lines, and a canary data value never appears in logs.
- [ ] GATE: The full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run id, gate command excerpts, HAR/trace paths) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported.

title: Workspace, config and CI: the Cargo workspace, the config and secrets loader, CI and Renovate
description:
## Goal
Create the repository skeleton every other bead builds in: one Cargo workspace producing one static binary (`partifactory`, with `part` as a CLI alias, every asset embedded, the build worker the same binary re-exec'd), a crate layout that keeps the core free of vendor adapters, the typed config and secrets loader (the env contract), and a CI pipeline that enforces formatting, lints, tests, licences, advisories and secret scanning from the first commit. A household server is set up once and left alone, so dependency hygiene and safe config have to be automatic from day one.

## Scope
- [ ] Workspace at the root: `resolver = "2"`, pinned `rust-toolchain.toml` (stable + rustfmt + clippy), release profile with `panic = "abort"`, LTO and strip for a ~20 MB `FROM scratch` musl image. A `dev` cargo feature (never in release builds) that later beads hang their `partifactory dev …` subcommands and fixtures on.
- [ ] Crates (`crates/pf-<name>`, each with a responsibility doc comment): config, db, blobs, model, build, caps, serve, prelude, ops, api, mcp, cli, auth, policy, oauth, ui, obs, janitor, backup, provision, render, runner, adapter-cloudflare, adapter-authentik, and the `partifactory` binary. Crates for post-Slice-1 work (provision, runner, the adapters) are empty stubs with their doc comment only. Directory placeholders `tests/e2e/`, `tests/agent_surfaces/`, `tests/golden/`, `tests/device/`, `docs/spikes/`, `deploy/proxy/`, `examples/ci/`.
- [ ] The binary with `clap` subcommand stubs (`serve`, `build-worker`, `runner`, `export`, `import`, `migrate`, `healthcheck`, `provision`, `doctor`, `deploy`, `config check`, `admin bootstrap`, `admin break-glass`, `bench`, `logs`) and `argv[0] == "part"` dispatching to the CLI. A stub exits 64 with `not implemented yet` until its bead lands.
- [ ] Adapter-boundary check: CI fails if any core crate depends on a `pf-adapter-*` crate.
- [ ] CI as plain scripts (`ci/fmt.sh`, `ci/clippy.sh`, `ci/test.sh`, `ci/deny.sh`, `ci/audit.sh`, `ci/gitleaks.sh`, `ci/check-boundaries.sh`, `ci/env-docs.sh`) plus one thin workflow for the forge in use (Gitea Actions today: `.gitea/workflows/ci.yml`, jobs choosing runners by the generic `rust` and `browser` labels; the workflow installs `cargo-nextest`, `cargo-audit` and `cargo-deny` itself, and `scripts/bootstrap-dev.sh` does the same on a laptop), each script its own job; nextest profiles `default` and `ci` (JUnit kept as an artifact). Later beads add their jobs (`e2e`, `store-durability`, `spike`, …) as more `ci/*.sh` scripts in the same shape.
- [ ] Secret scanning (AGENTS.md "Secrets and site config"): gitleaks in CI on every PR and as a pre-push hook installed by `scripts/install-hooks.sh`, with a `.gitleaks.toml` that knows the `pf_at_`, `pf_rt_` and `pf_pat_` token shapes and allowlists only the documented fixture values; a planted-secret fixture test proves both the CI job and the hook fail.
- [ ] §3h layer 1 from the start: Renovate (Cargo, Dockerfile base images pinned by digest, workflow pins; oxc/rolldown exact-pin only, never automerged), run as a scheduled Gitea Actions job (the `renovate/renovate` image pinned by digest, `platform: gitea`) with a `RENOVATE_TOKEN` repo secret. That bot token is the admin's to create (an admin prerequisite, recorded in the human-checks bead), so this bead proves the config with `renovate-config-validator` and a `--platform=local` dry run, which need no token, `cargo deny` (licences, bans, advisories) + `cargo audit` on every PR, and a nightly advisory run on `main`.
- [ ] The config crate: `site.toml` (path `PF_SITE_TOML`, default `/data/site.toml`) as typed `deny_unknown_fields` structs for every section the plan names — §5c's list (`[domain]`, `[ingress]`, `[dns]`, `[idp]`, `[idp.provisioner]`, `[admin]`, `[embed]`, `[alerts]`, `[backup]`, `[deploy]`, `[names]`, `[webhooks]`, `[mirror]`, `[render]`) plus `[unsafe]`, `[disk]`, `[advisories]` and `[backends]` — so a site file written once never breaks when a later feature lands (a section whose feature isn't built yet parses and validates but is inert); every key settable as `PF_<SECTION>_<KEY>` (env wins); secrets env or `PF_*_FILE` only, never in the file; a `Secret<T>` newtype that prints `[redacted]`, has no `Serialize` and zeroizes on drop.
- [ ] `partifactory config check`: loads exactly as `serve` would; missing required secret exits 2 naming the variable; cross-field rules (e.g. `PF_RUNNER_KEY` required only when the runner is on, the OIDC secret only when `[idp]` is set); the `[unsafe]` mechanism (§5h: a protection switched off without its `[unsafe] <name> = "off"` key fails, and a set `[unsafe]` key is reported as a warning). Its diagnostics are JSON log lines on stdout (`event="config.check"`), the same shape every later bead's gate asserts on.
- [ ] `docs/env.md` generated from the config structs; CI regenerates it and fails on diff.
- [ ] The root `Cargo.toml` has `exclude = ["spikes"]`: the spikes are their own Cargo workspace under `spikes/` and the sandbox rig its own npm package under `tests/sandbox-spike/`, so this bead and the two spike beads can run at once on `main` without editing each other's manifests. The spike beads add their `ci/spikes.sh` and `ci/spike.sh` jobs to this workflow once it exists; anyone adding a job reserves `.gitea/workflows/` and `ci/` through Agent Mail first.
- [ ] Build hygiene from the first commit, because unchecked Rust builds have repeatedly filled the admin's disk:
  - Profiles in the root `Cargo.toml`: `[profile.dev] debug = "line-tables-only"`, `[profile.dev.package."*"] debug = false` (dependencies carry no debuginfo), `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"`; `test` inherits `dev`; a `ci` profile (`inherits = "dev"`, `incremental = false`, `debug = false`) that every `ci/*.sh` uses. `--release` (and the musl target) only for gates, benches and the image.
  - One target dir per checkout (`target/`), shared by every agent: no per-agent `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, no sccache or second caches. One feature set for tests (`--features dev` everywhere, set in `ci/test.sh` and documented) so dependencies build once, not once per feature combination.
  - `scripts/disk-guard.sh`, called first by every `ci/*.sh` and by the e2e harness: exits non-zero with a clear message when the volume has less than `PF_DISK_MIN_FREE_GB` free (default 20) or `target/` is over `PF_TARGET_MAX_GB` (default 30), and prints what `clean-build.sh` would free.
  - `scripts/clean-build.sh` (dry run by default, `--apply` to act): `cargo sweep --time 2` (age-based, so it never deletes what a concurrent build is using), `target/*/incremental` dirs older than a day, `target/release` and `target/*-musl` once their gate is recorded, `target/e2e-logs/` and `target/test-logs/` beyond the newest 5 runs, harness containers, volumes and images labelled `pf.harness=1`, `docker builder prune --keep-storage 10GB`, and Playwright browser builds other than the pinned version. It never touches anything outside the repo except those labelled Docker objects and the Playwright cache, and never runs a full `cargo clean`.
  - CI sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and runs `clean-build.sh --apply` at the end of every job, pass or fail. `scripts/bootstrap-dev.sh` installs `cargo-sweep`.

## Plan refs
§5 Stack (one static binary, why Rust), §5b Builds and deploys (env contract, CI is an example), §5c `site.toml` sections, Secrets, Rotation, Site config itself, §5d Maintenance (Dependencies), §3h layer 1, §5f Portability, §5h Safe defaults, enforced (the `[unsafe]` table), decisions 2, 9, 22; AGENTS.md (secrets, gitleaks before every push).

## Considerations
- Required secrets: `PF_SESSION_KEY`, `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY`, `PF_DOMAIN_APEX`, `PF_METRICS_TOKEN`, the OIDC client secret if `[idp]` is set, `PF_RUNNER_KEY` if the runner is on; adapter tokens (`PF_DNS_API_TOKEN`, `PF_TUNNEL_TOKEN`, `PF_IDP_PROVISIONER_TOKEN`, `PF_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `PF_CDN_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`) are optional (§5b).
- `_FILE` contents: trim one trailing newline; an empty file is missing; both `PF_X` and `PF_X_FILE` set is an error, never a silent pick.
- CI is an example, not a dependency: nothing reads a CI vendor's API, and the public mirror runs no Actions and holds no secrets, so the scripts are what matter and run identically on a laptop. The example CI workflows in `examples/ci/` come after Slice 1; the one thin workflow here is the repo's own.
- oxc and rolldown are 0.x Rust APIs: Renovate must never bump them on its own (the compiler spike and the tsx epic pin and vendor them).
- `[unsafe]` here is the parsing and the `config check` rule. The safe-defaults registry `{name, config keys, unsafe_key}` that Health and `doctor` render is the retention bead's; it reads the same `[unsafe]` struct. Later beads (the rate-limit layer, quotas, the nightly export) register their protection names into it.
- The export age recipient is a public key, not a secret. The offline copy of `site.toml`, the admin pin and the age identity is documented in the `docs/env.md` header.
- gitleaks is the last line, not the first: the `Secret<T>` type and the log redaction (observability bead) keep secrets out of output; gitleaks keeps them out of git. Fixture tokens used in tests are documented in `.gitleaks.toml` so the hook never trains people to bypass it.
- No household names, internal IPs or IdP inventory anywhere in the repo (AGENTS.md); examples use `pf.test` or `<domain>`.

## Tests and logging
- `crates/partifactory/tests/cli_smoke.rs::{help_lists_subcommands, argv0_part_dispatches_to_cli, stub_exits_64}`.
- `ci/check-boundaries.sh` self-test with a fixture adding an adapter dep to `pf-model`; `ci/gitleaks.sh` self-test with a planted `pf_pat_` fixture in a scratch commit (expects a non-zero exit), and the same through the pre-push hook.
- `pf_config::tests::{missing_required_secret_exit_2, file_secret_equals_env_secret, both_env_and_file_is_error, file_trailing_newline_trimmed, empty_file_is_missing, env_overrides_toml (proptest over every key), unknown_key_suggests, unknown_section_rejected, every_plan_section_parses, cross_field_rules, unsafe_key_required_to_disable_protection, unsafe_key_reported_as_warning, canary_never_in_debug_display_logs_panics}` (the last formats, logs and panics with a `CANARY-` secret and asserts it never appears).
- `ci/env-docs.sh`: regenerate and `git diff --exit-code docs/env.md`.
- Log events from config load: `event="config.loaded" outcome="ok"`, `event="config.check" outcome="missing_secret" var="PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY"` (the variable name, never the value), `event="config.check" outcome="unsafe_set" key=…`.

## Verification gate
- Observed on the release binary built from `main`: `partifactory --help` lists the stubs; `part` (a symlink) reaches the CLI; `partifactory config check` with a scrubbed env exits 2 naming `PF_SESSION_KEY`; with `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY_FILE` it loads the same value as the env var (the check passes with either).
- CI green on `main` with every job visible (fmt, clippy, nextest, deny, audit, gitleaks, boundaries, env-docs); a deliberate fmt break, a clippy warning and a planted secret each failed CI once, then reverted; the nightly advisory job has run on `main` once (started by `workflow_dispatch`, the same job its schedule runs); `renovate-config-validator` passes and a `renovate --platform=local` dry run proposes the update for a deliberately outdated pin. The first real Renovate PR waits on the admin's bot token and is recorded in the human-checks bead, never here.
- Logs checked: the release binary's `config check` run with the scrubbed env prints a JSON line `event="config.check" outcome="missing_secret" var="PF_SESSION_KEY"` on stdout; the canary test's captured output contains `event="config.check"` lines and no canary value.
- No regressions: `ci/*.sh` run locally give the same results as CI.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run ids (PR run and nightly run), the Renovate dry-run output, and the `config check` transcript; `br gate report` for `ci_green` and `verified` before `br close`.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Spikes: oxc and rolldown as libraries, rmcp stateless Streamable HTTP, Leptos vs askama
description:
## Goal
Three one-day maturity spikes, run in week one beside the sandbox spike, each ending in a go/no-go note with a runnable example. They de-risk the three young dependencies the plan bets on: the TSX compiler (oxc + rolldown as Rust libraries in a child process), the MCP server SDK (rmcp 3.x, stateless Streamable HTTP), and the workspace UI framework (Leptos 0.8 SSR + hydration vs `askama`/`maud` + vanilla-JS islands). The `tsx` kind moved to right after Slice 1, but the compiler spike stays here so an oxc or rolldown problem still shows up first. The builds bead (child protocol), the MCP bead and the wrapper and Stockroom shell bead start from these notes, so this sits on the critical path.

## Scope
- [ ] Compiler (`spikes/spike-compiler`, note `docs/spikes/compiler.md`): re-exec itself as a child (`build-worker` shape), length-prefixed CBOR over stdin/stdout (the §3d build-child protocol); in the child, oxc transforms `App.tsx` (automatic JSX runtime, TS stripping) and rolldown bundles against an in-memory module set (`react`, `react-dom` 18.3, no network, no `node_modules` walk); emit ESM + an import map, minified. Enforce the 10 s deadline, `RLIMIT_AS` 1 GiB and `SIGKILL`; show a hang and a panic reported as failed builds (`timeout`, `builder_crashed`) with the parent still up. Measure spawn cost against a pre-forked pool (`max(1, min(2, cores/2))`), cold/warm time for three inputs (a 50-line component, a recharts-sized import, five files) and memory peak against the TSX targets (p50 < 150 ms, p99 < 1 s). Try esbuild-as-subprocess through the same protocol. Recommend a vendoring approach and the exact pins.
- [ ] MCP (`spikes/spike-mcp`, note `docs/spikes/mcp.md`): axum on `:8080` mounting rmcp's Streamable HTTP service at `/mcp`, stateless, with two toy tools from `deny_unknown_fields` + `JsonSchema` structs. The eight checks: stateless (no session id; `server/discover`, `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` of the 2026-07-28 revision); `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` from schemars with non-object outputs wrapped; tool annotations; errors as `isError: true` + `structuredContent` + one text line; auth failure as HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` raised by middleware before rmcp; image content blocks (PNG ≤ 1 MB); long markdown `instructions`; `part://` resources as projections. Connect with `claude mcp add --transport http spike http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer test"` and with rmcp's own client.
- [ ] UI (`spikes/spike-ui`, note `docs/spikes/ui.md`): build the share sheet (five-rung ladder, live sentence, Can view / Can contribute switch, Copy, a fake in-sheet step-up) in Leptos and in templates + an island; build the 44 px part-view bar as a hydrated Leptos page and measure its bundle with `brotli -q 11`; a 30-minute CodeMirror 6 interop probe; apply the decision rule; say how the wrapper's tiny standalone bundle is built under the chosen option.
- [ ] Each note: question, exact crate versions/commits, what was built, measurements, findings, risks, a decision line (go / no-go / go-with-fallback), and what the dependent beads must do differently. Those consequences are copied as a `br comment` onto each dependent bead (builds, MCP, the wrapper and Stockroom shell, the tsx epic).

## Plan refs
§5 Stack (TSX/JSX, MCP and Workspace UI rows; "Why Leptos, and when it loses"; "Maturity check before P0 freezes"), §3d The build worker (isolation, pool), §4b One operation registry and Adapters, §5a targets, §6 "Why the sandbox and TSX in P0", §6a Spikes, decision 39.

## Considerations
- The decision rule (§5): if the share sheet costs more than a day of framework friction, or the hydrated part-view bundle exceeds 300 KB brotli, use `askama`/`maud` + small vanilla-JS islands. Record friction hours honestly, overruns included. The wrapper stays a tiny standalone bundle with no framework hydration under either option.
- Pin Leptos 0.8.x (0.9 is in release candidates). oxc is 0.x with breaking releases and rolldown's semver promise covers its JS API, not the Rust crate, so pin exactly and vendor.
- Named fallbacks: esbuild-as-subprocess behind the same child protocol (compiler; don't invent a bundler); templates + islands (UI). rmcp has none: a no-go means hand-writing the stateless JSON-RPC endpoint over axum with rmcp's types, and the note says so.
- rmcp's OAuth support is client-side only; the spike only needs bearer extraction. No op may depend on an MCP-only feature (sampling, elicitation, notifications).
- A no-go is a valid outcome. Spike code is throwaway: its own Cargo workspace at `spikes/Cargo.toml` (the root workspace excludes `spikes/`, so this bead starts on day one beside the workspace bead without touching the root manifest), never linked into the release binary; delete them once the dependent beads land.
- Spike logs use `tracing` JSON with the shared field names (`event`, `outcome`, `route_class`) so the assertions carry straight over to the real crates.
- `ci/spikes.sh` runs `cargo test --manifest-path spikes/Cargo.toml` and joins the workspace bead's workflow once that exists (reserve `.gitea/workflows/` and `ci/` through Agent Mail). The Claude Code half of the MCP check needs the `claude` CLI on the agent's machine; the rmcp-client half runs anywhere.

## Tests and logging
- `spikes/spike-compiler/tests/child.rs::{panic_in_child_is_builder_crashed, hang_is_killed_after_deadline, rlimit_breach_is_failed_build, bundle_resolves_virtual_react_once}`.
- `spikes/spike-mcp/tests/mcp.rs::{tools_list_schemas_match_schemars, missing_token_is_http_401_not_tool_result, stateless_request_without_session_id_succeeds, error_is_iserror_with_structured_content}`.
- `spikes/spike-ui/measure.sh` prints the brotli size; output pasted in the note.
- Logs: `event="build.child" outcome="timeout|builder_crashed|ok"`; `event="http.request" route_class="mcp" status=401` for the token-less call.

## Verification gate
- Three notes merged, each with a decision line, a runnable example and the exact command; a second person (or agent) ran each example and recorded tool and crate versions.
- Observed runs: `cargo run -p spike-compiler -- examples/app.tsx` prints a bundle and an import map; Claude Code lists and calls both `spike-mcp` tools, and a token-less curl gets HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`; `spike-ui` serves `/leptos` and `/templates` with the measured bundle size.
- CI green on `main` with a job (`ci/spikes.sh`) building `-p spike-compiler -p spike-mcp -p spike-ui` and running their tests.
- Logs checked: the child-process tests assert `event="build.child"` with `outcome="timeout"` and `outcome="builder_crashed"`.
- No regressions: every CI job that exists still passes with the spike job added.
- Evidence on close: SHAs, CI run id, the transcripts from the notes, links to the `br comment`s on the dependent beads; `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/spikes/compiler.md` has a go/no-go decision, pinned versions, a timing table (cold/warm, three inputs), spawn cost vs a pre-forked pool, and memory peak against the TSX targets.
- [ ] `cargo run -p spike-compiler -- examples/app.tsx` prints a bundle and an import map.
- [ ] A hang, a memory-cap breach and a panic in the child are each reported as build failures (`timeout`, `builder_crashed`) and the parent stays up.
- [ ] The esbuild fallback ran through the same protocol, or the note explains why not.
- [ ] `docs/spikes/mcp.md` has a go/no-go, a table of the eight checks (pass/fail/workaround) and versions.
- [ ] `cargo run -p spike-mcp` + `claude mcp add --transport http spike http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer test"` lists and calls both tools; rmcp's own client does too.
- [ ] A request without a token gets HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` from middleware, never a tool result (curl transcript in the note).
- [ ] `docs/spikes/ui.md` states the hours of friction for the share sheet, the part-view hydrated bundle size in KB brotli (`brotli -q 11`), the CodeMirror interop result, how the wrapper bundle is built, and the decision per the §5 rule.
- [ ] `cargo run -p spike-ui` serves both variants at `/leptos` and `/templates`.
- [ ] Each note's consequences are copied as a `br comment` onto the beads that depend on it (builds, MCP, the wrapper and Stockroom shell, the tsx epic).
- [ ] Spike code lives under `spikes/` and is not linked into the release binary.
- [ ] GATE: All three notes are merged with a decision line, and each example was run by a second person or agent with the tool and crate versions recorded.
- [ ] GATE: Observed: the compiler example prints a bundle and import map; Claude Code lists and calls both MCP spike tools and a token-less curl gets 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`; `spike-ui` serves both variants with the measured bundle size.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with a job (`ci/spikes.sh`) that builds and tests `spike-compiler`, `spike-mcp` and `spike-ui`.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the child-process tests assert `event="build.child"` with `outcome="timeout"` and `outcome="builder_crashed"`.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: every CI job that exists still passes with the spike job added.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (SHAs, CI run id, the transcripts, links to the dependent-bead comments) and `ci_green` + `verified` gate reports.
