title: Human checks on real devices (non-blocking)
description:
**Human-only, non-blocking. Nothing depends on this bead, and it never blocks a release or another bead. Agents never claim it (`br ready --exclude-label human-only`).**

## Goal
Everything the swarm cannot see from CI, the emulators or the iOS Simulator: the real iPhone, Android and Telegram in-app-browser checks, the by-hand `communal_pixel_editor` run on the example deployment, and the Telegram passkey test with its two decided fixes (Slice 1 definition-of-done item 8, "not in the gate"). The admin does these whenever convenient, records the result here, and files any failure as a `bug` bead (`br create "..." -t bug -l found-in:<this bead's id>`) for the swarm. The emulated and simulated equivalents of every item already gate the beads that ship the feature, so a failure here is a finding, not a blocker.

## Scope
- [ ] Real-device pass (§7 Operations, `tests/manual/real-device-pass.md`): iPhone Safari, Android Chrome and the Telegram in-app browser (iOS and Android) for standalone open, part-host open (first open and reload), the `/l/` guest open, embedding (when P4 lands), invite acceptance (when P2b lands) and sign-in. Dated result files in `tests/manual/results/<date>-<device>.md`, validated by `scripts/check_manual_records.sh`; no personal data in them.
- [ ] The sandbox spike's "needs real-device confirmation" list (`docs/spikes/sandbox.md`), following the rig's manual iOS Safari instructions: the WebAuthn `rp.id` = apex assertion from the wrapper origin on a real iPhone (Safari) and in the Telegram webview on iOS and Android, plus any item the simulator could not answer.
- [ ] The by-hand `communal_pixel_editor` run on the example deployment (its IdP as plain OIDC, its tunnel as the proxy): a real agent connected by device code, the admin on a phone (Share → Anyone with the link → Can contribute → Copy; later Roll back data and Freeze), a signed-out phone on mobile data painting and then refused. Recorded with date, phone models and browser versions.
- [ ] The §7 suite from outside against the example deployment (`tests/security/` with `--base-url`), so the real ingress (the tunnel, the real client-IP header, the edge cache) is checked once by hand; the compose deployment run in CI is the blocking one.
- [ ] The Telegram passkey test (decision 36): passkey sign-in in Telegram's in-app browser on a real phone, about 5 minutes. On failure apply both fixes and re-test: set Telegram to open links in the normal browser (`docs/ops/telegram.md`) and make Hermes' messages hint "open in browser". The person-bound-link fallback stays rejected.
- [ ] The laptop drill against a physically separate OCI host (`scripts/drill.sh`), once per phase, because the CI system may be on the host that died (§5c); the CI drill against a second Docker context is the blocking one.
- [ ] Later phases add their real-phone items here as they ship: PWA install on a real phone and the P1 phone checks (SSO open at the part's own host, a public link from mobile data unfurling as a card) with the rest of P1; the Hermes-on-Telegram flow and invite acceptance on a phone (P2, P2b); the family-hub embed and tap-to-edit on a phone (P4).
- [ ] Admin prerequisites the swarm can't provide (each unblocks a line, never a bead's start): the Renovate bot token as the `RENOVATE_TOKEN` repo secret, then the first real Renovate PR recorded here; the container-registry push credential and the release token for the Shipping bead's tagged release.

## Plan refs
§7 Operations (real-device pass); §2 Telegram decision; §3a UX click budgets ("a manual pass on a real iPhone, an Android phone and the Telegram in-app browser"); Slice 1 definition of done item 8; §5c drills; §6 P1 and P4 Done when (the phone parts); decisions 35, 36, 52.

## Considerations
- Real phones never block anything (decision 52). Every item here has an emulated or simulated stand-in in the bead that ships the feature: Playwright Chromium with mobile emulation and the virtual authenticator, Playwright WebKit with a mobile profile, Playwright Firefox, and Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh`). This bead is where the real thing is confirmed afterwards.
- A failure here is filed as a `bug` bead labelled `found-in:<this bead's id>` and linked with `br dep add` to the bead it affects; it never reopens a closed bead.
- Do items as they become possible: the Slice 1 items once the Shipping and pixel beads are closed, the later-phase items as their epics ship. Partial results are fine; record what was run.
- Only the by-hand halves live here. The automated halves of the lines that came with them (the portability lane, the CI drill, the compose §7 run, the family hub's service-labelled writes) stay in the beads and epics that own them.

## Tests and logging
- Nothing automated gates here. Record each run as a dated result file (device, OS and browser versions, item, pass/fail, screenshot path), and for the by-hand pixel run the `server.jsonl` excerpt from the example deployment showing the ordered events the CI spec asserts (`event="op" op="part_create" outcome="ok"` through the guest's refused write).

## Verification gate
- The gate is the admin's own recorded results: dated result files for each item attempted, with device and browser versions and screenshots, and the Telegram passkey result (pass, or fail with both fixes applied and a re-test).
- `ci_green` here means "CI was green on the commit that was tested" (record the commit SHA and its CI run id); there is no CI job for this bead.
- `verified` is the admin's gate report naming the result files.
- No regressions is not asserted here: a failure becomes a `bug` bead for the swarm.
- Evidence on close: the result file paths, the commit SHA tested, and the ids of any `bug` beads filed.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A dated result exists for iPhone Safari, Android Chrome and the Telegram in-app browser covering every existing real-device item (standalone open, part-host open first and on reload, the `/l/` guest open, sign-in; embedding and invite acceptance once they exist).
- [ ] The sandbox spike's "needs real-device confirmation" items (the apex `rp.id` assertion from the wrapper origin on a real iPhone and in the Telegram webview on iOS and Android, and anything the simulator could not answer) have a recorded result, run by the rig's manual iOS Safari instructions.
- [ ] DoD 8, the by-hand run: `communal_pixel_editor` passes once by hand on the example deployment (its IdP as plain OIDC, its tunnel as the proxy): a real agent, the admin on a phone, a signed-out phone on mobile data; the `server.jsonl` excerpt shows the CI spec's ordered events.
- [ ] DoD 8, Telegram: the passkey result is recorded; on failure Telegram is set to open links in the normal browser and Hermes' messages say "open in browser", and a re-test is recorded.
- [ ] The §7 lines for what exists pass from outside against the example deployment (`tests/security/ --base-url`), the guest, agent and render-sidecar lines included; every §7 manual line has a recorded result.
- [ ] The laptop drill against a physically separate OCI host has run once per phase and its `backup/drills/<ts>.json` is recorded.
- [ ] Rest of P1, when it ships: the part installs as a separate app from its manifest on a real phone; the admin opens a part on a phone at its own host link via SSO; a public link opens from mobile data with no login and unfurls as a card (recorded).
- [ ] P4, when it ships: a family-hub page embeds a family part on iPhone Safari and Android Chrome (recorded).
- [ ] Every failure found here is filed as a `bug` bead labelled `found-in:` this bead and linked to the bead it affects; nothing here reopens a closed bead, and no bead depends on this one (checked with `br dep list`).
- [ ] GATE: The admin's dated result files exist for every item attempted (device, OS and browser versions, pass/fail, screenshot paths), validated by `scripts/check_manual_records.sh`.
- [ ] GATE: `ci_green` is reported as "CI was green on the commit tested", with that commit SHA and CI run id; `verified` is the admin's own gate report naming the result files.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence: the result file paths, the commit SHA tested and the ids of any `bug` beads filed.

title: The trusted wrapper, its chrome API, the content-free card and the Stockroom workspace shell
description:
## Goal
The link to post is the part's own host, `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`. This bead builds what lives there: a trusted, unsandboxed wrapper that frames the sandboxed content at `/c/<cap>/…` with no cap in the address bar, the workspace chrome API it talks to (CORS for exactly the sandboxed part-host origins), the content-free preview card, the Stockroom foundation with the Slice 1 workspace pages, and the wrapper's chrome bar. The share sheet and public links, Connected agents, and the Health page live in their own beads.

## Scope
- [ ] Wrapper at `/` and every path outside `/c/`, `/l/`, `/_pf/` (the path is passed on to the frame): cap from `#pf=` then `sessionStorage`, else `location.replace` to `/grant?…&mode=wrap`; `share=…` fragments kept in `sessionStorage` across the hop and re-applied; `history.replaceState` before any other script; the sandboxed frame (`sandbox` attribute as §4a.6, belt and braces with the header); messages matched by `event.source`, never `event.origin`; `pf:regrant` answered through the chrome API with no navigation; `<noscript>` "Sign in to open"; `/_pf/manifest.webmanifest` (`id` and `scope` = `/`) and icons. Strict wrapper CSP (scripts and styles only from the blob host, `connect-src` only the workspace, `frame-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors` = workspace + embedders), `no-referrer`, `noindex`, never `Set-Cookie`, identical for every User-Agent. The wrapper's script and styles are shared blobs registered at start and referenced at serve time.
- [ ] Chrome API `/api/chrome/v1/<part>/…`: `grant` (the identity bead's regrant handler behind this CORS layer), `summary` (incl. `head`, `live` and `features`, which drives which controls render), `stepup` (the identity bead's WebAuthn verify). CORS echoes only an active, sandboxed part's own origin on its own routes (credentials, `Vary: Origin`, methods `GET, POST`, header `Content-Type`, preflight `max-age` 600, never `*` or `null`); writes need `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site|same-origin` and a JSON body. Nothing an agent may do exists only here.
- [ ] Content-free card: two static 1200×630 PNGs (private; "Anyone with the link"), golden files with SVG source, embedded in the binary, at `/og/<sha256>.png` on the workspace, `public, immutable`; an og helper whose `og:title`/`og:description` match the card exactly, plus `twitter:card=summary_large_image` and an absolute https `og:image`; a card input type with no part-derived field.
- [ ] Stockroom foundation: `tokens.css` (light + dark, §4a.3 verbatim), spacing/radius/elevation/motion tokens, self-hosted IBM Plex, icon sprite, mark and wordmark, 48 px top bar (mark home, theme toggle, avatar menu with sign out and sign out everywhere), CI contrast test.
- [ ] Workspace pages: Stockroom styling and og tags for the identity bead's sign-in and `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` pages (Ask for access comes after Slice 1, so the 403 page offers only "Sign in as someone else"); gallery (drawer-front cards linking straight to part hosts, the `Recent · Mine · Shared with me` filters that Slice 1's personal spaces can fill, kind filter, grid/list, day sections, being-made and scratch-expiry badges, the empty state with **Connect an agent** and the copyable `claude mcp add` line in its Slice 1 form (with `--header "Authorization: Bearer <personal token>"`, since OAuth authorization code comes after the slice), skeletons); error pages (404 with up to 3 close names you can see, 403, 429, 500 with the request id); 360×740 mobile (56 px gallery bar, list by default).
- [ ] Chrome bar: 44 px desktop / 40 px phone (hides on scroll down), back, tag chip, title, name in mono, `REV n`, audience chip, Share, ⋯ (Copy link, Open standalone), registration corner ticks, cross-fade; the "being made…" drafting sheet drawn from `summary` while `live` is null (its live cross-fade to REV 1 runs on the shared data bead's `pf:version` and is verified in the public-links bead); unsandboxed parts open Share on the workspace (Slice 1 has no way to set `unsandboxed`, so this is tested on a fixture row; the toggle and the admin list of unsandboxed parts are rest-of-P1 work).

- [ ] Gallery thumbnails in Slice 1 (decision 53): the latest passing render screenshot of the live version (`part_previews`, `source: render`, written by the part_check bead, which lands after this one: this bead's tests seed `part_previews` rows through a `dev`-feature fixture, and the part_check bead's gate proves a real render reaches the gallery), else the "being made…" frame; served at `/api/v1/thumbs/<part>?v=<n>`, session- and grant-checked, `private, immutable`. Agent thumbnails, SVG thumbs, posters and clips come after Slice 1 (rest-of-P1 epic).

## Plan refs
§2 The link to post (first-open flow, chrome actions, CORS, CSRF, wrapper CSP, who opens it), §2 Serving (framed expiry), §4c Tier (a), §4a.2–4a.7, §4a.9, §5 Leptos decision rule, §7 The wrapper, Chrome-API CORS, Links and cards. Decisions 19, 25, 40.

## Considerations
- Read `docs/spikes/sandbox.md` first: items 10 (the wrapper flow), 12 and 13 (the passkey from the wrapper origin) decide this bead's details.
- UI framework per the Leptos spike; the wrapper bundle is standalone with no hydration either way.
- First open costs one client-side hop (the server never sees the fragment); reloads none.
- CORS never admits an unsandboxed part (same-origin with its wrapper), `blobs`, or a redirecting old name; use the names cache. Renames come after Slice 1, so the old-name case is a fixture row.
- The audience decides the card, never the UA. Static PNGs can't carry the host name, so the card and og text omit it; note it on close.
- Amber only for "Public link"; agents blueprint blue; colour never the only signal; no font CDN, ever (Plex Mono + system sans is the fallback).
- Wrapper and chrome are shared blobs served at serve time, so a platform fix reaches every part on deploy (§3h layer 1).
- The admin pin, `admin bootstrap`, break-glass and workspace step-up are the identity bead's; this bead verifies only what needs the wrapper page: a passkey asserting from a part-host wrapper origin, and step-up started from the wrapper.
- Lines needing the share sheet, public links or the placeholder's live cross-fade are verified in the public links bead.
- This bead needs `/grant`, step-up and the content listener, not the op registry, so it runs in parallel with the registry bead (§6a "/grant → the part-host wrapper and its chrome API"). The chrome API's `summary` is a projection of the same part-service read `part_get` wraps; whichever of the two beads lands second routes it through the registry, so nothing an agent may do exists only here.
- The wrapper first-open and regrant specs also run in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (local lane, evidence attached to `verified`); real phones never block anything.

## Tests and logging
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/{wrapper_headers,root_ua_independence,chrome_cors_fuzz,chrome_csrf,og_route}.rs`, `pf_serve::og::tests::*`, `crates/pf-ui/tests/contrast.rs`.
- E2E (`chromium-desktop` + `webkit-mobile`): `tests/e2e/wrapper_{first_open,fragment,isolation,regrant,chrome}.spec.ts`, `stepup_from_wrapper.spec.ts`, `gallery_open.spec.ts`, `gallery_thumbs.spec.ts` (latest-render thumbnail and placeholder; thumb 404 without access) (HAR: no third-party requests, fonts from the workspace only), `tests/e2e/visual/*`.
- Logs: `event="wrapper.serve" audience=…`, `event="chrome.cors" decision="deny"`, `event="chrome.grant" outcome=…`, `event="og.serve"`, `event="stepup.verify" origin=… outcome=…`, `event="ui.render" page="gallery"`.

## Verification gate
- On the binary built from `main` in the e2e harness: a signed-in person opens `https://pixel-part.pf.test/` from the gallery in one click with one silent `/grant` hop and a clean address bar, and a reload makes no hop; a signed-out `curl -si` of the root returns the private card, no cap, no part bytes and no `Set-Cookie`, byte-identical for a bot UA; `chrome_cors_fuzz` runs against the live server; a workspace passkey asserts from the wrapper; screenshots of the gallery and part view in light, dark and 360 px.
- CI green on `main`: nextest and harness e2e jobs include the tests above.
- Logs: the e2e run asserts `event="wrapper.serve"`, `event="chrome.grant" outcome="ok"` and `event="stepup.verify" outcome="ok"`.
- Simulator lane (evidence, not a CI check): `wrapper_first_open` and `wrapper_regrant` pass in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator; posts and screenshots attached to `verified`.
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, passes.
- Evidence on close (commit SHAs, CI run id, curl excerpts, screenshot paths) plus the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] After first open the address bar shows `https://<name>-part.<domain>/<path>` with no fragment, the deep path reaches the frame, and a reload makes no `/grant` request.
- [ ] A `#share=…` fragment present before the hop is re-applied after the cap is read.
- [ ] A test script inside the part tries `parent.document` and `parent.sessionStorage` and fails; a message from any window other than the frame is ignored.
- [ ] The wrapper response has the strict wrapper CSP, `no-referrer`, `noindex` and no `Set-Cookie`; signed out, the root contains no cap and no part bytes and carries the private card og tags and the `<noscript>` link.
- [ ] Root responses are byte-identical for bot and browser User-Agents.
- [ ] `/_pf/manifest.webmanifest` has `scope: "/"` and `id: "/"`.
- [ ] The wrapper's script and styles are shared blobs referenced at serve time, so a wrapper fix ships with a deploy and needs no part rebuild.
- [ ] CORS headers (with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and `Vary: Origin`) are present only for the active, sandboxed part's own origin on its own routes; a part origin calling another part's chrome route gets none.
- [ ] `Origin: null`, a sibling part's origin, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, an old redirecting name, `https://evil.example`, and `http://` variants all get no CORS headers (`chrome_cors_fuzz` against the live server).
- [ ] A chrome-API write without `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site|same-origin`, or without a JSON body, is refused.
- [ ] From the wrapper origin, `POST …/grant` returns a fresh cap for an allowed viewer and the standard 403/401 shape otherwise.
- [ ] When the cap window passes, a framed part's prelude sends exactly one `pf:regrant`, the wrapper sets a new frame `src` through the chrome API, and the page continues with no top-level navigation.
- [ ] The wrapper renders only the controls listed in `summary.features` (Slice 1: Share, Copy link, Open standalone); Copy link copies exactly `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`.
- [ ] A part with `live: null` shows the "being made…" drafting sheet with its title block.
- [ ] Both card PNGs are golden files with fixed text only, 1200×630, each ≤ 150 KB, embedded in the binary; `GET /og/<sha256>.png` serves each with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `image/png` and no `Set-Cookie`, and any other hash returns 404; the private and public-link variants differ only in the audience line; the card input type has no part-derived field.
- [ ] The og:title/og:description on the root, sign-in and 403 pages equal the private card text exactly.
- [ ] The contrast test is green, light and dark.
- [ ] Fonts are served from the binary only: no request leaves the workspace origin for fonts (asserted in e2e).
- [ ] Gallery thumbnails (decision 53): a part with a seeded `part_previews` row for its live version shows that screenshot (the `part_previews` row with `source: render`, from `/api/v1/thumbs/<part>?v=<n>`, session- and grant-checked, `private, immutable`); one without shows the "being made…" frame; a viewer without access gets 404 on the thumb URL.
- [ ] The gallery card opens the part host in 1 click; the gallery shows the being-made and scratch-expiry badges and the empty state.
- [ ] Error pages 404 (with close names the viewer can see), 403 (no title), 429 and 500 (with the request id) render in Stockroom style.
- [ ] Visual snapshots of the gallery and the part view at 360 px, light and dark.
- [ ] The 40 px phone bar hides on scroll down; hit targets are ≥ 44×44.
- [ ] A passkey registered on the workspace asserts from a part-host wrapper origin (virtual authenticator in Chromium), and an admin action started from the wrapper without a fresh assertion returns `step_up_required` and completes after the in-wrapper assertion.
- [ ] GATE: On the binary built from `main` in the e2e harness, a signed-in person opens `https://pixel-part.pf.test/` from the gallery in one click with one silent `/grant` hop and a clean address bar, a reload makes no hop, a signed-out `curl -si` of the root returns the private card, no cap, no part bytes and no `Set-Cookie` (identical for a bot UA), `chrome_cors_fuzz` passes against the live server, and a workspace passkey asserts from the wrapper.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with `crates/pf-serve/tests/{wrapper_headers,root_ua_independence,chrome_cors_fuzz,chrome_csrf,og_route}.rs` and `crates/pf-ui/tests/contrast.rs` in the nextest job, and `tests/e2e/wrapper_*.spec.ts`, `gallery_open.spec.ts`, `stepup_from_wrapper.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/visual/*` in the harness e2e job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts `event="wrapper.serve"`, `event="chrome.grant" outcome="ok"` and `event="stepup.verify" outcome="ok"`.
- [ ] GATE: Simulator lane (evidence, not a CI check): `wrapper_first_open` and `wrapper_regrant` pass in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (`tests/device/ios-sim.sh`), with posts, screenshots and the runtime version attached to the `verified` report.
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every earlier bead's gate tests, passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, curl excerpts, gallery and part-view screenshot paths in light, dark and 360 px) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gate reports recorded.

comments.author: admin
comments.text:
From spike pf-twz8 (docs/spikes/ui.md, spikes/spike-ui + spike-ui-app): by the §5 rule, Leptos 0.8.22 is a GO for the workspace. Friction was about 0.2 h. The hydrated part view (bar + share sheet) is 90.5 KB brotli-11 without wasm-opt, against a 300 KB rule. CodeMirror 6 interop passes both ways.
What this bead must do:
(1) WRAPPER: hand-written vanilla ES modules + one CSS file. No framework, bundler or hydration. Embed them with include_bytes!, precompress with brotli-11 in build.rs, and serve them as a content-addressed shared blob, with a budget of 15 KB brotli. Port spikes/spike-ui/static/share-island.js (ladder, live sentence, Can view/Can contribute, Copy, an in-sheet step-up hook calling navigator.credentials.get()) and the bar markup in templates/part.html. The spike's island + CSS is 1.6 KB brotli. Take the live sentence from the server (chrome API/op), so the wording isn't duplicated in JS and Rust.
(2) STOCKROOM SHELL: leptos =0.8.22 + leptos_axum =0.8.10, SSR + hydration. Call any_spawner::Executor::init_tokio() at startup, or every SSR request panics (leptos::task::Executor is private, so any_spawner is a direct dependency). Build the wasm with a wasm-release profile (opt-level=z, lto, codegen-units=1, panic=abort) plus wasm-bindgen-cli =0.2.129, which must equal the crate version. Build the wasm before the server, then embed pkg/. cargo-leptos isn't needed: see spikes/spike-ui/measure.sh. Add a CI budget check that fails above 250 KB brotli.
(3) Gate browser-only code with cfg(feature="hydrate"). Keep JsValue handles in StoredValue::new_local, because they're !Send.
(4) CodeMirror: glue via #[wasm_bindgen(module=...)], as in spikes/spike-ui-app/static/editor-glue.js. Vendor CodeMirror as a shared blob, not esm.sh.
(5) Cost to weigh: the wasm32 target adds about 0.5 GB of target/ per profile, plus a pinned CLI. If the admin wants no wasm toolchain, askama =0.16.1 + islands (/templates in the spike) is equivalent and works.

title: P4 Family, hub and phone: onboarding, embedding, service identities, slides and Mermaid, screenshots, phone editing, OTLP
description:
**Not broken down yet. Break it into chunky beads (a conversion step) when this phase starts, using what Slice 1 taught.**

## Goal
Bring the whole family in and meet them where they are: onboarding into the family space, family parts embedded in the family hub (with its own service identity), a family-only Hermes profile, slides and diagrams, and editing or commenting straight from a phone. Optional OTLP export lands here too.

## Scope
- [ ] Family onboarding: invite into the `family` space (admin, step-up, only for new people), a first-run tour. (The personal space created on first sign-in is Slice 1, in the identity bead pf-j8x0.)
- [ ] Embedding: `[embed] frame_ancestors` feeds the part CSP and the wrapper CSP; the embedder frames the part host root or `/c/` with a server-minted `src`; `pf-embed.js` handles `pf:regrant` with no navigation.
- [ ] Service identities: `principal_kind = service`, spaces fixed to `family`, created only by the admin with step-up; writes labelled as the service; `requested_by` recorded and shown as unverified. The family hub's connection first.
- [ ] The Hermes `hub-family` profile: a family-space-only agent profile for the household chat.
- [ ] The `slides` kind (block = slide) plus Mermaid and KaTeX for markdown and slides, client-side from the shared blob host.
- [ ] Phone editing: "Edit text" tap-to-edit for HTML and the other non-Markdown kinds (Markdown and `text` parts use the formatted view instead, decision 54) as an anchor edit (`old_str` = the original text), falling back to "Ask the agent"; long-press point-and-comment with an anchor `{version, block_id | selector, text_quote, rect}`, over the wrapper <-> part postMessage channel.
- [ ] Optional OTLP export adapter (traces, logs, metrics), off by default, never required.

## Plan refs
§2 Embedding, Framed expiry; §3b Service identities, "Agent consent is limited to spaces"; §3c Phone editing; §4 Example consumers (the family hub); §5f Embedding and Telemetry export rows; §5g; §6 P4; §6a P4; decisions 14, 22.

## Considerations
- Live space inheritance is why onboarding works: "everything in Family is the family's" stays true when someone joins later. Granting an existing account is inward; inviting a new person is the admin's.
- Embedding default is empty: only the part's own host and the workspace may frame it. A framed part never navigates itself to `/grant` (a subframe navigation from an opaque origin is cross-site for `SameSite=Lax`, so a sign-in page would render in the frame). Same-site embedders like the family hub get the Lax cookie on the regrant call; cross-site embedders can only use the server-minted `src` path. Document it.
- `versions.author_user` is `NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)`, and a service has no person: recommended is a reserved `local` user row per service (`in_audience = 0`, no passkey, can't sign in). Decide and record it.
- Enforcement for the hub-family profile is the connection's consented spaces, so even a prompt-injected profile can't leave `family`. Hermes is an example consumer; nothing in core depends on it.
- Mermaid and KaTeX run client-side so the build child stays within 10 s with no network, and the CSP doesn't change. The slide shell uses Jig styles.
- Screenshot thumbnails, posters and `og:video` previews moved to the rest-of-P1 epic (pf-5cyr, decision 53).
- Phone edits are anchor edits, not DOM serialisation: the source stays the diffable truth. The prelude only answers "what is at this point"; the server verifies the proposed `old_str`.
- OTLP exports only already-redacted data; add OTLP payloads to the no-content fuzz test's sinks when enabled.

## Order inside the phase
Family onboarding after native invites (P2b); family-hub embedding and service identities; slides and Mermaid after block ids; phone editing; OTLP (§6a).

## Verification gate
- Observed on a running build: a family member opens a hub-embedded part, fixes a typo by tapping it on the phone, long-presses to ask Hermes for a change, and Hermes, watching the event log, tells them in its own chat when the fix lands, on `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (local lane, evidence attached to `verified`); the real-phone pass is the non-blocking human-checks bead's.
- CI green on `main` with the embedding, service-identity, slides and phone-editing e2e specs in the harness job.
- Logs checked: the e2e run asserts the service-labelled write (`principal="conn:..."` with the service actor) and the refused non-family write (`outcome="forbidden"`).
- No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- Evidence on close: commit SHAs, CI run id, gate output, engine and simulator runtime versions, screenshot paths; `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A new family member invited to the space sees all family parts and none of the admin's private parts; their personal space exists on first sign-in and the first-run tour shows once
- [ ] Allowed origin frames root and `/c/`; disallowed origin is blocked by `frame-ancestors`.
- [ ] Expiring cap in an embedded frame recovers via `pf-embed.js` without a navigation.
- [ ] Default config (empty list) yields exactly `frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace>`.
- [ ] Service connection creatable only by the admin with step-up; spaces fixed to `family`.
- [ ] Service write to a non-family space → `forbidden {space}`.
- [ ] Writes labelled as the service; `requested_by` shown as unverified.
- [ ] The profile can create parts in `family` only; a write elsewhere is refused with `forbidden {space}`
- [ ] Golden slide deck renders; block ops address slides
- [ ] Mermaid and KaTeX render client-side in markdown and slides from the shared blob host, with no CSP change and no build-time network (golden pages on Chromium and WebKit)
- [ ] On a phone, a typo fixed by tapping it becomes one `part_edit`; a long-press comment carries `{version, selector|block, quote}`
- [ ] With a local collector configured, traces and logs arrive carrying request ids; with it unset, nothing is sent and nothing degrades
- [ ] A family member opens a hub-embedded part, fixes a typo by tapping it, long-presses to ask Hermes, and Hermes tells them in its own chat when the fix lands
- [ ] With OTLP enabled, the no-content fuzz test finds no canary in the exported payloads.
- [ ] A family-hub-shaped embedder page frames a family part on `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (recorded as `verified` evidence); an origin not in the list cannot frame it; the family hub's writes are labelled as the service. The real-phone embed check is the human-checks bead's.
- [ ] GATE: Observed on a running build: a family member opens a hub-embedded part, fixes a typo by tapping it, long-presses to ask Hermes for a change, and Hermes tells them in its own chat when the fix lands, on `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator (evidence attached to `verified`); the real-phone pass is the human-checks bead's and never blocks.
- [ ] GATE: CI green on `main` with the embedding, service-identity, slides and phone-editing e2e specs in the harness job.
- [ ] GATE: Logs checked: the e2e run asserts the service-labelled write and the refused non-family write (`outcome="forbidden"`).
- [ ] GATE: No regressions: the full e2e suite, including every Slice 1 gate test, still passes.
- [ ] GATE: Closed with evidence (commit SHAs, CI run id, gate output, engine and simulator runtime versions, screenshot paths) and the `ci_green` and `verified` gates reported in br.

title: Shipping: the OCI image and compose deliverable, the security suite, the drill and the device-emulation pass
description:
## Goal
Ship partifactory as three vendor-free things (an amd64 OCI image deployed by digest, `deploy/compose.yaml`, the env contract in `docs/env.md`) with a health-gated `partifactory deploy` that rolls itself back. Then prove it from outside: every section-7 line for what exists runs as a test against the compose deployment through its proxy, a drill restores the newest export on a second OCI host in under 15 minutes, and the device pass runs on emulated and simulated devices (Playwright Chromium with mobile emulation, WebKit with a mobile profile and Firefox, plus Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator). Real phones never block: the real iPhone, Android and Telegram checks live in the non-blocking human-checks bead.

## Scope
- [ ] Image: `cargo-chef` cached deps, static musl binary with every asset embedded, `FROM scratch` + CA certs (~20 MB), non-root `65532`, builder images pinned by digest, `partifactory healthcheck` (no shell in the image). Builds use one BuildKit cache bounded by `docker builder prune --keep-storage 10GB` after each build, labelled `pf.harness=1` images for local runs, and the drill removes its second Docker context's containers, volumes and images when it finishes.
- [ ] Release on tag (`scripts/release.sh`, CI-agnostic): pushed image, `release/digest.txt`, `part` CLI binaries, `SHA256SUMS`, forge release assets (so a laptop drill doesn't depend on the CI host), `cargo binstall` metadata.
- [ ] `deploy/compose.yaml`: image by digest, `/data` volume, `8080`/`8081` to the proxy only, `9090` local only, `_FILE` secrets, the `render` profile (the sidecar service definition from the part_check bead, carried into the published file), `proxy` profile (the one `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` + maintenance page from the observability bead), `json-file` 10m x 3 on every service; `deploy/.env.example` checked against `docs/env.md` (generated by the workspace bead) by `scripts/check_env_contract.sh`; `docs/host.md` (the host contract, §5b).
- [ ] `partifactory deploy`: record previous digest, pull, forward-only `migrate`, start beside the old one, wait for `/readyz`, switch, watch 2 minutes, roll back on failure; Docker or Podman, `--host ssh://`.
- [ ] The e2e harness switches from `tests/e2e/harness/compose.yaml` to the shipped `deploy/compose.yaml` (plus a harness overlay for Dex, Caddy and the fake CDN), so every gate from here on runs on the deliverable. The overlay swaps in a `dev`-feature image built from the same commit for the earlier specs that drive `partifactory dev …`, the dev token, the test-clock endpoint, the fixture directory or `[mirror] test_resolve`; the §7 suite, `tests/deploy/*`, the drill and the device pass run on the release image, which has none of those (asserted by `image_checks.sh`).
- [ ] Section-7 suite `tests/security/` + `checklist.yaml` (stable id per line mapped to a test, a `covered_by` test in an earlier bead, a manual record, or `pending` with its owning bead; the real-device line maps to the human-checks bead as `manual`); raw-request client, Playwright on three engines plus the mobile projects, a canary sibling service, open-redirect and CORS fuzzers, the no-secrets-in-logs/metrics canary across every surface; runs from outside against the compose deployment through Caddy in the e2e harness. The same suite is runnable against any deployment (`--base-url`), which the human-checks bead uses for the example deployment.
- [ ] Drill `scripts/drill.sh`: export + image and CLI from the release assets + the offline site config into a throwaway stack on a second OCI host (in CI a second Docker context or daemon; from a laptop for the human-checks run), e2e suite, `backup/drills/<ts>.json` (`{ok, rto_s, failures}`), `pf_last_drill_ok` / `pf_last_drill_age_s`, the Health drill row; `docs/ops/moving.md`, `docs/ops/backup.md`. The drill is also the migration test (forward migrations on a production-shaped export).
- [ ] Refresh reuse after import: with the token service deployed, reuse within 24 h of `kv.import_at` does not revoke the family; after 24 h it does.
- [ ] Device-emulation pass `tests/device/`: `device-pass.spec.ts` on `chromium-mobile`, `webkit-mobile` and `firefox-desktop` for standalone open, part-host open (first open and reload), the `/l/` guest open and sign-in (Dex on every project; passkey step-up with the virtual authenticator on Chromium, where Playwright offers one); `ios-sim.sh device-pass` runs the same self-reporting pages in Mobile Safari in the iOS Simulator and records posts and screenshots; `tests/manual/real-device-pass.md` stays as the script the human-checks bead follows, with `scripts/check_manual_records.sh` validating its result files when they exist; `docs/ops/telegram.md` documents the two decided Telegram fixes.

## Plan refs
§5b Builds and deploys (deliverable, env contract, host contract, deploy); §3 Topology (ingress contract); §5c drills and moving hosts; §5h (container log limits); §7 (all but Backends, Updates and advisories and adapter lines); §2 Telegram decision; §3a UX (device matrix); Slice 1 "Shipping it" and definition of done items 2 (device matrix, beside the pixel bead), 4 and 5; decisions 22, 36, 42, 52.

## Considerations
- Never `:latest`. Migrations stay forward-compatible with the previous binary (rollback runs the old binary on the migrated DB). `/readyz` ignores the IdP. Each deploy bumps the boot epoch: open tabs re-grant once, silently.
- Deferred (decision 42, rest of P1): arm64, SBOM, `cosign`, nginx/Traefik, example CI workflows. The runner joins compose with P2a.
- From outside because a proxy forwarding `:9090`, trusting a spoofed client-IP header or caching private blobs only shows through the real ingress. Assert the canonical CSP byte for byte; fuzz `/grant` (`//evil`, `\\evil`, `%2f%2f`, `@evil`, CRLF) and chrome-API origins (`null`, `blobs-part`, renamed names, lookalikes).
- Lines already proven inside an earlier bead (e.g. "no agent token, scope or op can make a public link" in the MCP/conformance bead, the guest wall in the public-links bead) are mapped `covered_by` and re-run here from outside; this bead doesn't re-implement them.
- Adapter lines and portability-lane runs come after Slice 1; the two old lines that need the portability lane are verified in the rest-of-P1 epic. Backend lines are P2a; advisory lines the advisories epic. The run against the example deployment (its tunnel, its IdP) is the admin's and lives in the human-checks bead; nothing here waits on it.
- §5c says drills run from a laptop because the CI system may be on the host that died. That reason holds for the real drill, which is the human-checks bead's laptop run against a physically separate host. The gate here is the same script in CI against a second Docker context, so "another OCI host" is real at the daemon level and the RTO is measured on every change.
- Telegram (decision 36) stays decided: the fixes on a failure are set Telegram to open links in the normal browser and make Hermes hint "open in browser". The test itself is a real-phone check and belongs to the human-checks bead; this bead approximates the webview with the WebKit lanes and never builds the rejected person-bound-link fallback. No personal data in result files.
- Releases need two forge secrets the admin provides: a container-registry push credential and a token allowed to create releases. They are admin prerequisites (the human-checks bead lists them).
